4.1.1: Eternal salutation to that Radiance whose half-body is graced by the Daughter of the Mountain: who, though free from all change, takes on the form of the universe through his own māyā alone; whose two splendours of a compassionate side-glance are called heaven and liberation; and whom yogins always behold in the heart as the non-dual bliss of inner awareness. ॥1॥
4.1.2: May that indescribable Radiance bring about auspiciousness: whose glance is gentle with compassion, whose lotus-face is lovely with a smile, which shines with the digit of the moon, which has quelled the terrible threefold affliction, whose form is being-and-consciousness glowing with supreme bliss, and which is encircled by the arms of the Daughter of the Mountain. ॥2॥
4.1.3: The sages said: You have rightly told, O Sūta, out of a wish for the welfare of the worlds, the greatness of Śiva's incarnations, together with many narratives. ॥3॥
4.1.4: And again, dear one, please narrate with great affection the supreme greatness of Śiva connected with the liṅga. You are blessed, O best of Śaivas. ॥4॥
4.1.5: Listening from your lotus-mouth, O lord, we are not satiated. Let that delightful nectar of Śiva's glory be told once more. ॥5॥
4.1.6: The auspicious liṅgas that exist on earth at each and every tīrtha, or the famous ones that stand in other places, ॥6॥
4.1.7: all those divine liṅgas of the Supreme Lord, O disciple of Vyāsa, describe to us for the welfare of the worlds. ॥7॥
4.1.8: Sūta said: Well asked, O best of sages, for the welfare of the worlds. Out of affection for you, O twice-born ones, I shall tell of them briefly. ॥8॥
4.1.9: O sage, there is no counting all the Śiva-liṅgas. The whole earth is full of liṅgas; the whole world consists of liṅgas. ॥9॥
4.1.10: The tīrthas are endowed with liṅgas; everything is established in the liṅga. There is no count of them; I shall tell of a few of them. ॥10॥
4.1.11: Whatever visible thing is seen, whatever is described or remembered, all that is indeed the form of Śiva; there is nothing else whatsoever. ॥11॥
4.1.12: Nevertheless, listen with love: I shall tell, as I have heard, O best of sages, of those liṅgas that are on the earth. ॥12॥
4.1.13: They exist in Pātāla, in heaven, and likewise on earth. Everywhere Śambhu is worshipped by gods, asuras and humans. ॥13॥
4.1.14: The three worlds, with their gods, asuras and humans, are pervaded by Śambhu in the form of the liṅga, for the grace of the worlds, O most excellent ones. ॥14॥
4.1.15: For the grace of the worlds, Maheśvara assumes various liṅgas here, at tīrthas and likewise in other places. ॥15॥
4.1.16: Wherever and whenever Śambhu was remembered with devotion by his devotees, there he descended, accomplished the task, and then remained. ॥16॥
4.1.17: For the benefit of the worlds he also established his own liṅga. By worshipping that liṅga one attains perfection. ॥17॥
4.1.18: There is no count of the liṅgas on earth; nevertheless, O twice-born ones, the principal ones are being told by me. ॥18॥
4.1.19: Among the principal ones, I shall declare here those that are foremost, hearing which a person is freed from all sins in an instant. ॥19॥
4.1.20: The jyotirliṅgas here, which are the most foremost of all, O excellent one, I shall tell today; hearing of them one dispels sin. ॥20॥
4.1.21: Somanātha in Saurāṣṭra, Mallikārjuna on Śrīśaila, Mahākāla in Ujjayinī, Parameśvara at Oṅkāra, ॥21॥
4.1.22: Kedāra on the slope of the Himālaya, Bhīmaśaṅkara in Ḍākinī, Viśveśa in Vārāṇasī, Tryambaka on the bank of the Gautamī, ॥22॥
4.1.23: Vaidyanātha in Citābhūmi, Nāgeśa in the Dārukā forest, Rāmeśa at Setubandha, and Ghuśmeśa at Śivālaya. ॥23॥
4.1.24: Whoever, rising at dawn, recites these twelve names is freed from all sins and obtains the fruit of all accomplishments. ॥24॥
4.1.25: Whatever desire the best of men recite them with in view, that very desire they will obtain, here and in the hereafter, O lords of sages. ॥25॥
4.1.26: Those of pure intent who recite them without desire will never again dwell in a mother's womb. ॥26॥
4.1.27: Through the worship of these alone, the sorrows of all the varṇas are destroyed; in this world and the next, liberation certainly comes about. ॥27॥
4.1.28: Their food-offering should be accepted and eaten with care; all the sins of the one who does so are reduced to ashes in an instant. ॥28॥
4.1.29: The fruit of the jyotirliṅgas, O twice-born ones, cannot be fully described in detail even by Brahmā and the others, nor likewise by anyone else. ॥29॥
4.1.30: For one by whom even one of them has been worshipped without interruption for six months, the suffering arising from birth in a mother's womb will not occur. ॥30॥
4.1.31: If one born in a low birth sees a jyotirliṅga, his next birth will be in a pure and noble family. ॥31॥
4.1.32: Having obtained birth in a noble family, wealthy and a master of the Vedas, he then performs auspicious deeds and attains imperishable liberation. ॥32॥
4.1.33: Whether a mleccha, an outcaste, or a eunuch, O lords of sages, he becomes twice-born and is liberated; therefore one should undertake the sight of it. ॥33॥
4.1.34: I have told a little of the fruit of the jyotirliṅgas. Now hear of the upaliṅgas of the jyotirliṅgas, O best of sages. ॥34॥
4.1.35: The liṅga arising from Someśvara is declared to be Antakeśa; at the confluence of the Mahī with the sea, that liṅga is the upaliṅga. ॥35॥
4.1.36: The upaliṅga arising from Mallikārjuna is declared to be the one famed as Rudreśvara, at Bhṛgukakṣa, bestowing happiness. ॥36॥
4.1.37: The liṅga born of Mahākāla is renowned as Dugdheśa; it is famous on the Narmadā and is held to remove all sins. ॥37॥
4.1.38: The liṅga born of Oṃkāra is known as Kardameśa; famous at Bindusaras, it grants the fruit of all desires. ॥38॥
4.1.39: Born of Kedāreśvara is Bhūteśa on the bank of the Yamunā, declared to remove great sins for those who see and likewise worship it. ॥39॥
4.1.40: Arising from Bhīmaśaṅkara is the one known as Bhīmeśvara; famous on the Sahya mountain, it greatly increases strength. ॥40॥
4.1.41: That upaliṅga which arose from Viśveśvara is renowned as Śaraṇyeśvara; and that which is declared as arising from Tryambaka is known as Siddheśvara. ॥41॥
4.1.42: That which arose from Vaidyanātha is remembered as Vaijanātha; that which sprang from Nāgeśvara is called Bhūteśvara. ॥42॥
4.1.43: It stands on the bank of the Mallikā-Sarasvatī and removes sin by being seen. And that which arose from Rāmeśvara is remembered as Gupteśvara. ॥43॥
4.1.44: And that which arose from Ghuśmeśa is remembered as Vyāghreśvara. Thus the upaliṅgas of the jyotirliṅgas have been declared here by me, O brāhmaṇas. ॥44॥
4.1.45: They remove sins by being seen and grant all desires. These are the most eminent and have indeed attained pre-eminence; now let other principal ones also be heard, O best of sages. ॥45॥
4.1.iti: Thus ends the first adhyāya, named The greatness of the jyotirliṅgas and their upaliṅgas, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥1॥
4.2.1: Sūta said: On the bank of the Gaṅgā, the renowned Kāśī indeed grants liberation. It should be known as made up of liṅgas, and it is remembered as Śiva's dwelling-place. ॥1॥
4.2.2: There itself the chief liṅga is declared to be Avimuktaka; Kṛttivāseśvara is Śiva directly, and equal to it is Vṛddhakālaka. ॥2॥
4.2.3: And Tilabhāṇḍeśvara, and Daśāśvamedha too; at the confluence of the Gaṅgā with the ocean, the liṅga is remembered as Saṅgameśa. ॥3॥
4.2.4: The one declared as Bhūteśvara always grants every aim to devotees. The one famed as Nārīśvara is near the Kauśikī. ॥4॥
4.2.5: On the bank of the Gaṇḍakī stands Baṭukeśvara. Famed as Pūreśvara, a liṅga on the bank of the Phalgu grants happiness. ॥5॥
4.2.6: And Siddhanātheśvara, who by being seen grants success to men; and likewise the one famed as Dūreśvara in the northern town. ॥6॥
4.2.7: And one named Śṛṅgeśvara, and likewise Vaidyanātha; and the one famed as Japyeśvara, which is at the battle-site of Dadhīci. ॥7॥
4.2.8: Gopeśvara is well known, another is remembered as Raṅgeśvara; also Vāmeśvara, Nāgeśa, Kāmeśa and Vimaleśvara. ॥8॥
4.2.9: Vyāseśvara is famed, and Sukeśa likewise; Bhāṇḍeśvara is famed, and Huṅkāreśa likewise. ॥9॥
4.2.10: Surocana is famed, and Bhūteśvara itself; likewise Saṅgameśa is declared, the destroyer of great sins. ॥10॥
4.2.11: Then on the bank of the Taptakā is Kumāreśvara; Siddheśvara is famed, and Seneśa is likewise remembered. ॥11॥
4.2.12: One is declared as Rāmeśvara, and Kumbheśa is held to be supreme; also Nandīśvara and Puñjeśa, and likewise Pūrṇaka on the Pūrṇā. ॥12॥
4.2.13: And at Prayāga is Brahmeśvara, installed long ago by Brahmā at the Daśāśvamedha tīrtha, granting the fruit of the four aims of life. ॥13॥
4.2.14: Likewise there is Someśvara, who wards off all calamities, and Bhāradvājeśvara, who increases brahmic splendour. ॥14॥
4.2.15: Śūlaṭaṅkeśvara is declared to be directly the granter of desires, and right there Mādhaveśa, who effects the protection of devotees. ॥15॥
4.2.16: The one called Nāgeśa is famous in the city of Sāketa, O brāhmaṇas; he grants happiness especially to those born in the Solar dynasty. ॥16॥
4.2.17: In the city of Puruṣottama is Bhuvaneśa, granting great success, and Lokeśa, a great liṅga bestowing all bliss. ॥17॥
4.2.18: Kāmeśvara, the liṅga of Śambhu; Gaṅgeśa, who brings supreme purity; and Śukreśvara, established by Śukra out of desire for the welfare of the worlds. ॥18॥
4.2.19: Likewise Vaṭeśvara is famed, granting the fruit of all desires; on the bank of the Sindhu is Kapāleśa, and Vaktreśa, destroyer of all sins. ॥19॥
4.2.20: Dhautapāpeśvara is directly the Supreme Lord present by a portion; others are declared as Bhīmeśvara and remembered as Sūryeśvara. ॥20॥
4.2.21: Nandīśvara should be known as the giver of knowledge, worshipped by the world; Nākeśvara is greatly meritorious, and likewise Rāmeśvara is remembered. ॥21॥
4.2.22: One named Vimaleśvara, and Kaṇṭakeśvara; and likewise, at the confluence with the eastern ocean, Dhartukeśa. ॥22॥
4.2.23: Candreśvara should be known as granting the fruit of moon-like radiance; and the granter of all desires is remembered as Siddheśvara. ॥23॥
4.2.24: Bilveśvara is famed, and likewise Andhakeśa, where the demon Andhaka was slain long ago by Śaṅkara. ॥24॥
4.2.25: Śambhu, having taken on this form by a portion, remained there again; famed as Śaraṇeśvara, he always grants happiness to the worlds. ॥25॥
4.2.26: Kardameśa is declared supreme, and Koṭīśa is on Mount Arbuda; Acaleśa is famed, always granting happiness to the worlds. ॥26॥
4.2.27: Nāgeśvara abides perpetually on the bank of the Kauśikī; and the one called Anantēśvara is a vessel of welfare and auspiciousness. ॥27॥
4.2.28: Yogeśvara is famed, and likewise Vaidyanātheśvara; Koṭīśvara should be known, and one is remembered as Sapteśvara. ॥28॥
4.2.29: Bhadreśvara is famed — Hara himself, named Bhadra; likewise Caṇḍīśvara is declared, and Saṅgameśvara too. ॥29॥
4.2.30: The Śiva-liṅgas that arose in the eastern direction, and others too that are ordinary — these have been told to you here. ॥30॥
4.2.31: Likewise, the Śiva-liṅgas that arose in the southern direction, O best of sages — those I shall now tell you. ॥31॥
4.2.iti: Thus ends the second adhyāya, named The greatness of the Śiva-liṅga, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥2॥
4.3.1: Sūta said: In Brahmapurī at Citrakūṭa there is the liṅga called Mattagajendraka, installed long ago by Brahmā, which grants the fulfilment of all desires. ॥1॥
4.3.2: To its east is the liṅga Koṭīśa, bestower of all boons; to the west of the Godāvarī is the liṅga named Paśupati. ॥2॥
4.3.3: In the southern direction there is one called Atrīśvara, the god himself, for the benefit of the worlds and for the happiness of Anasūyā— ॥3॥
4.3.4: the god manifested himself and, during a drought, kept beings alive. He is indeed Śaṅkara himself, directly, present by a portion of himself. ॥4॥
4.3.5: The sages said: O Sūta, O Sūta, most fortunate one, how did Hara, supreme and divine, arise as Atrīśvara? Tell us the truth, O you of good vows. ॥5॥
4.3.6: Sūta said: Well asked, O best of sages. I shall tell the auspicious story, by constantly hearing which one is surely freed from sins. ॥6॥
4.3.7: In the southern direction, near Citrakūṭa, there is a great forest named Kāmada, beneficial for the austerities of the virtuous. ॥7॥
4.3.8: There Brahmā's son, the sage named Atri himself, accompanied by Anasūyā, performed extremely severe austerity. ॥8॥
4.3.9: Once, long ago, in that very place, O sage, by fate there occurred a terrible drought lasting a hundred years, bringing misery to living beings. ॥9॥
4.3.10: Then all the trees dried up, and the leaves and fruits too; nowhere was water seen for daily needs, O lords of sages. ॥10॥
4.3.11: No moisture could be found; harsh winds blew in the ten directions; a great and very painful cry of woe arose on earth. ॥11॥
4.3.12: Seeing the destruction of beings, Atri's beloved wife, the virtuous one, said to Atri: I cannot bear this suffering. ॥12॥
4.3.13: Then the best of sages, seated himself on his seat, having performed breath-control three times, became absorbed in samādhi. ॥13॥
4.3.14: He, Atri, the wise and foremost sage, meditated by his self upon the supreme light abiding in the self—Śaṅkara, the changeless. ॥14॥
4.3.15: While the master was absorbed in meditation, his disciples went far away; lacking food, they then abandoned their own guru, the sage. ॥15॥
4.3.16: Then that devoted wife Anasūyā was left alone, and she constantly served that best of sages with joy. ॥16॥
4.3.17: Having made a beautiful earthen liṅga with mantra according to the rules, she worshipped Śaṅkara, also with mental offerings. ॥17॥
4.3.18: She praised Śaṅkara with devotion, having served him again and again; with palms joined, having circumambulated her lord Śiva, ॥18॥
4.3.19: then Anasūyā, of good conduct, the sage's beloved, made the return circuit with prostrations like a staff. ॥19॥
4.3.20: All the Daityas and Dānavas, seeing the beautiful woman then, became agitated there and stayed far off because of her radiance. ॥20॥
4.3.21: Just as creatures keep far away on seeing fire, so, seeing her then, they did not come near here. ॥21॥
4.3.22: O foremost of brāhmaṇas, Anasūyā's service to Śiva, refined by mind, speech and body, surpassed even Atri's austerity. ॥22॥
4.3.23: For as long as the best of sages was intent on breath-control, for that long the lady performed her service. ॥23॥
4.3.24: That couple then remained there, each intent on his or her own task, O tiger among sages; no one else stayed there. ॥24॥
4.3.25: As time passed thus, Atri, the best of seers, absorbed in supreme meditation, was aware of nothing at all. ॥25॥
4.3.26: Anasūyā too, that virtuous woman, worshipped her husband and likewise Śiva; that chaste one knew nothing else higher. ॥26॥
4.3.27: Through his austerity and her worship, all the gods and seers, and likewise the rivers headed by the Gaṅgā, ॥27॥
4.3.28: all came together with great affection to see the two; and seeing that austerity and service, they were filled with supreme wonder. ॥28॥
4.3.29: Seeing that marvel of the two, they declared worship to be superior: Of the two, which is more excellent—austerity or worship? ॥29॥
4.3.30: Having observed all of it in both—what is called Atri's austerity and Anasūyā's devoted service—they declared worship to be superior. ॥30॥
4.3.31: Difficult austerity was performed by earlier seers too, but where has anyone ever done such as this? Thus they said. ॥31॥
4.3.32: Blessed is this sage, and blessed likewise is this Anasūyā, since by these two such excellent austerity is performed again with supreme love. ॥32॥
4.3.33: Who in the three worlds now performs such auspicious, difficult and excellent austerity as this? None is known. ॥33॥
4.3.34: Having praised the two, they all then went back as they had come—except Gaṅgā and Giriśa Śiva. ॥34॥
4.3.35: Gaṅgā, the virtuous one, pleased by her devotion to me and captivated by her dharma, said: Having done her a favour, I shall go. ॥35॥
4.3.36: Śiva too, bound by the meditation of the sage Atri, O lords of sages, remained there with his full portion and did not go to Kailāsa. ॥36॥
4.3.37: Thus fifty-four years had passed here, O best of seers, and still no rain fell then. ॥37॥
4.3.38: As long as Atri thus remained in meditation through austerity, Anasūyā then made the resolve: I will not take anything. ॥38॥
4.3.39: While this was being done, with the sage remaining in austerity, hear now what happened in the course of Anasūyā's excellent worship. ॥39॥
4.3.iti: Thus ends the third adhyāya, named The austerity of Anasūyā and Atri, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥3॥
4.4.1: Sūta said: Once that best of sages, Atri, foremost among the knowers of Brahman, on waking said to his beloved: Give me water. ॥1॥
4.4.2: She too, the virtuous one, taking the water-pot without fail, went into the forest there thinking: From where can water be brought by me? ॥2॥
4.4.3: What shall I do? Where shall I go? From where indeed can water be brought? Overcome with bewilderment thus, she saw that Gaṅgā. ॥3॥
4.4.4: As she was following her, Gaṅgā—the goddess, best of rivers, bearing a beautiful form—then spoke to her: ॥4॥
4.4.5: Gaṅgā said: I am pleased with you, O lady. Tell me now, where are you going? You are blessed, O fortunate one; truly I will carry out your command. ॥5॥
4.4.6: Sūta said: Hearing those words then, the ascetic wife of the sage, herself much astonished, replied lovingly, O Brahmins: ॥6॥
4.4.7: Anasūyā said: Who are you, O lotus-petal-eyed one, and from where have you come? Be kind and tell me the truth; so said the virtuous, well-spoken, chaste lady. ॥7॥
4.4.8: Sūta said: When the sage's wife had spoken thus there, O lords of sages, Gaṅgā, best of rivers, of divine form, then spoke these words: ॥8॥
4.4.9: Gaṅgā said: Having seen your service to your husband and to Śiva, the Supreme Self, and having seen your righteousness, O virtuous one, I have stayed near you. ॥9॥
4.4.10: I am Gaṅgā, come here because of your devotion, O sweetly smiling one. I have become subject to you; choose whatever you desire. ॥10॥
4.4.11: Sūta said: When Gaṅgā had said this, the virtuous lady bowed, stood before her and said: If you are pleased with me now, give me water. ॥11॥
4.4.12: Hearing these words, she Gaṅgā said: Make a pit. Anasūyā quickly came, made it, and stood there in that very moment. ॥12॥
4.4.13: She Gaṅgā entered there and then took the form of water. Filled with the greatest wonder, she Anasūyā took up the water. ॥13॥
4.4.14: Anasūyā, the sage's wife, then spoke these words to the divine-formed best of rivers, for the happiness of the worlds: ॥14॥
4.4.15: Anasūyā said: If you are well pleased with me and have compassion for me, you should stay here until my husband comes. ॥15॥
4.4.16: Sūta said: Hearing these words of Anasūyā, which bring joy to the good, Gaṅgā said: I am greatly pleased; I will stay if you give me the merit of your service to Atri, O sinless one. ॥16॥
4.4.17: When she Gaṅgā had said this there, she Anasūyā did accordingly; giving that divine water to her husband, she stood before him. ॥17॥
4.4.18: The sage, too, with great delight, having duly sipped water for purification according to rule, drank that divine water, and having drunk it attained bliss. ॥18॥
4.4.19: Ah! This is not the water that is drunk every day. Reflecting thus, he quickly looked all around. ॥19॥
4.4.20: Seeing the trees withered and the quarters very parched, the best of sages said to her: Has rain not fallen again? ॥20॥
4.4.21: Hearing what he said, she answered, no, no. Then he again said to his beloved: From where was the water brought by you? ॥21॥
4.4.22: When he said this, Anasūyā fell into great bewilderment and became anxious in her mind, O lords of sages. ॥22॥
4.4.23: If I tell it, there will be self-exaltation on my part; if I do not tell it, there will be a breach of my vow. ॥23॥
4.4.24: It should be told by me in such a way that neither fault arises. While she was reflecting thus, she was asked again and again. ॥24॥
4.4.25: Then the devoted wife, having gained understanding through the grace of Śambhu, said: Listen, my lord; I shall tell you what happened. ॥25॥
4.4.26: Anasūyā said: By the might of Śaṅkara and by your own good deeds, Gaṅgā has come right here; this water is hers. ॥26॥
4.4.27: Sūta said: Hearing these words then, the sage, his mind filled with wonder, spoke lovingly to his beloved, remembering Śaṅkara in his mind: ॥27॥
4.4.28: Atri said: O beloved, beautiful one, do you speak the truth or false words? Even if you speak truly, I do not believe it, for this is rare indeed. ॥28॥
4.4.29: O auspicious one, how has that come about today which is always impossible even for yogins and gods? My astonishment is supreme. ॥29॥
4.4.30: If it is seen to be so, then I will believe it, not otherwise. Hearing these words, his beloved replied to her husband: ॥30॥
4.4.31: Anasūyā said: Come with me, O lord, great sage, if you wish to see Gaṅgā, the best of rivers. ॥31॥
4.4.32: Sūta said: Having said this, the devoted wife took her husband along and, remembering Śiva, went quickly to where Gaṅgā, the best of rivers, was. ॥32॥
4.4.33: There the devoted wife showed her husband that Gaṅgā, abiding in the pit, herself of divine form. ॥33॥
4.4.34: Having gone there and seen the beautiful pit filled with water up to the brim, the best of sages said: Blessed is she! ॥34॥
4.4.35: What is my penance compared to this, and what then of others' penance? Having said this, the tiger among sages then praised her with devotion. ॥35॥
4.4.36: Then the sage bathed well there in the blessed water, sipped it for purification, and again and again offered praise there. ॥36॥
4.4.37: Anasūyā too then bathed in that beautiful water. The sage performed his daily rites, and so did Anasūyā, firm in her vows. ॥37॥
4.4.38: Then Gaṅgā said to her: I am going to my own place. When this was said, the virtuous lady again spoke to the best of rivers: ॥38॥
4.4.39: Anasūyā said: O sovereign goddess, if you are pleased and if you have compassion for me, you should remain steadfastly in this penance-grove, O goddess. ॥39॥
4.4.40: It is the nature of the great that, having accepted someone, they do not abandon them. Having said this, she joined her palms and praised her again and again. ॥40॥
4.4.41: The sage too spoke likewise: You must stay here, O best of rivers. Be favourable, O goddess, and make us feel protected. ॥41॥
4.4.42: Hearing those pleasing words of his, Gaṅgā, the best of rivers, with a gladdened mind, spoke these words to Anasūyā. ॥42॥
4.4.43: Gaṅgā said: If you give me the fruit arising from one year's worship of Śaṅkara and of service to your husband, then I shall stay, for the sake of helping the gods. ॥43॥
4.4.44: I am not so pleased by gifts, nor by baths at sacred places, nor by sacrifices or yogic practices, as by a wife's devotion to her husband. ॥44॥
4.4.45: The delight of mind that arises from seeing a chaste, devoted wife does not come from any other means. I have spoken the truth, O virtuous lady. ॥45॥
4.4.46: By seeing a woman devoted to her husband, my sins are destroyed. A devoted wife becomes especially pure, equal to Gaurī. ॥46॥
4.4.47: Therefore, if you give that merit for the welfare of the world, then I shall become steadfast here, if you desire its well-being. ॥47॥
4.4.48: Sūta said: Hearing these words, that devoted wife Anasūyā gave to Gaṅgā all the merit born of that year. ॥48॥
4.4.49: For it is the nature of the great to bring about the welfare of others; gold, sandalwood and sugarcane juice are examples of this. ॥49॥
4.4.50: Seeing this great act of wifely devotion by Anasūyā, Mahādeva was pleased and swiftly manifested from the earthen liṅga. ॥50॥
4.4.51: Śambhu said: Seeing this deed of yours, O virtuous one, I am pleased, O devoted wife. Ask a boon of me, dear one, for you are most dear to me. ॥51॥
4.4.52: Then that couple, beholding Śambhu Hara of beautiful form, endowed with five faces and other features, became greatly astonished. ॥52॥
4.4.53: Bowing, praising, joining their palms, filled with great devotion, the two worshipped Śaṅkara, the benefactor of the worlds, and spoke. ॥53॥
4.4.54: The couple said: If you are pleased, O Lord of the gods, and the Mother of the universe is pleased, stay in this penance-grove and be the giver of happiness to the worlds. ॥54॥
4.4.55: Then Gaṅgā was pleased, and Śiva too was pleased; and both of them remained there where the best of sages was. ॥55॥
4.4.56: The Lord, remover of others' sorrow, became known by the name Atrīśvara; and Gaṅgā too then remained there in a pit, by her divine power (māyā). ॥56॥
4.4.57: From that day onward there has always been inexhaustible water there; in that pit, a mere hand's span in size, Gaṅgā became the Mandākinī. ॥57॥
4.4.58: To that very place the divine sages came together with their wives — all those twice-born who had earlier departed, coming back from one holy place after another. ॥58॥
4.4.59: Barley and rice grew again; and those people, devoted to sacrifices and rites, joined with those excellent sages, performed oblations (homa). ॥59॥
4.4.60: Satisfied by those rites, the clouds then sent rain, and supreme joy arose in the world, O lords of sages. ॥60॥
4.4.61: Thus has the glory of Atrīśvara been told to you, bringing happiness, granting enjoyment and liberation, fulfilling all desires and increasing devotion. ॥61॥
4.4.iti: Thus ends the fourth adhyāya, named The greatness of Atrīśvara, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥4॥
4.5.1: Sūta said: On the divine mountain Kālañjara dwells Nīlakaṇṭha, the Great Lord, ever in the form of a liṅga and ever granting bliss to his devotees. ॥1॥
4.5.2: His greatness is divine, proclaimed in Śruti and Smṛti. There is a tīrtha there by that name; bathing in it destroys sins. ॥2॥
4.5.3: O you of good vows, the Śiva-liṅgas that exist on the bank of the Revā, bestowing all happiness here—their number is not known. ॥3॥
4.5.4: And she the Revā is indeed of the very form of Rudra, removing sin by mere sight; whatever stones lie in her are of Śiva's form. ॥4॥
4.5.5: Even so, O lords of sages, I shall tell of other principal Śiva-liṅgas, which grant both enjoyment and liberation. ॥5॥
4.5.6: There is one well named Ārteśvara, remover of sin; one renowned as Parameśvara; and one remembered as Siṃheśvara. ॥6॥
4.5.7: Likewise here are Śarmeśa and Kumāreśvara, the renowned Puṇḍarīkeśvara, and Maṇḍapeśvara. ॥7॥
4.5.8: There was one named Tīkṣṇeśa, removing sin by sight; and on the bank of the Narmadā one named Dhundhureśvara, destroyer of sin. ॥8॥
4.5.9: One is renowned as Śūleśvara, likewise Kumbheśvara is remembered; one named Kubereśvara, and likewise Someśvara is remembered. ॥9॥
4.5.10: Nīlakaṇṭha, Maṅgaleśa, the great Maṅgalāyatana, and the god Mahākapīśvara, who was installed by Hanumān. ॥10॥
4.5.11: Then there is the god Nandika, who wards off the sin of crores of killings, and is proclaimed the giver of all desires and aims, and the giver of liberation. ॥11॥
4.5.12: Whoever worships Nandīkeśa daily with supreme joy—all success will be his; there is no doubt. ॥12॥
4.5.13: O best of sages, whoever bathes in the Revā there at that bank—his desires are fulfilled and all his sin perishes. ॥13॥
4.5.14: The sages said: How did such greatness of his arise there, O great-minded one? By the grace of Nandikeśa, may it now be told by you. ॥14॥
4.5.15: Sūta said: You have asked well; I shall tell it as I heard it. O Śaunaka and the other sages, all of you listen attentively. ॥15॥
4.5.16: Formerly the best of sages was asked in this way by Yudhiṣṭhira; as he spoke, so I tell it, in keeping with my affection for you. ॥16॥
4.5.17: On the western bank of the Revā there shines a city named Karṇikī, rich in great beauty and crowded with people of the four varṇas. ॥17॥
4.5.18: There a certain excellent brahmin, born in the lineage of Utathya, went to Kāśī after entrusting his wife to his two sons. ॥18॥
4.5.19: That brahmin died right there, and the two sons then heard of it; the two young sons performed his funeral rites. ॥19॥
4.5.20: And the wife, wishing her sons' welfare, raised the two sons; and, keeping aside a little, she divided the wealth. ॥20॥
4.5.21: A little wealth was kept as her own for the sake of the rites at her death. Then, after some time had passed, that brahmin's wife— ॥21॥
4.5.22: —once, when on the point of death, she performed various meritorious acts; yet, O brahmins, by the working of fate that brahmin's wife did not die. ॥22॥
4.5.23: When their mother, by fate, did not give up her life-breaths, the two sons, seeing that suffering of their mother, then spoke. ॥23॥
4.5.24: The two sons said: What is lacking, mother, that there is such great suffering? Express it quickly and gladly; then we two shall do it. ॥24॥
4.5.25: Sūta said: Hearing that, she said there: Much is lacking for me; if that indeed is done, death would come easily. ॥25॥
4.5.26: Her eldest son said: Let it be told by you; I shall do it. Then it was told by her. ॥26॥
4.5.27: The brahmin's wife said: Listen lovingly to my words, son. Formerly I had a heartfelt wish to go to Kāśī; it did not come about, and now I am dying. ॥27॥
4.5.28: My bones, son, must be cast by you diligently into the water of the Gaṅgā; then good will come to you today, no doubt. ॥28॥
4.5.29: Sūta said: When the mother had spoken thus, that eldest son, devoted to his mother, spoke to his mother of good vows, who was facing death. ॥29॥
4.5.30: The son said: Mother, you may give up your life-breaths in peace, no doubt. Having first done your task, afterwards I shall do my own. ॥30॥
4.5.31: Having thus placed water in her hand as a pledge, no sooner had the son gone into the house than she died there, intent on remembering Hara. ॥31॥
4.5.32: Having arranged all the rites due to her, and having performed the monthly ceremony, he set out to go. ॥32॥
4.5.33: The elder of the two, known by the name Suvāda, taking her bones, went forth with the wish to reach the tīrtha. ॥33॥
4.5.34: Taking along a certain servant and accompanied by him, he then consoled his wife and sons, wishing to do what was dear to his mother. ॥34॥
4.5.35: Having performed the śrāddha, gifts and the like, the feeding of brahmins, and the excellent rite, and having made auspicious invocations, the brahmin departed from his house. ॥35॥
4.5.36: That day, having travelled twenty yojanas, when the sun had set he stayed in a pleasant village, in the house of a certain brahmin. ॥36॥
4.5.37: That brahmin performed the sandhyā and other good rites according to rule, and there he offered hymns and the like to Śambhu of wondrous deeds. ॥37॥
4.5.38: Then the brahmin remained there with his servant, and two muhūrtas of the night passed there. ॥38॥
4.5.39: Meanwhile a wonder occurred there. Listen to it attentively, O sages; I shall tell it to you. ॥39॥
4.5.iti: Thus ends the fifth adhyāya, named The death of the brahmin woman, in the Nandikeśvara Māhātmya, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥5॥
4.6.1: Sūta said: And there was one auspicious cow tied up there in the courtyard. Just then, at night, the brahmin householder, who had gone out, came home. ॥1॥
4.6.2: Seeing the cow standing unmilked in the courtyard, he, wearied with vexation and wishing to milk her, spoke to his own wife, O lords of sages. ॥2॥
4.6.3: Dear, the cow has not been milked by you. Told thus, she brought the calf; then, having very quickly called the woman for the milking, ... ॥3॥
4.6.4: then that brahmin, the master of the house, eager for milk, himself made an effort to tie the calf to the peg, O sages. ॥4॥
4.6.5: The calf, pulling away, struck him on the foot, and the brahmin suffered pain, O you of good vows. ॥5॥
4.6.6: Because of that blow to his foot, the twice-born, stupefied with anger, then beat the calf very hard with blows. ॥6॥
4.6.7: The calf, hurt by him, then became exhausted. The cow was milked, but out of anger the twice-born did not release the calf. ॥7॥
4.6.8: The cow, who had given herself to be milked with great affection, then wept; and seeing her weeping, the calf then spoke these words. ॥8॥
4.6.9: The calf said: Why are you weeping, mother? What sorrow has come upon you? Tell me that, out of love. Hearing that, the cow spoke. ॥9॥
4.6.10: Hear my sorrow, son—indeed I cannot even speak it. You were beaten by that wicked one, and by that sorrow came to me as well. ॥10॥
4.6.11: Sūta said: Hearing his mother's words, that calf enlightened her; firmly grounded in the truth of prārabdha karma, he replied to his mother. ॥11॥
4.6.12: What is to be done? Where is one to go? For we are bound by karma. As deeds were done before, so they are experienced now. ॥12॥
4.6.13: A deed is done laughing; it is reaped weeping. There is no one who gives sorrow, and no one who gives happiness. ॥13॥
4.6.14: Joy and sorrow are given by another—this is held to be wrong understanding. I myself am the doer here—that too is called false knowledge. ॥14॥
4.6.15: Sorrow comes from one's own karma, and happiness from that same karma. Therefore karma is revered; everything rests in karma. ॥15॥
4.6.16: You and I, mother, and these living beings and the rest—all are bound by karma; they should never be grieved over by you. ॥16॥
4.6.17: Sūta said: Having heard thus her son's words full of wisdom, the cow, wretched and filled with grief for her son, said this. ॥17॥
4.6.18: The cow said: Child, you know everything—that creatures are subject to karma. Yet, seized by māyā, I fall into sorrow again. ॥18॥
4.6.19: Much weeping has been done, yet no relief from sorrow comes. Hearing these words, the calf said this to his mother. ॥19॥
4.6.20: The calf said: If you understand this, why weep again? Is anything achieved by doing so? Therefore give up your sorrow now. ॥20॥
4.6.21: Sūta said: Hearing her son's words thus, his mother, the cow, full of sorrow, then sighed deeply and spoke words to the calf. ॥21॥
4.6.22: The cow said: My sorrow will go only when a like sorrow befalls the brahmin too; I tell you this truly. ॥22॥
4.6.23: In the morning, son, he will be struck by me with my two horns, and once struck, his life will depart at once—there is no doubt. ॥23॥
4.6.24: The calf said: The fruit of the karma done earlier is being reaped now. And what fruit, mother, will you obtain from this killing of a brahmin? ॥24॥
4.6.25: Through merit and sin in equal measure, birth occurs in Bhārata; and when both are exhausted by experiencing their fruits, mother, liberation is attained. ॥25॥
4.6.26: Sometimes karma is destroyed, sometimes its experiencing arises. Therefore do not again set yourself to do such a deed. ॥26॥
4.6.27: How am I your son today, and how indeed are you my mother? The pride in sonship and motherhood is vain—let this be considered. ॥27॥
4.6.28: Know this: where is a mother, where a father, where a husband, where a wife? No one here belongs to anyone; all reap the fruits of their own deeds. ॥28॥
4.6.29: Knowing this, mother, you should give up sorrow with great effort, and practise virtuous conduct out of desire for happiness in the other world. ॥29॥
4.6.30: The cow said: I know this, son, but this māyā does not leave me. I shall give him a sorrow equal to your sorrow; that indeed I shall do. ॥30॥
4.6.31: And moreover, I have seen the place here where the sin of brahmin-slaying is destroyed; so my sin of killing will surely go away. ॥31॥
4.6.32: Sūta said: Hearing these words of his mother, the cow, O best of the twice-born, the calf fell silent there; nothing more was said by him. ॥32॥
4.6.33: Hearing that wondrous exchange between the two, the travelling brahmin then pondered in his heart, astonished, O lords of sages. ॥33॥
4.6.34: Only after seeing this most wondrous event in the morning should I go; and then from here I must go on to that place. ॥34॥
4.6.35: Sūta said: Having thus reflected in his heart, O twice-born ones, that brahmin, devoted to his mother and supremely amazed, slept there together with his servant. ॥35॥
4.6.36: Then, when morning came, the master of the house rose, woke that traveller, and said these words. ॥36॥
4.6.37: The brahmin said: Why are you still sleeping? It is fully morning. Set out on your journey to the country where you wish to go. ॥37॥
4.6.38: He replied: Listen, brahmin: there is pain in my servant's body. We will stay a little while and then go. ॥38॥
4.6.39: Sūta said: Having made this pretext, the man then slept on, in order to learn the whole of that wondrous, astonishing affair. ॥39॥
4.6.40: Then, at milking time, the brahmin, wishing to go somewhere on business, spoke to his own son. ॥40॥
4.6.41: The father said: Son, I am going off again somewhere on some business. Dear child, you must milk this cow of ours carefully. ॥41॥
4.6.42: Sūta said: Having said this, that excellent brahmin went off somewhere. The son then got up there and released the calf. ॥42॥
4.6.43: His mother herself then came for the milking. Then the brahmin's son, the calf—distressed, being struck with a peg— ॥43॥
4.6.44: —led to the cow's side to tie it up, eager for the milk. Then the cow, enraged, struck him with her horn. ॥44॥
4.6.45: Struck in a vital spot, he fell down unconscious. People gathered there saying, the boy has been gored by the cow. ॥45॥
4.6.46: Crying, water, water, they ran to where his father and others were. While efforts were being made, the boy died then. ॥46॥
4.6.47: When the boy died there, a great cry of lament arose. His mother was stricken with grief and wept again and again. ॥47॥
4.6.48: What shall I do? Where shall I go? Who can take away my sorrow? Weeping thus, she then beat the cow and let it loose. ॥48॥
4.6.49: That cow, white in colour, was then at once seen to have turned dark. Oh, look! the people cried out to one another. ॥49॥
4.6.50: Then the travelling brahmin, having seen this wonder, set out; wherever the cow went, there the brahmin followed her. ॥50॥
4.6.51: Raising her tail, the cow quickly ran toward the Narmadā, and coming near this Nandika tīrtha, into the Narmadā's water— ॥51॥
4.6.52: —having plunged in three times, she became white. She went back the way she came, and the brahmin was filled with amazement. ॥52॥
4.6.53: Oh, this is a most blessed tīrtha, removing the sin of slaying a brahmin! The brahmin himself bathed there, and likewise his servant. ॥53॥
4.6.54: Having bathed, the two went on, praising that river. On the way a certain beautiful woman, adorned with ornaments, met them. ॥54॥
4.6.55: She said to him: O traveller, from where are you going, so greatly astonished? Abandon deceit and tell the truth before me, O best of brahmins. ॥55॥
4.6.56: Sūta said: Hearing these words, the brahmin told everything exactly as it was. Then the woman again said to the brahmin there, stay here. ॥56॥
4.6.57: Hearing what she said, the brahmin stopped, and humble-minded he replied: What is it to be told? Speak. ॥57॥
4.6.58: She said: Here, at the very spot you saw, cast your mother's bones now. Why go elsewhere? ॥58॥
4.6.59: Your mother, O best of travellers, assuming a truly excellent divine body, will quickly attain the blessed state of Śambhu himself. ॥59॥
4.6.60: When the month of Vaiśākha arrives, on the auspicious seventh day of the bright fortnight, Gaṅgā always comes here, O best of brahmins. ॥60॥
4.6.61: Today itself is that seventh day. I am Gaṅgā, and I am going there. Having said this, the goddess Gaṅgā vanished, O best of sages. ॥61॥
4.6.62: The brahmin turned back, and as soon as he cast half of his mother's bones from his cloth into that tīrtha, a marvel took place. ॥62॥
4.6.63: His own mother was seen, having attained a divine body: You are blessed, you have fulfilled your duty, and the family has been purified by you. ॥63॥
4.6.64: May your wealth, grain, lifespan and lineage increase. Having repeatedly given this blessing to her son, she went to heaven. ॥64॥
4.6.65: There, having enjoyed abundant and supreme happiness for a long time, she attained the highest state by the grace of Śaṅkara. ॥65॥
4.6.66: And her son the brahmin, having then cast the remaining bones there as well, became joyful in mind and, purified in soul, went to his own home. ॥66॥
4.6.iti: Thus ends the sixth adhyāya, named The brahmin woman goes to heaven, in the account of the greatness of the Nandikeśvara liṅga, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥6॥
4.7.1: The sages said: How did Gaṅgā come, especially to the Narmadā, on the seventh day of the month of Vaiśākha? O Sūta, O lord, describe this. ॥1॥
4.7.2: And how did the Lord come to be known by the name Nandikeśa? Tell us that story too, with great kindness, O wise one. ॥2॥
4.7.3: Sūta said: Well asked, O best of sages, is this question concerning Nandikeśa. I shall now tell it today; hearing it increases merit. ॥3॥
4.7.4: A Brāhmaṇa woman named Ṛṣikā, daughter of a certain twice-born, was married according to rule to a certain Brāhmaṇa. ॥4॥
4.7.5: By the power of past deeds, that wife of the Brāhmaṇa, though of good vows, O chief Brāhmaṇas, became a widow while still a girl. ॥5॥
4.7.6: Then that Brāhmaṇa's wife, observing the vow of celibacy, performed very severe austerity, preceded by worship of an earthen liṅga. ॥6॥
4.7.7: At that time a wicked, powerful asura named Mūḍha, a great sorcerer, went there, struck by the arrow of desire. ॥7॥
4.7.8: Seeing her performing austerity, beautiful and exceedingly desirable, he begged her for enjoyment, displaying various enticements. ॥8॥
4.7.9: But that woman of good vows, devoted to meditation on Śiva, did not cast even a glance of desire on him, O lords of sages. ॥9॥
4.7.10: That Brāhmaṇa woman, devoted to austerity, did not respect him; she was exceedingly steadfast in austerity, resorting to meditation on Śiva. ॥10॥
4.7.11: Then that demon-king Mūḍha, scorned by that slender woman, became angry and afterwards showed her a terrible form. ॥11॥
4.7.12: Then the evil-souled one spoke harsh, frightening words and terrified that wife of the Brāhmaṇa again and again. ॥12॥
4.7.13: Then that slender Brāhmaṇa's wife, whose refuge was Śiva, stricken with fear, lovingly uttered the name Śiva many times. ॥13॥
4.7.14: Extremely distressed, that woman, uttering Śiva's name, took refuge in Śambhu for the protection of her own dharma. ॥14॥
4.7.15: To protect one who had sought refuge, to uphold good conduct, and for her joy, Śiva indeed appeared. ॥15॥
4.7.16: Then Śaṅkara, affectionate to his devotees, instantly reduced to ashes that demon-king named Mūḍha, overcome by lust. ॥16॥
4.7.17: Then the Supreme Lord, whose mind is skilled in protecting devotees, looking at her with a compassionate glance, said, ask for a boon. ॥17॥
4.7.18: Hearing Maheśa's words, that chaste Brāhmaṇa lady beheld Śaṅkara's auspicious form, which produces bliss. ॥18॥
4.7.19: Then bowing to Śambhu, the Supreme Lord who brings happiness, the chaste one of pure intent, with joined palms and bowed shoulders, praised him. ॥19॥
4.7.20: Ṛṣikā said: O God of gods, O Mahādeva, affectionate to those who seek refuge, you are the friend of the afflicted, the Lord, ever the protector of devotees. ॥20॥
4.7.21: Here you have protected my dharma from the asura named Mūḍha; since this wicked one has been slain, the world has been protected by you. ॥21॥
4.7.22: Grant me supreme, unfailing devotion to your feet. This alone is the boon, O Lord; what could be greater than this? ॥22॥
4.7.23: Hear another request of mine, O all-pervading one, O Maheśvara: for the benefit of the worlds, remain established here. ॥23॥
4.7.24: Sūta said: Having thus praised Mahādeva, that Ṛṣikā of auspicious vows fell silent; then Giriśa, the mine of compassion, spoke. ॥24॥
4.7.25: Giriśa said: O Ṛṣikā, you are of good conduct and especially my devotee. All the boons that you have asked for have been granted to you. ॥25॥
4.7.26: Meanwhile the gods, Hari, Brahmā and others, learning of Śiva's manifestation, came there filled with joy. ॥26॥
4.7.27: Bowing to Śiva with great love, they all worshipped him; and, O Brāhmaṇas, bowed down, pure-minded, with joined hands, they praised him. ॥27॥
4.7.28: At this time Gaṅgā, the heavenly river, with a very gracious heart, spoke to that chaste Ṛṣikā, praising her observance. ॥28॥
4.7.29: Gaṅgā said: For my sake, give me your word: in the month of Vaiśākha, for one day, you must grant me nearness so that I may stay here. ॥29॥
4.7.30: Sūta said: Hearing Gaṅgā's words, that chaste woman of good vows lovingly said, so be it, for the welfare of the worlds. ॥30॥
4.7.31: For her joy, Śiva Hara, well pleased, merged with his full portion into that earthen liṅga worshipped by her. ॥31॥
4.7.32: All the gods, very pleased, praised Śiva and her; Viṣṇu, Brahmā and the others, and also the heavenly river, went each to their own abode. ॥32॥
4.7.33: From that day it became such an excellent purifying tīrtha, and Śiva became renowned as Nandikeśa, destroyer of all sins. ॥33॥
4.7.34: Gaṅgā too goes there every year on that day with good intent, to wash away her own sin, which she has taken on from men, O Brāhmaṇas. ॥34॥
4.7.35: A man who bathes there properly and worships Nandikeśa is freed from all sins, even brahmin-slaying and the like. ॥35॥
4.7.iti: Thus ends the seventh adhyāya, named The greatness of the Nandikeśvara Śiva-liṅga, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥7॥
4.8.1: Sūta said: O twice-born ones, listen with true devotion as I describe those Śiva-liṅgas that are famed on earth in the western direction. ॥1॥
4.8.2: In the city of Kapilā there is the supremely divine Śiva-liṅga named Kālarāmeśvara, which takes away sin merely by being seen. ॥2॥
4.8.3: And at the western ocean Mahāsiddheśvara is celebrated; he grants dharma, wealth and desires, and likewise bestows liberation too. ॥3॥
4.8.4: Situated on the shore of the western ocean is Gokarṇa, the most excellent holy place, which destroys sins such as the killing of a brahmin and grants the fruit of all desires. ॥4॥
4.8.5: In Gokarṇa there are Śiva-liṅgas by crores upon crores, and countless tīrthas stand at every step. ॥5॥
4.8.6: What is the use of saying much here? Everything situated in Gokarṇa, in every way, is a visibly manifest liṅga of Śiva, and all its waters are tīrthas. ॥6॥
4.8.7: Dear one, the greatness of the Śiva-liṅgas and of all the tīrthas in Gokarṇa is described in the Purāṇas by the great sages. ॥7॥
4.8.8: In the Kṛta age he Mahābala is white, in the Tretā deep red, in the Dvāpara yellow-coloured, and in the Kali age he will be dark. ॥8॥
4.8.9: Though Mahābala pervades the hollows of the seven netherworlds, when the terrible Kali age arrives he will become soft. ॥9॥
4.8.10: Even great sinners, having worshipped here the Śiva-liṅga Mahābala in Gokarṇa, have gone to the abode of Śaṅkara. ॥10॥
4.8.11: O sages, those who go there to Gokarṇa on a day of an auspicious constellation and worship him with devotion become Rudras; there is no doubt. ॥11॥
4.8.12: Whatever man, whoever he may be, worships that Śiva-liṅga in Gokarṇa at any time whatever, he goes to the abode of Brahmā. ॥12॥
4.8.13: Out of the wish for the welfare of the gods, Brahmā, Viṣṇu and the rest, the god Śaṅkara is ever present there under the name Mahābala. ॥13॥
4.8.14: That liṅga, obtained through severe austerity by the demon named Rāvaṇa, was installed in Gokarṇa by the Leader of the Gaṇas Gaṇeśa. ॥14॥
4.8.15: Viṣṇu, Brahmā, the great Indra, the Viśvedevas, the hosts of Maruts, the Ādityas, the Vasus, the two Aśvins, and the Moon together with the stars— ॥15॥
4.8.16: These gods, travelling in aerial cars, together with their attendants, attend upon his eastern gate for the sake of pleasing him. ॥16॥
4.8.17: Yama, Death himself in person, Citragupta and Agni, together with the Pitṛs and the Rudras, have resorted to the southern gate. ॥17॥
4.8.18: Varuṇa, lord of rivers, with the hosts of rivers beginning with the Gaṅgā, resorting to the western gate, serve Mahābala. ॥18॥
4.8.19: Likewise Vāyu, Kubera and the sovereign goddess Bhadrakālikā, with the Mothers headed by Caṇḍikā, have resorted to the northern gate. ॥19॥
4.8.20: All the gods with the Gandharvas, the Pitṛs, the Siddhas and Cāraṇas, the Vidyādharas, Kimpuruṣas, Kinnaras, Guhyakas and birds— ॥20॥
4.8.21: Various Piśācas, Vetālas and mighty Daityas, all the Nāgas beginning with Śeṣa, the Siddhas and all the sages— ॥21॥
4.8.22: —praise that god and bow down to Mahābala; they obtain their desired wishes and enjoy themselves as they please. ॥22॥
4.8.23: Many have performed fine austerity there and, having worshipped that all-pervading Lord, have attained the supreme accomplishment, which gives happiness here and hereafter. ॥23॥
4.8.24: The Śiva-liṅga in Gokarṇa is declared to be the gate of liberation; O twice-born ones, he who is named Mahābala is worshipped and praised there. ॥24॥
4.8.25: The worship of Mahābala on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight of Māgha especially bestows liberation on all, even on sinners. ॥25॥
4.8.26: On this holy day of Śiva, great multitudes of all four varṇas, eager to see the grand festival, come from every land. ॥26॥
4.8.27: Women, the old, children and those living in the four āśramas, having come there and seen the Lord of gods, attained fulfilment of their purpose. ॥27॥
4.8.28: They attained this through the power of Mahābala; and once a certain Cāṇḍāla woman, having worshipped that liṅga of Śiva, quickly went to Śiva's world. ॥28॥
4.8.iti: Thus ends the eighth adhyāya, named The greatness of Mahābala, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥8॥
4.9.1: The sages said: O Sūta, O Sūta, most fortunate one, you are blessed, the best of Śaivas. Who is the cāṇḍāla woman who was mentioned? Tell us her story, O lord. ॥1॥
4.9.2: Sūta said: O twice-born ones, listen with true devotion to that most wondrous story, interwoven with Śiva's power, which increases the devotion of those who hear it. ॥2॥
4.9.3: That cāṇḍāla woman, in a former birth, was a brahmin's daughter named Saumini, moon-faced and endowed with every auspicious mark. ॥3॥
4.9.4: Then, O twice-born ones, when the maiden Saumini had come of age and was a young woman, her father duly gave her in marriage to a certain brahmin's son. ॥4॥
4.9.5: Having obtained a husband, she of good vows, radiant with fresh youth, enjoyed herself with him for some time, O best of the twice-born. ॥5॥
4.9.6: Then Saumini's husband, the young brahmin, afflicted by a severe illness, met his death through the course of time, O twice-born ones. ॥6॥
4.9.7: When her husband died, that woman, grieved and deeply dejected in mind, lived in the house for some time, of good conduct and virtuous character. ॥7॥
4.9.8: Then, her heart possessed by desire, though a widow, owing to the peculiar force of youth she became unchaste. ॥8॥
4.9.9: Learning of her evil deed that defiled the family, her kinsmen assembled, dragged her far away by the hair, and abandoned her. ॥9॥
4.9.10: A certain prominent śūdra, seeing her wandering at her own will in the forest, made her his woman and then took her to his own house. ॥10॥
4.9.11: Then she, eating meat and constantly drinking liquor, fond of sexual pleasure, bore a daughter by that śūdra. ॥11॥
4.9.12: Once, when her husband had gone somewhere, the unchaste Saumini, having drunk liquor, craved a meal of meat. ॥12॥
4.9.13: Then, with the rams tethered together with the cows in the pen outside, at nightfall, when it was blind with darkness, she took a sword and went. ॥13॥
4.9.14: Without reflecting, owing to her drunken state, that most wretched meat-lover killed a single bleating calf, thinking it a ram. ॥14॥
4.9.15: Having brought the slain animal home and realising it was a calf, the woman in fear said, Śiva, Śiva, owing to some meritorious deed of the past. ॥15॥
4.9.16: Having meditated on Śiva for a moment, she, eager to eat meat, cut up that very calf and made the meal she desired. ॥16॥
4.9.17: Thus, after much time had passed, O twice-born ones, Saumini fell under the sway of Death and went to Yama's abode. ॥17॥
4.9.18: Yama, too, considering her merit and her former deeds, turned her back from residence in hell and made her of cāṇḍāla birth. ॥18॥
4.9.19: Then, fallen from Yama's city, she entered the womb of a cāṇḍāla woman, and was born blind, dark as an extinguished coal. ॥19॥
4.9.20: Blind from birth, she lost father and mother even in childhood; being wretched and afflicted by severe leprosy, she was married by no one. ॥20॥
4.9.21: Then, tormented by hunger, miserable, staff in hand and sightless, she appeased the fire of her belly with the leftover morsels of cāṇḍālas. ॥21॥
4.9.22: Thus, having passed her long life in great hardship, her whole body seized by old age, she suffered insurmountable misery. ॥22॥
4.9.23: Once, as Śiva's holy day was approaching, that cāṇḍāla woman learned that crowds of travellers were going to that shrine of Gokarṇa. ॥23॥
4.9.24: Then that cāṇḍāla woman too, longing for clothing and food, set out very slowly to beg from the crowds. ॥24॥
4.9.25: Having gone there, the cāṇḍāla woman wandered here and there, beseeching the crowds with piteous words and outstretched cupped hands. ॥25॥
4.9.26: As the cāṇḍāla woman was thus begging, a most virtuous traveller cast a sprig of bilva into her outstretched cupped hands. ॥26॥
4.9.27: Feeling it again and again as it fell into her hands, and judging it inedible, the distressed woman threw it far away. ॥27॥
4.9.28: Released from her hand in the night, that bilva sprig by good fortune fell on the top of a certain Śiva-liṅga. ॥28॥
4.9.29: Thus, on the night of Śiva's fourteenth, though she begged the travellers again and again, by the turn of fate she obtained nothing at all. ॥29॥
4.9.30: Thus, unknowingly, the pure vow of Śiva's fourteenth came about, along with the vigil that bestows supreme bliss. ॥30॥
4.9.31: Then at dawn that woman, overwhelmed by great sorrow, miserable, slowly turned back alone toward her own place. ॥31॥
4.9.32: Exhausted by her long fast, stumbling at every step, having crossed only that much ground, she fell down unconscious. ॥32॥
4.9.33: Then, by Śambhu's grace, she went to the supreme abode, mounting a splendid aerial chariot brought swiftly by Śiva's attendants. ॥33॥
4.9.34: Because earlier this woman, though unchaste, uttered Śiva's name even by accident, by that merit, augmented here, O brahmins, she attained the divine abode of Mahābala. ॥34॥
4.9.35: For at holy Gokarṇa, on Śiva's day, having fasted and kept vigil, she performed at night the worship with bilva on Śiva's head. ॥35॥
4.9.36: Even today, by the grace of Mahābala, she enjoys the fruit of this merit performed without intention. ॥36॥
4.9.37: Such is Śaṅkara's great liṅga Mahābala, which instantly removes all sins and bestows supreme bliss. ॥37॥
4.9.38: Thus, O brahmins, I have told you the supreme greatness of the excellent Śiva-liṅga called Mahābala. ॥38॥
4.9.39: Now I shall tell another wondrous account of its greatness, by merely hearing which devotion to Śiva quickly arises. ॥39॥
4.9.iti: Thus ends the ninth adhyāya, named The attainment of a good end by the Cāṇḍāla woman, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥9॥
4.10.1: Sūta said: In the illustrious Ikṣvāku dynasty there was a supremely righteous king named Mitrasaha, the foremost of all archers. ॥1॥
4.10.2: That king's beloved, Madayantī, was most devoted to dharma and auspicious; she was renowned as a chaste wife, like Damayantī the wife of Nala. ॥2॥
4.10.3: Once King Mitrasaha, who was fond of hunting, went into a dense forest accompanied by a great army. ॥3॥
4.10.4: Roaming there, the king slew a night-prowler named Kamaṭha, a very wicked villain who tormented the virtuous. ॥4॥
4.10.5: Then his sinful younger brother, a deceiver, thinking, I shall overcome him by trickery alone, went to the king's presence. ॥5॥
4.10.6: Seeing him of humble appearance, come to take up service, the king out of ignorance made him superintendent of the kitchen. ॥6॥
4.10.7: Then, having sported in that forest for some time, the king turned back, gave up the hunt, and joyfully returned to his own city. ॥7॥
4.10.8: When the anniversary of his father's death arrived, the king invited his own preceptor Vasiṣṭha, brought him to his house, and fed him with devotion. ॥8॥
4.10.9: Seeing placed before him a dish of vegetables and meat mixed with human flesh by the demon in the guise of a cook, the preceptor then spoke. ॥9॥
4.10.10: The guru said: Fie on you, O king! Since human flesh has been offered to me by you, a deceiver and villain, you shall therefore become a demon. ॥10॥
4.10.11: Then, realising that it had been done by the demon, the preceptor reconsidered and made that curse last twelve years. ॥11॥
4.10.12: The king, knowing the curse to be undeserved, was overcome with anger; taking water in his cupped hands, he made ready to curse the preceptor. ॥12॥
4.10.13: Then his beloved, the chaste and righteous Madayantī, falling at his feet, restrained him from that curse. ॥13॥
4.10.14: Then, desisting from the curse out of regard for her words, he let the water fall on his own feet; his feet became stained. ॥14॥
4.10.15: From then on, O lords of sages, that king became known in this world as Kalmaṣāṅghri ('stained-foot'), indeed through the power of that water. ॥15॥
4.10.16: Through the curse of his preceptor, the best of sages, King Mitrasaha became a terrible, violent demon roaming the forest. ॥16॥
4.10.17: Bearing a demonic form like Kāla, Antaka and Yama, he roamed the forest and devoured various creatures, humans and others. ॥17॥
4.10.18: Once, somewhere in the forest, he, looking like Death, saw a young newly-married sage couple sporting together. ॥18॥
4.10.19: That man-eating demon, afflicted by the curse, seized the young son of the sage in order to eat him, as a tiger seizes a fawn. ॥19॥
4.10.20: Seeing her husband seized under his arm, his frightened beloved pleaded with him, speaking piteous words. ॥20॥
4.10.21: Though entreated many times, that pitiless, evil-minded man-eater cut off the brahmin boy's head and devoured it. ॥21॥
4.10.22: Then that wretched chaste woman, greatly grieved, lamented, gathered her husband's bones, and made a fierce blazing pyre. ॥22॥
4.10.23: Following her husband and entering the fire, that brahmin woman cursed the king in his demon form: ॥23॥
4.10.24: From today, whenever you unite with women, then shall be your death. Having said this, the chaste woman entered the fire. ॥24॥
4.10.25: That king too, having undergone his preceptor's curse for its fixed term, regained his own form and joyfully went to his home. ॥25॥
4.10.26: Knowing of the curse of the brahmin's chaste wife, Madayantī, greatly fearing widowhood, restrained her husband who desired love-making. ॥26॥
4.10.27: Childless and disgusted with royal pleasures, the king gave up all his wealth and went to the forest. ॥27॥
4.10.28: He saw the sin of brahmin-slaying, very painful and hideous in form, following behind him and threatening him again and again. ॥28॥
4.10.29: Seeking release from her, the king, dejected in mind, employed various means such as japa, vows, and sacrifices. ॥29॥
4.10.30: O brahmins, when the king's brahmin-slaying did not cease by various means such as bathing at holy places, he then went to Mithilā. ॥30॥
4.10.31: Having reached an outer garden, tormented by intense anxiety about her, the king saw the sage Gautama approaching. ॥31॥
4.10.32: Approaching Gautama of pure heart, that great king, having gained some relief from seeing him, bowed again and again. ॥32॥
4.10.33: Then, asked by him about his welfare, sighing long and hot, and having gained comfort from his compassionate glance, the king spoke to him. ॥33॥
4.10.34: The king said: O sage, this insurmountable brahmin-slaying torments me; unseen by others, dear sir, she threatens me at every step. ॥34॥
4.10.35: Since a brahmin's son was devoured by me while I was burnt by the curse, there is no expiation of that sin even by thousands of penances. ॥35॥
4.10.36: Wandering about, O sage, I tried various means to quell it; yet the brahmin-slaying of sinful me has not ceased—what more can I do? ॥36॥
4.10.37: Today I feel as though my birth has borne fruit, for by the mere sight of you a flood of joy has arisen in me. ॥37॥
4.10.38: Today, O fortunate one, grant peace to me, a sinner who has taken refuge at your lotus-feet, so that I may attain happiness. ॥38॥
4.10.39: Sūta said: Thus addressed by the king, Gautama, his mind moist with compassion, properly prescribed the expiation for terrible sins. ॥39॥
4.10.40: Gautama said: Well done, O great king, you are blessed; give up fear of great sins. When Śiva is the ruler, where is fear for devotees who seek refuge? ॥40॥
4.10.41: Listen, O king, O greatly fortunate one: there is another established sacred site, the abode of Śiva called Gokarṇa, which destroys even the great sins. ॥41॥
4.10.42: There sins cannot remain, not even the greatest of the great; Śiva himself is present there under the name Mahābala. ॥42॥
4.10.43: Among all Śiva-liṅgas, Mahābala is the sovereign; in the four ages he takes four colours, and he removes all sins. ॥43॥
4.10.44: Gokarṇa, an excellent tīrtha, lies on the shore of the western ocean; there is that Śiva-liṅga which destroys great sins. ॥44॥
4.10.45: Great sinners, having gone there, bathed abundantly in the tīrthas and worshipped Mahābala, have attained the abode of Śaṅkara. ॥45॥
4.10.46: So you too, O lord of kings, should go to Gokarṇa, the abode of Giriśa, worship that liṅga, and attain fulfilment. ॥46॥
4.10.47: Having bathed there in all the tīrthas and worshipped Mahābala, freed from all sins, you will attain Śiva's world. ॥47॥
4.10.48: Sūta said: Thus instructed by the great-souled sage Gautama, the king, his mind overjoyed, went to Gokarṇa. ॥48॥
4.10.49: Having bathed well there in the tīrthas and duly worshipped Mahābala, his entire mass of sins shaken off, he attained the supreme abode of Śambhu. ॥49॥
4.10.50: Whoever regularly listens to this beloved story of Mahābala goes to Śiva's world together with twenty-one generations of his family. ॥50॥
4.10.51: Thus I have narrated to you the supremely wondrous greatness of Mahābala, the liṅga of Giriśa, which removes all sins. ॥51॥
4.10.iti: Thus ends the tenth adhyāya, named The greatness of the Śiva-liṅga called Mahābala, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥10॥
4.11.1: The sages said: O Sūta, O Sūta, most fortunate one, blessed are you, whose mind is devoted to Śiva! This wondrous story of the Mahābala liṅga has been narrated to us by you. ॥1॥
4.11.2: And whatever Śiva-liṅgas there are in the northern direction, tell us their pure glory, which destroys sin. ॥2॥
4.11.3: Sūta said: Listen attentively, O Brāhmaṇas: I shall relate in brief the glory of the Śiva-liṅgas, particularly of the northern ones. ॥3॥
4.11.4: Gokarṇa is another holy region, destroying the great sins; and there is a great forest there, holy and very extensive. ॥4॥
4.11.5: There stands the supreme Śiva-liṅga named Candrabhāla, brought by Rāvaṇa out of true devotion, granting all accomplishments. ॥5॥
4.11.6: O lords of sages, his abiding there, like that of Vaidyanātha, is for the welfare of all the worlds, he being an ocean of compassion. ॥6॥
4.11.7: Having bathed at Gokarṇa and worshipped Candrabhāla, one attains the world of Śiva — truly, truly, there is no doubt. ॥7॥
4.11.8: The glory of the Candrabhāla liṅga is supremely wondrous; it cannot be described fully, even by Vyāsa, who delights in devotion and love. ॥8॥
4.11.9: The great glory of the Candrabhāla Mahādeva liṅga has been told somehow; now listen to that of another liṅga. ॥9॥
4.11.10: The Dādhīca Śiva-liṅga, at the tīrtha of the Miśra sages, was installed with great love by Dadhīci, lord of sages. ॥10॥
4.11.11: Going there and bathing in that tīrtha properly according to rule, one should reverently worship the Śiva-liṅga Dādhīceśvara. ॥11॥
4.11.12: Right there, the image of Dadhīci should be worshipped according to rule, promptly, for Śiva's pleasure, by those seeking the fruit of pilgrimage. ॥12॥
4.11.13: When this is done, O best of sages, a man becomes fulfilled; having enjoyed every happiness here, he attains the highest goal hereafter. ॥13॥
4.11.14: At the Naimiṣāraṇya tīrtha there is a Śiva-liṅga, installed by all the sages, famed as Ṛṣīśvara, bestowing happiness. ॥14॥
4.11.15: By seeing and worshipping it, even sinful people obtain enjoyment and liberation, here and hereafter, O lords of sages. ॥15॥
4.11.16: At the Hatyāharaṇa tīrtha, the sin-removing Śiva-liṅga should be especially worshipped; it destroys crores of the sins of killing. ॥16॥
4.11.17: At the Devaprayāga tīrtha, the Śiva-liṅga named Laliteśvara, destroyer of all sins, should always be worshipped by men. ॥17॥
4.11.18: In the city called Nayapāla, renowned on earth, is the liṅga named Paśupatīśa, granting the fruit of all desires. ॥18॥
4.11.19: That Śiva-liṅga indeed exists in the form of the head portion; I shall narrate its story in the description of Kedāreśvara. ॥19॥
4.11.20: Near it is the most wondrous Śiva-liṅga named Muktinātha; by seeing and worshipping it, enjoyment and liberation are obtained. ॥20॥
4.11.21: Thus the excellent description of the liṅgas in the four directions has been told to you, O best of sages. What else do you wish to hear? ॥21॥
4.11.iti: Thus ends the eleventh adhyāya, named The greatness of the Candrabhāla and Paśupatinātha liṅgas, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥11॥
4.12.1: The sages said: O Sūta, by the grace of Vyāsa you know every matter; nothing is unknown to you. Therefore we ask you. ॥1॥
4.12.2: The liṅga is worshipped in the world, and what you have told about it is just so; but is there not some other reason for it here? ॥2॥
4.12.3: Pārvatī, the beloved of Śiva, is heard in the world to have the form of the bāṇa pedestal. What is the reason for this, O Sūta? Tell it as you have heard it. ॥3॥
4.12.4: Sūta said: O twice-born, I heard from Vyāsa the story of the different kalpas; that very story I tell now. Let it be heard, O best of sages. ॥4॥
4.12.5: Let that very event which happened long ago to the twice-born in the Dāru forest be heard properly; I shall narrate it as I heard it. ॥5॥
4.12.6: There was an excellent forest named Dāru; there lived the best of sages, devotees of Śiva, ever and always intent on meditation on Śiva. ॥6॥
4.12.7: They performed the worship of Śiva at the three times of day without interruption; those lords of sages praised him with divine hymns of many kinds. ॥7॥
4.12.8: Once they all went into the forest to gather sacrificial fuel—all those bulls among the twice-born, Śaivas intent on meditation on Śiva. ॥8॥
4.12.9: Meanwhile Śaṅkara himself, the Blue-red One, assuming a deformed appearance, came there in order to test them. ॥9॥
4.12.10: Naked, exceedingly radiant, adorned with ash as his ornament, he behaved in an indecent way, holding his liṅga in his hand. ॥10॥
4.12.11: With the intention in his mind of doing what was dear to those forest-dwellers, Hara himself, pleased with his devotees, went lovingly to that forest. ॥11॥
4.12.12: Seeing him, those wives of the sages fell into great fear; others, agitated and amazed, likewise came together again to him. ॥12॥
4.12.13: Some embraced him, and others took hold of his hand; then those women, jostling one another, were wholly immersed in him. ॥13॥
4.12.14: At that very time the eminent sages arrived; seeing him acting improperly, they were distressed and overcome with anger. ॥14॥
4.12.15: Then, stricken with distress, all those sages, deluded by Śiva's māyā, said: Who is this? Who is this? ॥15॥
4.12.16: When that naked ascetic said nothing at all, then those great sages spoke to that fearsome person. ॥16॥
4.12.17: Since you are doing what is improper, destructive of the Vedic path, therefore let that liṅga of yours fall to the surface of the earth. ॥17॥
4.12.18: Sūta said: When they had said this, the liṅga of that avadhūta, Śiva of wondrous form, fell instantly. ॥18॥
4.12.19: That liṅga, like fire, burned everything that stood before it; wherever it went, there it burned again. ॥19॥
4.12.20: It went into Pātāla, and likewise into heaven; it went everywhere on earth, and nowhere did it stay still. ॥20॥
4.12.21: The worlds became agitated, and those sages were greatly distressed; none found peace—neither the gods nor the sages. ॥21॥
4.12.22: All those gods and sages by whom Śiva had not been recognised, distressed, assembled quickly and went to Brahmā for refuge. ॥22॥
4.12.23: Going there, all those twice-born bowed to and praised Vidhi, and told the whole event to Brahmā, the maker of creation. ॥23॥
4.12.24: Brahmā, hearing their words and knowing them to be deluded by Śiva's māyā, bowed to Śaṅkara and spoke to those best of sages. ॥24॥
4.12.25: Brahmā said: O twice-born, you, though men of knowledge, do what is blameworthy; if the ignorant were to do so, what more need be said? ॥25॥
4.12.26: Having thus opposed the god Śiva, who can hope for welfare? Whoever at midday does not attend to a guest— ॥26॥
4.12.27: the guest goes away taking that person's merit and leaving behind his own sin; how much more so in the case of Śiva himself? ॥27॥
4.12.28: As long as the liṅga is not stable, nothing auspicious will arise anywhere in the three worlds; this I tell you truly. ॥28॥
4.12.29: You must act in such a way that the Śiva-liṅga may become steady here, O sages; let it be carefully considered in your minds. ॥29॥
4.12.30: Sūta said: Thus addressed, the sages bowed and said to Brahmā: O Vidhi, what should we do? Instruct us what is to be done. ॥30॥
4.12.31: Thus addressed by those lords of sages, Brahmā, grandfather of all worlds, then himself spoke to them. ॥31॥
4.12.32: Brahmā said: Let the gods worship the goddess Girijā and entreat Śivā; if she takes the form of the yoni, then it will attain stability. ॥32॥
4.12.33: I shall now explain the procedure for it; listen, all of you, O excellent ones. Perform it with love, and she will be pleased. ॥33॥
4.12.34: Having set up a pot and drawn an excellent eight-petalled lotus, one should then fill it with sacred water, along with dūrvā grass and barley sprouts. ॥34॥
4.12.35: Then one should consecrate that pot with Vedic mantras, having performed its worship by the method taught in śruti, while remembering Śiva. ॥35॥
4.12.36: O great sages, one should bathe that liṅga with that water; sprinkled with the Śatarudriya mantras, it will attain peace. ॥36॥
4.12.37: Then, having installed the auspicious bāṇa in the form of Girijā's yoni, that liṅga should be installed upon it, and one should again consecrate it with mantras. ॥37॥
4.12.38: With fragrances and sandal-paste, with flowers, incense and the like, and with worship such as food-offerings, one should please the Supreme Lord. ॥38॥
4.12.39: Likewise with prostrations, holy hymns, instrumental music and songs; then, having performed the svastyayana benediction rite, one should proclaim, Victory! ॥39॥
4.12.40: Be gracious, O Lord of gods, bringer of joy to the world. You are the creator and the preserver, you are the destroyer, beyond all words. ॥40॥
4.12.41: You are the origin of the world, the womb of the world, and also the one who dwells within the world. Be calm, O Maheśāna, and protect all the worlds. ॥41॥
4.12.42: When this rite has been performed, well-being will come about, there is no doubt. There will be no disturbance in these three worlds; there will always be happiness. ॥42॥
4.12.43: Sūta said: Thus addressed, those Brāhmaṇas and gods bowed to the Grandfather Brahmā and went for refuge to that Śiva, desiring the happiness of all the worlds. ॥43॥
4.12.44: Then Śaṅkara, worshipped with supreme devotion and entreated, became very pleased, and the Great Lord spoke to them. ॥44॥
4.12.45: Maheśvara said: O gods and all you sages, listen to my words with respect. If my liṅga is held in the form of a yoni, then there will be well-being. ॥45॥
4.12.46: Apart from Pārvatī, no other is able to hold the liṅga. Held by her, my liṅga will quickly become calm. ॥46॥
4.12.47: Sūta said: Hearing that, O lords of sages, the sages and gods, greatly delighted, taking Brahmā along, then entreated Girijā. ॥47॥
4.12.48: Having pleased Girijā and the bull-bannered one Śiva too, and having performed the rite described earlier, the excellent liṅga was installed. ॥48॥
4.12.49: By the procedure prescribed in the mantras, the gods and the sages likewise pleased Girijā and Śiva, for the sake of dharma. ॥49॥
4.12.50: All the gods and sages especially worshipped Śiva — Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and others too, and the three worlds with their moving and unmoving beings. ॥50॥
4.12.51: Śiva became very pleased, and so did Śivā, the Mother of the world; and then she held that liṅga in that form. ॥51॥
4.12.52: When the liṅga was installed, there was then welfare for the worlds, and that liṅga became famous in the three worlds, O Brāhmaṇas. ॥52॥
4.12.53: It is known as Hāṭakeśa and also as Śivāśiva. By worshipping it, happiness arises for people in every way. ॥53॥
4.12.54: Here there will be abundant prosperity of every kind, bringing many joys; and hereafter supreme liberation — no doubt need be entertained about this. ॥54॥
4.12.iti: Thus ends the twelfth adhyāya, named The cause of the form of the liṅga, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥12॥
4.13.1: Sūta said: O brāhmaṇas, I have lovingly told you how Śiva came to take the form of the liṅga, worthy of worship in the three worlds. What else do you wish to hear? ॥1॥
4.13.2: The sages said: O lord, tell us the greatness of the Andhakeśvara liṅga, and here you should also kindly tell us about other Śiva-liṅgas. ॥2॥
4.13.3: Sūta said: Long ago the demon Andhakāsura, tormentor of the gods, dwelling in a pit in the ocean, brought the three worlds under his control. ॥3॥
4.13.4: Coming out of that pit and oppressing the people, the very mighty demon would then enter that pit again. ॥4॥
4.13.5: All the gods, distressed, entreated Śiva again and again and reported everything, their own suffering, O chief sages. ॥5॥
4.13.6: Sūta said: Hearing those words of the gods, the Supreme Lord, slayer of the wicked and refuge of the good, replied with a gracious mind. ॥6॥
4.13.7: Śiva said: I shall have that demon Andhaka, tormentor of the gods, slain. Lead out the army, O gods; I am coming with my gaṇas. ॥7॥
4.13.8: Then, when that terrifying Andhaka, enemy of gods and sages, had come out of the pit, the gods occupied the pit. ॥8॥
4.13.9: The demons and the gods fought a most terrible battle, and then, by Śiva's grace, the gods became very strong. ॥9॥
4.13.10: Hard pressed by the gods, he made for the pit, but just as he reached it he was transfixed with the trident by Śiva, the Supreme Self. ॥10॥
4.13.11: Lying there, he then meditated on Śambhu and prayed: One who sees you at the time of death becomes like you in an instant. ॥11॥
4.13.12: Praised in this way, Śaṅkara was pleased and spoke there: Name a boon; I shall grant it to you. ॥12॥
4.13.13: Hearing these words, the demon, now endowed with a sāttvic disposition, bowed deeply to Śiva, praised him, and spoke again. ॥13॥
4.13.14: Andhaka said: O Lord of the gods, if you are pleased, grant me auspicious devotion to you, and showing special grace, remain established here. ॥14॥
4.13.15: Sūta said: Thus addressed by him, Hara cast that demon into that pit, and he himself remained there in the form of a liṅga, out of desire for the good of the world. ॥15॥
4.13.16: The man who worships that liṅga, Andhakeśa, daily attains the fulfilment of his wishes within six months; there is no doubt. ॥16॥
4.13.17: But the brāhmaṇa who worships for six months this liṅga, which benefits the world, for the sake of livelihood, is known as a devalaka. ॥17॥
4.13.18: He then becomes, here, just like a devalaka; and for one who is called a devalaka there is no entitlement as a twice-born. ॥18॥
4.13.19: The sages said: Who is called a devalaka, and what is his duty? O most wise one, tell us the truth for the welfare of the worlds. ॥19॥
4.13.20: Sūta said: There was a brāhmaṇa named Dadhīci, most righteous, master of the Vedas, ever delighting in devotion to Śiva and devoted to the Śaiva scriptures. ॥20॥
4.13.21: He had a son known by the name Sudarśana; and Sudarśana's wife was named Dukūlā, born of a wicked family. ॥21॥
4.13.22: The husband was under her control; he had four sons. He too always performed the worship of Śiva alone. ॥22॥
4.13.23: At that time Dadhīci had to stay in another village; because of ties with his kinsmen, he was not released by them. ॥23॥
4.13.24: Having told his son, remain devoted to Śiva, and having said this, Dadhīci, best of Śaivas, being let go, departed. ॥24॥
4.13.25: His son Sudarśana too performed the worship of Śiva. In this way a very long time passed, O chief sages. ॥25॥
4.13.26: Then once Śivarātri arrived, and on it all observed the fast, each of their own accord, as the occasion came. ॥26॥
4.13.27: He who was known as Sudarśana, having performed the worship, went away; but having had union with a woman on Śivarātri, he came here again. ॥27॥
4.13.28: He did not bathe, yet performed Śiva's worship that night. Because of the fruition of that deed, Śaṅkara, angered, spoke. ॥28॥
4.13.29: Maheśvara said: O wicked one, on Śivarātri you have had intercourse with a woman, and without bathing, thoughtlessly, you have performed my worship. ॥29॥
4.13.30: Since you did this knowingly, therefore become dull-witted. Become untouchable to me, and behold me only from afar. ॥30॥
4.13.31: Sūta said: Thus cursed by Maheśa, Sudarśana, son of Dadhīci, deluded by Śiva's māyā, at once became dull-witted. ॥31॥
4.13.32: At that moment, O brāhmaṇas, Dadhīci, best of Śaivas, returned from the other village and heard what had happened. ॥32॥
4.13.33: He too, as if rebuked by Śiva, became exceedingly grieved, and, in sorrow over his son's deed, wept: Alas, I am ruined! ॥33॥
4.13.34: Dadhīci, esteemed by the good, said again and again: By this wicked son my excellent family has been ruined. ॥34॥
4.13.35: The son too, stricken, and rebuked by his own father, was seized by remorse and at once denounced his wife as a wanton woman. ॥35॥
4.13.36: There his father worshipped Girijā with excellent rites, with great effort and great devotion, for the sake of his son's well-being. ॥36॥
4.13.37: Sudarśana too himself worshipped Girijā, following the method of Caṇḍī worship, with great devotion and auspicious hymns. ॥37॥
4.13.38: Thus father and son, through various means and with deep devotion, made the goddess Girijā, who loves her devotees, pleased. ॥38॥
4.13.39: Pleased by the power of their service, Caṇḍikā Girijā then adopted Sudarśana as her son, O sage. ॥39॥
4.13.40: Caṇḍikā herself propitiated Śiva for the sake of her son; Caṇḍī, angry and then no longer angry, again had a gracious mind toward that son. ॥40॥
4.13.41: Then, knowing that Maheśa, the bull-bannered one, was pleased, and having bowed to him, she herself placed Sudarśana on his lap. ॥41॥
4.13.42: Then Girijā herself performed the ghee-bath of her son; and a sacred thread of three twists, joined with a single knot, ॥42॥
4.13.43: Ambikā then gave with affection to her son Sudarśana, imparting the Śiva-Gāyatrī consisting of sixteen syllables, ॥43॥
4.13.44: namely Oṃ namaḥ śivāya preceded by the word śrī. She said: This boy (baṭu) should perform the saṅkalpa-worship sixteen times, ॥44॥
