4.13.45: worshipping the bull-bannered one from bathing up to prostration, with mantras, musical instruments and offerings, in the presence of the sages. ॥45॥
4.13.46: She then made him recite many name-mantras. And then Caṇḍikā, with a well-pleased heart, and likewise Śiva said: ॥46॥
4.13.47: Whatever wealth, grain and the like is offered to me, all that is to be accepted by you; it will not lead to any fault. ॥47॥
4.13.48: In my rites you are the foremost, and especially in the Devī's rites; ghee, oil and all else offered to me is to be taken by you. ॥48॥
4.13.49: When a prājāpatya feast takes place, then you alone should be the one fed; then the worship is complete, otherwise it is all fruitless. ॥49॥
4.13.50: A round tilaka is to be made by you, and bathing always done; the Śiva-sandhyā is to be performed, and its Gāyatrī. ॥50॥
4.13.51: Having first done my service, other duty befitting your family should be done. When everything is done thus, there will be well-being; your faults are forgiven by me. ॥51॥
4.13.52: Sūta said: Having said this, his four sons were then consecrated as baṭukas in the four directions by Śiva, the supreme Self. ॥52॥
4.13.53: And Caṇḍī, placing her son Sudarśana near herself, directed his sons, having given boons in many ways. ॥53॥
4.13.54: The Goddess said: Whoever is my baṭuka, between two opposing battle-arrays his victory shall always be; no doubt should be entertained in this. ॥54॥
4.13.55: By whom you are worshipped, by him alone am I truly worshipped. And your own duty must always be done by you all, O son. ॥55॥
4.13.56: Sūta said: Thus boons were given out of compassion to the great-souled Sudarśana together with his sons by Śiva and Śivā, for the sake of the worlds. ॥56॥
4.13.57: Because they were established by Śiva and Śivā, they are called baṭukas; because they were born of one fallen from austerity, they are called tapo'dhamas (lowly in austerity). ॥57॥
4.13.58: By the grace of Śiva and Śivā they all spread out in many ways. And theirs is the first worship, the great worship of the great-souled Lord. ॥58॥
4.13.59: As long as the worship of Śaṅkara has not been done by him the baṭuka, so long others' worship should not be done; if it is done, it is not auspicious. ॥59॥
4.13.60: Whether good or bad, one should not abandon the baṭuka; in the prājāpatya and in feeding, a single baṭu is preeminent. ॥60॥
4.13.61: Likewise in the rites of Śiva and Śivā a special distinction is seen here; hear that, O very wise one, as I tell it to you, O sinless one. ॥61॥
4.13.62: In the city of that same king Bhadra, during the daily feeding, in the observance of the prājāpatya, near the liṅga Andhakeśa, ॥62॥
4.13.63: the wondrous event that took place through Śiva's grace — let it be heard with great delight; I narrate it as I have heard it. ॥63॥
4.13.64: A banner was given to that king by the pleased Śambhu, and the king was told graciously by that God of gods: ॥64॥
4.13.65: Let the banner be tied up in the morning, O king; it will fall at night when my prājāpatya is thus completed, and so again each day. ॥65॥
4.13.66: Otherwise this banner of mine will stay fixed even at night. Having said this, Śambhu, the treasure of compassion, pleased with the king, vanished. ॥66॥
4.13.67: With the words so be it, this became the rule of that king, O great sage: the prājāpatya was performed daily according to the procedure of Śiva-worship. ॥67॥
4.13.68: The banner would rise of itself in the morning and fall in the evening, if the rite here had been completed. ॥68॥
4.13.69: Once, here, the rite of the baṭu was done first, and that banner fell even without the feeding of the brāhmaṇas. ॥69॥
4.13.70: Seeing that, the king then asked the learned men there: The brāhmaṇas are still eating here, yet the banner has not stayed up — ॥70॥
4.13.71: how has it fallen here? O brāhmaṇas, tell truthfully. Thus asked, the brāhmaṇas, best of the learned, then spoke: ॥71॥
4.13.72: O great king, at the brāhmaṇa-feast a baṭuka, Caṇḍī's son, was fed first; Śiva was pleased, and therefore the banner fell. ॥72॥
4.13.73: Hearing that, the king and all the other people there were amazed, and then they gave praise. ॥73॥
4.13.74: Thus their glory was increased by Śaṅkara; hence the baṭukas are proclaimed the best by those who know ancient lore. ॥74॥
4.13.75: The Śiva-worship should first be concluded (removed) by them, not otherwise; others have no entitlement here, by Śiva's command. ॥75॥
4.13.76: The concluding removal (uttāraṇa) must be done with the words, may the worship be complete; this alone is their task, and nothing else. ॥76॥
4.13.77: All this which was asked has been narrated, O lords of sages; hearing it, a man indeed obtains the fruit of Śiva-worship. ॥77॥
4.13.iti: Thus ends the thirteenth adhyāya, named The origin of the baṭukas, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥13॥
4.14.1: The sages said: Now tell us the greatness of the Jyotirliṅgas, and likewise their origin; tell everything just as you have heard it. ॥1॥
4.14.2: Sūta said: Listen, O brahmins; I shall tell their greatness and likewise their origin, briefly and according to my understanding, as I heard it from my true teacher. ॥2॥
4.14.3: The greatness of these cannot be told even in hundreds of years, O best of sages; nevertheless I shall tell it to you. ॥3॥
4.14.4: Among them Somanātha is proclaimed the first. Listen attentively first to its greatness, O sage. ॥4॥
4.14.5: Twenty-seven daughters, beginning with Aśvinī, were given to the Moon by the great-souled Dakṣa, O lords of sages. ॥5॥
4.14.6: Having obtained the Moon as their husband they shone especially; and the Moon too, having obtained them, shone constantly. ॥6॥
4.14.7: A gem shines through gold, and gold through a gem. Now hear what happened at that time. ॥7॥
4.14.8: Among all the wives, the one called Rohiṇī was dear to him as no other ever was. ॥8॥
4.14.9: The others, falling into sorrow, went to their father for refuge; having gone, they told him their grief as it was. ॥9॥
4.14.10: Hearing this, Dakṣa too was then grieved; O brahmins, coming to the Moon he then spoke words calmly. ॥10॥
4.14.11: Dakṣa said: O treasure of digits (kalānidhi), you were born in a spotless family; why then is there partiality, more and less, in you toward all who depend on you? ॥11॥
4.14.12: If it has been done, it is done; but it should not be done by you again. Conduct marked by unevenness is declared to lead to hell. ॥12॥
4.14.13: Sūta said: Having thus personally entreated the Moon, his son-in-law, Dakṣa went to his own home, fully resolved. ॥13॥
4.14.14: But the Moon, deluded, did not act on his word, through the power of Śiva's Māyā, by which the world is deluded. ॥14॥
4.14.15: When good is destined for someone, good indeed comes to him; and when ill is destined, how can good come to him? ॥15॥
4.14.16: The Moon, under the sway of powerful destiny, did not heed that word; attached to Rohiṇī, he never regarded any other. ॥16॥
4.14.17: Hearing that, Dakṣa, skilled as his name says, came again himself, full of grief, and entreated the Moon with good counsel. ॥17॥
4.14.18: Dakṣa said: Listen, O Moon: since you did not honour what I asked of you earlier in many ways, therefore become subject to waning. ॥18॥
4.14.19: Sūta said: When he had said this, the Moon at once became wasting; and as the Moon dwindled, there arose a great cry of distress. ॥19॥
4.14.20: Then all the gods and sages, thinking, what is to be done? Alas, how will it be? fell into grief and became distraught, O sage. ॥20॥
4.14.21: Informed by the Moon, all the gods headed by Indra and the sages headed by Vasiṣṭha went to Brahmā for refuge. ॥21॥
4.14.22: Having gone there, the sages and gods, greatly distressed, bowed to Brahmā, praised him, and told him the whole affair, O sage. ॥22॥
4.14.23: Brahmā too, hearing their words, was greatly amazed; extolling Śiva's Māyā, he spoke to them, making them hear. ॥23॥
4.14.24: Brahmā said: Alas, a great calamity has occurred, bringing sorrow to the whole world. The Moon was always wicked, and Dakṣa has cursed him. ॥24॥
4.14.25: All kinds of deeds have been done many times by the wicked Moon. Hear, O sages and gods, the Moon's former doing. ॥25॥
4.14.26: Going to Bṛhaspati's house, the wicked one carried off Tārā, his wife; and then he betook himself to the Daityas. ॥26॥
4.14.27: Taking refuge with the Daityas, he then waged war with the gods. Restrained by me and by Atri, the Moon (śaśin) gave Tārā back to him. ॥27॥
4.14.28: Seeing her pregnant, he (Bṛhaspati) said, I will not take her. Dissuaded by us, Jīva then reluctantly took her back. ॥28॥
4.14.29: He said again, if she gives up the embryo here, I will take her. Then, when I had made her give up the embryo there, O best of sages— ॥29॥
4.14.30: —when asked whose this embryo was, she said, Soma's. Afterwards she was taken back by him, Bṛhaspati, dissuaded by me. ॥30॥
4.14.31: Many such misdeeds of the Moon are told; why recount them again? How is it that he still acts so even today? ॥31॥
4.14.32: What has happened has rightly happened; it surely cannot be otherwise. Now I shall tell you a remedy; listen with attention. ॥32॥
4.14.33: Let the Moon go with the gods to the auspicious holy field of Prabhāsa, and there worship Śiva according to the Mṛtyuñjaya rite. ॥33॥
4.14.34: Placing the Lord before him there, let the Moon perform austerities constantly; then Śiva, pleased, will make him free from waning. ॥34॥
4.14.35: Sūta said: Hearing these words of Brahmā, all those gods and sages returned and then came to where Dakṣa and the Moon were. ॥35॥
4.14.36: Then the gods, taking the Moon and reassuring Dakṣa, and all the sages, went to Prabhāsa and there performed— ॥36॥
4.14.37: —having invoked the best of sacred waters, Sarasvatī and the rest, worship with an earthen liṅga according to the Mṛtyuñjaya rite. ॥37॥
4.14.38: Then all those gods and the pure-minded sages, having established the Moon at Prabhāsa, joyfully went each to his own abode. ॥38॥
4.14.39: The Moon performed austerities continuously for six months, and the bull-bannered Śiva was worshipped with the Mṛtyuñjaya mantra. ॥39॥
4.14.40: Having repeated that mantra ten crore times and meditating on the Mṛtyuñjaya mantra, the Moon remained with an unwavering mind. ॥40॥
4.14.41: Having seen him, the god Śaṅkara, the Lord, became pleased. Then, appearing before him, the one who is affectionate to his devotees spoke to the Moon, his own devotee. ॥41॥
4.14.42: Śaṅkara said: Choose a boon — may good be with you — whatever is desired by your mind. I am pleased, O Moon; I will grant everything, a boon unsurpassed. ॥42॥
4.14.43: Candra said: If you are pleased, O Lord of the gods, what could be unattainable for me? Even so, O Śaṅkara, ward off the waning of my body. ॥43॥
4.14.44: And may my offence be forgiven; do me good always. When this had been said by him, Śiva then spoke these words. ॥44॥
4.14.45: Śiva said: In one fortnight, O Candra, let your digit wane day by day; and in the other fortnight let that digit grow again continuously. ॥45॥
4.14.46: Sūta said: When it was so, the gods, their minds overflowing with joy, and likewise all the sages, came together quickly, O brahmins. ॥46॥
4.14.47: Having come, they all then pronounced blessings upon Candra; bowing to Śiva and joining their palms, they prayed to him with reverence. ॥47॥
4.14.48: The gods said: O God of gods, Mahādeva, Supreme Lord, salutations to you. Together with Umā, O Śambhu, O Master, remain here firmly. ॥48॥
4.14.49: Sūta said: Then Śaṅkara, who had earlier been praised by Candra with true devotion, the Lord who is formless, became endowed with form once more. ॥49॥
4.14.50: And being pleased, for the sake of the glory of the holy site for the gods and for Candra's fame, Śaṅkara there, by the name of Candra, ॥50॥
4.14.51: became renowned in the three worlds by the name Someśvara, the destroyer, through his worship, of diseases such as consumption and leprosy, O brahmins. ॥51॥
4.14.52: Blessed is he, fulfilled is he Candra, by whose name Śaṅkara himself, the Lord of the worlds, abides there, purifying the surface of the earth. ॥52॥
4.14.53: That pool was established right there by all those gods; and there, moreover, it remains never separated from Śiva and Brahmā. ॥53॥
4.14.54: It is famed on earth as Candrakuṇḍa, the destroyer of sins. The man who bathes there is freed from all sins. ॥54॥
4.14.55: All diseases, beginning with consumption, which are indeed incurable — they all go to destruction merely by bathing there for six months. ॥55॥
4.14.56: And having circumambulated Prabhāsa, the pure-souled one obtains the merit that comes from going around the whole earth; when he dies he is honoured in heaven. ॥56॥
4.14.57: Having seen the Soma-liṅga, a man is freed from all sin; having obtained the fruit his mind desires, when he dies he attains heaven. ॥57॥
4.14.58: Whatever fruit one aims at when performing the pilgrimage to this excellent tīrtha, that very fruit he obtains in every way; there is no doubt about this. ॥58॥
4.14.59: Thus those sages and gods, having seen such a fruit, joyfully bowed to Śiva and, taking with them the Moon, now free from waning, ॥59॥
4.14.60: and having circumambulated that tīrtha, they departed, praising it. And Candra too took up again his own ancient task. ॥60॥
4.14.61: Thus the whole origin of Someśa has been related. In this way the Someśvara liṅga came into being, O lords of sages. ॥61॥
4.14.62: The man who hears of its origin, or causes others to hear it, obtains all his desires and is freed from all sins. ॥62॥
4.14.iti: Thus ends the fourteenth adhyāya, named The origin of the Somanātha jyotirliṅga, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥14॥
4.15.1: Sūta said: After this I shall relate the origin of Mallikārjuna, on hearing which a devoted and wise person is freed from all sins. ॥1॥
4.15.2: What was told before, that I tell again: the divine story of Kumāra, which destroys all sins. ॥2॥
4.15.3: When Kumāra, the son of Śivā, the mighty foe of Tāraka, having gone round the earth, came back to Kailāsa, ॥3॥
4.15.4: then the divine sage Nārada came and told him the whole affair—the marriage of the lord of the gaṇas Gaṇeśa and the rest—misleading him by his own cunning. ॥4॥
4.15.5: Hearing that, Kumāra bowed to his two parents and went to the Krauñca mountain, even though restrained by them. ॥5॥
4.15.6: When his mother Girijā was grieved by separation from Kumāra, then Śambhu, who gives good understanding, spoke to her: ॥6॥
4.15.7: Why are you sad, beloved? Do not grieve, Pārvatī. Your son will come back, O fair-browed one; let this intense sorrow be abandoned. ॥7॥
4.15.8: When Pārvatī, deeply grieved, did not accept that, then Śaṅkara sent the divine sages there. ॥8॥
4.15.9: All the gods and sages, together with the gaṇas, joyful and wise, went there to bring back Kumāra. ॥9॥
4.15.10: Going there, they all bowed deeply to Kumāra and, having appealed to him in many ways, made their request with respect. ॥10॥
4.15.11: But Kumāra, the venerable one, overcome by great pride, did not accept that request of the gods and others, though it was filled with Śiva's command. ॥11॥
4.15.12: Then they all returned to Śiva, bowed, and having received Śaṅkara's command, went each to his own abode. ॥12॥
4.15.13: Then, as he did not come, the goddess Girijā felt the pain of separation from her son, and Śambhu too fell into great sorrow. ॥13॥
4.15.14: Then the two, very grieved and dejected, following worldly custom, went out of great affection to where their son was staying. ॥14॥
4.15.15: That son, called Kumāra, learning of his parents' arrival at the mountain, went far away—three yojanas—out of lack of affection. ॥15॥
4.15.16: When their son had gone far from the Krauñca mountain, the two settled there, assuming the form of light. ॥16॥
4.15.17: Afflicted by love for their son, Śiva and Śivā go on each parva day to see their own son Kumāra. ॥17॥
4.15.18: On the new-moon day Śambhu himself goes there; on the full-moon day Pārvatī certainly goes there. ॥18॥
4.15.19: From that day onward, the unique liṅga of Śiva called Mallikārjuna became famous in the three worlds. ॥19॥
4.15.20: Whoever beholds that liṅga is freed even from all sins—there is no doubt of this—and would obtain all his desires. ॥20॥
4.15.21: Sorrow departs far away and he gains supreme bliss; he never again undergoes the suffering born of a mother's womb. ॥21॥
4.15.22: Abundance of wealth and grain, renown and health, and the attainment of desired fruits arise—there is no doubt of this. ॥22॥
4.15.23: Thus has been told the second jyotirliṅga, named Mallika, which by its sight bestows every happiness; it was narrated for the good of the world. ॥23॥
4.15.iti: Thus ends the fifteenth adhyāya, named The second jyotirliṅga, named Mallikārjuna, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivapurāṇa. ॥15॥
4.16.1: The sages said: O Sūta, through the grace of Vyāsa you know every matter. Having heard the story of the Jyotis the jyotirliṅgas, we do not feel satisfied at all. ॥1॥
4.16.2: Therefore, O lord, showing us incomparable kindness in particular, tell us now about the third jyotirliṅga. ॥2॥
4.16.3: Sūta said: I am blessed, I have fulfilled my purpose, since I have come into the company of you illustrious ones, O brahmins. Blessed indeed is the company of the good. ॥3॥
4.16.4: Therefore, considering it my good fortune, I shall tell the purifying, divine story that destroys sins; listen with reverence. ॥4॥
4.16.5: There is the lovely city of Avantī, which grants liberation to all embodied beings; dear to Śiva, supremely holy, it purifies the world. ॥5॥
4.16.6: There lived an excellent brahmin, devoted to auspicious rites, a student of the Vedas, always engaged in Vedic rituals. ॥6॥
4.16.7: Having established the sacred fires and ever devoted to Śiva's worship, the brahmin worshipped an earthen image of Śiva every day. ॥7॥
4.16.8: Having obtained the fruit of all his rites, the brahmin Vedapriya, ever devoted to true knowledge, attained the goal of the good. ॥8॥
4.16.9: His four sons were like him, excellent sages, always devoted to Śiva's worship and never inferior to their parents. ॥9॥
4.16.10: Devapriya was the eldest of them, Priyamedhas came next, the third was named Sukṛta, and the fourth Dharmavāhī, of good vows. ॥10॥
4.16.11: Through the power of their merit, happiness grew on earth, just as the moon waxes continually in the bright fortnight. ॥11॥
4.16.12: So too their virtues, bringing happiness, kept increasing there, and that city then became filled with brahminical splendour. ॥12॥
4.16.13: Meanwhile, hear, O best of brahmins, the excellent event that happened there; I shall tell it as I have heard it. ॥13॥
4.16.14: On the mountain Ratnamāla there was a great asura named Dūṣaṇa, a mighty king of the Daityas, ceaselessly hostile to dharma. ॥14॥
4.16.15: By the boon granted by Brahmā he treated the world as worthless; the gods were defeated by him and likewise driven from their abodes. ॥15॥
4.16.16: On earth the Vedic and Smṛti duties were entirely shattered by that wicked one, just as hares are by a lion. ॥16॥
4.16.17: As many Vedic observances as there were, all were driven far away; at every sacred ford and holy site dharma was likewise taken far away. ॥17॥
4.16.18: Only the lovely city of Avantī is still seen there with dharma intact; having reflected thus, hear what he then did. ॥18॥
4.16.19: That great asura Dūṣaṇa, accompanied by a large army, came there, aiming at all the brahmins living there. ॥19॥
4.16.20: Having arrived there, that lord of the Daityas, the great villain and enemy of brahmins, summoned four excellent Daityas and spoke these words. ॥20॥
4.16.21: The demon said: Why do these wicked brahmins not obey my command? Devoted as they are to Vedic dharma, all of them deserve punishment in my view. ॥21॥
4.16.22: All the gods and kings in the world have been defeated by me; can the brahmins not be brought under control, O best of Daityas? ॥22॥
4.16.23: If they wish to live, then let them abandon the dharma of Śiva and the supreme dharma of the Vedas and become partakers of happiness. ॥23॥
4.16.24: Otherwise their lives will be in danger. This I have spoken truly; carry it out without hesitation. ॥24॥
4.16.25: Sūta said: Having resolved thus, those four Daityas then appeared in the four directions like fires, as at the dissolution of old. ॥25॥
4.16.26: Then those brahmins, hearing of the Daityas' undertaking, felt no distress there, being absorbed in meditation on Śiva. ॥26॥
4.16.27: Resorting to firmness, those brahmins did not move even a hair's breadth from their supreme meditation. What are those wretches before Śiva? ॥27॥
4.16.28: Meanwhile the fair city was overrun by them, and the people, tormented by them, came to the brahmins. ॥28॥
4.16.29: The people said: O masters, what should be done? The wicked ones have arrived; many people have been harmed, and they have come near. ॥29॥
4.16.30: Sūta said: Hearing these words of theirs, those sons of Vedapriya, ever trusting in Śaṅkara, spoke to those brahmins. ॥30॥
4.16.31: The brahmins said: Listen: we have no strength to frighten the wicked, nor are there weapons by which they might be turned back. ॥31॥
4.16.32: Here our humiliation would be the humiliation of even an ordinary protector; how much more, then, will it be that of the all-powerful Śiva? ॥32॥
4.16.33: May the Lord Śiva protect us today from fear of the asuras; there is no other refuge in the world than Śiva, loving to his devotees. ॥33॥
4.16.34: Sūta said: Thus resolving on firmness, and having duly worshipped the earthen liṅga, those brahmins remained absorbed in meditation. Just then those brahmins were seen by the Daitya with his army. ॥34॥
4.16.35: Dūṣaṇa uttered the words, let them be killed, let them be slain. But those words spoken by the Daitya were not heard at all by the brahmins, the sons of Vedapriya, intent on the path of meditation on Śambhu. ॥35॥
4.16.36: Then, just as that evil-minded one wished to kill those brahmins, at that very moment a pit opened with a loud sound at the place of the earthen liṅga. ॥36॥
4.16.37: From that pit arose Śiva, bearing a fearsome form, renowned as Mahākāla, slayer of the wicked and refuge of the good. ॥37॥
4.16.38: I, Mahākāla, have arisen for the destruction of wicked ones like you. You villain, go far away from the presence of the brahmins. ॥38॥
4.16.39: Having said this, Mahākāla Śaṅkara then swiftly reduced Dūṣaṇa together with his army to ashes with a mere roar of huṃ. ॥39॥
4.16.40: Part of the army was slain by him, part of the army fled; and Dūṣaṇa was killed here by Śiva, the Supreme Self. ॥40॥
4.16.41: Just as darkness goes to destruction everywhere on seeing the sun, so too, on seeing Śiva, that army of the demon perished. ॥41॥
4.16.42: The drums of the gods resounded and a shower of flowers fell. All the gods, Hari, Brahmā and the others, likewise assembled. ॥42॥
4.16.43: Having bowed with devotion to that god Śaṅkara, who brings welfare to the world, the Brahmins, with palms joined, praised him with various hymns. ॥43॥
4.16.44: Having comforted the Brahmins, Śiva himself, Mahākāla, the great Lord, being very pleased, said: Ask for a boon. ॥44॥
4.16.45: Hearing that, all those Brahmins then, with palms joined, bowing deeply to Śiva with devotion, spoke with heads bent low. ॥45॥
4.16.46: The brahmins said: O Mahākāla, O Mahādeva, O Lord who punishes the wicked, O Śambhu, O Śiva, grant us liberation from the ocean of worldly existence. ॥46॥
4.16.47: O Śiva, you must remain right here for the protection of the world. O Śambhu, O Lord, always deliver the people who behold you. ॥47॥
4.16.48: Sūta said: Thus addressed by them, Śiva remained there in that very beautiful pit, for the protection of his devotees, having granted them the good destination. ॥48॥
4.16.49: Those Brahmins attained liberation; and then the abode of Śiva, who is in the form of the liṅga, extended for a krośa in the four directions. ॥49॥
4.16.50: Śiva became famous on earth by the name Mahākāleśvara. O Brahmins, one who has seen him will not suffer even the slightest sorrow, even in a dream. ॥50॥
4.16.51: Whoever worships that liṅga with whatever desire in mind obtains that very desire, and also gains liberation in the hereafter. ॥51॥
4.16.52: O you of good vows, all this has been related: the origin and the glory of Mahākāla. What else do you wish to hear? ॥52॥
4.16.iti: Thus ends the sixteenth adhyāya, named The greatness of the Mahākāla jyotirliṅga, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥16॥
4.17.1: The sages said: O greatly wise one, tell us again the greatness of the jyotirliṅga bearing the name Mahākāla, the protector of its devotees. ॥1॥
4.17.2: Sūta said: O Brāhmaṇas, listen attentively to the greatness of the Mahākāla liṅga, which brings about the protection of devotees and increases devotion. ॥2॥
4.17.3: In Ujjayinī there was a great king named Candrasena, who knew the true meaning of all the scriptures, a devotee of Śiva, with senses subdued. ॥3॥
4.17.4: O twice-born ones, that king had a friend, the gaṇa Maṇibhadra, a chief among the gaṇas of Girīśa, honoured by all the worlds. ॥4॥
4.17.5: Once that lord of gaṇas, the generous-minded Maṇibhadra, with a pleased face, gave him a great jewel, the Cintāmaṇi. ॥5॥
4.17.6: That jewel, shining like the Kaustubha and resembling the sun, surely bestows auspiciousness whether it is meditated upon, seen, or even heard of. ॥6॥
4.17.7: Bronze, copper, iron, tin, stone and the like, or anything else touched by the surface of its radiance, quickly becomes gold. ॥7॥
4.17.8: Wearing the Cintāmaṇi on his neck, King Candrasena, who had taken refuge in Śiva, shone exceedingly, like the sun in the midst of the gods. ॥8॥
4.17.9: Hearing that Candrasena, the best of kings, wore the Cintāmaṇi on his neck, all the kings of the earth became agitated at heart with greed. ॥9॥
4.17.10: All the jealous, foolish kings begged Candrasena by various means for that jewel obtained from a divine being. ॥10॥
4.17.11: O Brāhmaṇas, the request of all the kings was rendered futile by that Candrasena, a firm devotee of Mahākāla. ॥11॥
4.17.12: Thus slighted by King Candrasena, all those kings of all the lands then became enraged. ॥12॥
4.17.13: Then all those kings, equipped with fourfold armies, became ready, it is said, to conquer Candrasena in battle. ॥13॥
4.17.14: All of them, having assembled and made a mutual agreement on signals, with many soldiers besieged the four gates of Ujjayinī. ॥14॥
4.17.15: Seeing his own city being besieged by all the kings, the king went for refuge to that very Mahākāleśvara. ॥15॥
4.17.16: Free of doubt, fasting, firm in resolve, with mind fixed on nothing else, that king worshipped Mahākāla day and night. ॥16॥
4.17.17: Then the blessed Śambhu Mahākāla, pleased in mind, devised a means to protect him; hear it attentively. ॥17॥
4.17.18: At that very time, O Brāhmaṇas, a certain cowherd woman wandering in that best of cities came with her child near Mahākāla. ॥18॥
4.17.19: Carrying a boy five years of age, she, a widow, watched with reverence the worship of Mahākāla performed by the king. ॥19॥
4.17.20: Having seen that most wondrous worship of Śiva performed by him, she bowed down and returned again to her own camp. ॥20॥
4.17.21: The cowherdess's son, having seen all this completely, out of curiosity set his mind on performing that worship of Śiva. ॥21॥
4.17.22: Bringing a pleasing stone, he with devotion set it up as a Śiva-liṅga in an empty spot within the camp, not far from his own dwelling. ॥22॥
4.17.23: Having established it, he worshipped it with fragrances, ornaments and garments, with incense, lamps, unbroken rice and the like, and also prepared a food offering with make-believe substances. ॥23॥
4.17.24: Worshipping again and again with lovely leaves and flowers, and performing various dances, he bowed down repeatedly. ॥24॥
4.17.25: At this time, that cowherd woman affectionately called her son, whose good mind was absorbed in Śiva, to have his meal. ॥25॥
4.17.26: When the boy, his mind steeped in Śiva's worship, did not want food even though called many times, then the mother went there. ॥26॥
4.17.27: Seeing him seated before Śiva with eyes closed, she seized his hand, dragged him, and struck him in anger. ॥27॥
4.17.28: When her son, though dragged and beaten, still did not come, she destroyed that worship, throwing the liṅga far away. ॥28॥
4.17.29: Scolding her son, who was crying out alas, alas in distress, the cowherd woman, filled with anger, went back into her house. ॥29॥
4.17.30: Seeing the worship of the trident-bearing god destroyed by his mother, the boy cried out, O God of gods, and fell down. ॥30॥
4.17.31: Overwhelmed by grief, he suddenly lost consciousness; regaining consciousness after a moment, he opened his eyes. ॥31॥
4.17.32: At that very moment, by Śiva's grace, the child soon saw there a beautiful shrine of Mahākāla that had come into being. ॥32॥
4.17.33: It had a large golden door, an excellent arched gateway with doors, and was resplendent with a platform of precious, flawless blue diamonds. ॥33॥
4.17.34: It was furnished with many wonderful pitchers of refined gold, with brilliantly shining jewelled pillars and floors inlaid with crystal. ॥34॥
4.17.35: In its midst the cowherdess's son saw the jewelled liṅga of Śaṅkara, the treasury of compassion, along with the worship he himself had offered. ॥35॥
4.17.36: Seeing it, the child rose up at once, amazed in mind, and was as though immersed in an ocean of supreme bliss. ॥36॥
4.17.37: Then, having praised Giriśa and bowed again and again, the boy left the temple of Śiva when the sun had set. ॥37॥
4.17.38: Then he saw his own dwelling, resembling the city of Purandara (Indra), instantly turned to gold, wonderful and supremely radiant. ॥38॥
4.17.39: Rejoicing, at nightfall he entered the house, endowed with every splendour and strewn with masses of jewels and gold. ॥39॥
4.17.40: There he saw his mother sleeping, bearing divine marks, her limbs shining with jewelled ornaments, like a very celestial maiden. ॥40॥
4.17.41: Then, O brahmins, that son, a recipient of Śiva's grace, overwhelmed with joy, quickly raised his mother up. ॥41॥
4.17.42: Having risen and beheld the marvel, she found everything as though never seen before; deeply immersed in great bliss, she embraced that son of hers. ॥42॥
4.17.43: Having heard from her son's mouth all about the grace of Girijā's lord, she informed the king, who worships Śiva unceasingly. ॥43॥
4.17.44: That king, having completed his observance, came at once in the night and saw the power of the cowherdess's son, which had pleased Śiva. ॥44॥
4.17.45: Having seen all that, the king, together with his ministers and priest, was plunged, beside himself, into an ocean of supreme bliss. ॥45॥
4.17.46: That king Candrasena, shedding tears out of love and joyfully uttering Śiva's name, embraced that boy. ॥46॥
4.17.47: O twice-born ones, a wondrous great festival arose there, and all, overwhelmed with joy, sang the praises of Maheśa. ॥47॥
4.17.48: Thus, owing to the most wondrous happenings, the sight of Śiva's greatness, and the excitement of the citizens, that night passed like a moment. ॥48॥
4.17.49: Then at dawn the kings, who were stationed besieging the city for battle, heard of that event from the mouths of their spies. ॥49॥
4.17.50: Hearing that, all those kings who had come there, having assembled and being greatly astonished, spoke thus to one another. ॥50॥
4.17.51: The kings said: This king Candrasena is a devotee of Śiva, very hard to conquer, the unperturbed lord of Ujjayinī, the city of Mahākāla. ॥51॥
4.17.52: He in whose city even such children are devoted to Śiva's vows — that king Candrasena is truly a great servant of Śaṅkara. ॥52॥
4.17.53: Surely, by opposing him, Śiva will become angry, and from that anger we shall all be destroyed. ॥53॥
4.17.54: Therefore peace must certainly be made with this king; when that is done, Maheśāna will show supreme compassion. ॥54॥
4.17.55: Sūta said: Having resolved thus, those kings gave up their enmity and became well-intentioned; all of them were well pleased and laid down the weapons and missiles in their hands. ॥55॥
4.17.56: Those kings entered the lovely city of Mahākāla and, with Candrasena's approval, worshipped Mahākāla. ॥56॥
4.17.57: Then those kings went to the house of the cowherd woman, all praising her good fortune and divine exaltation. ॥57॥
4.17.58: There they were received and honoured by Candrasena, who came forward to meet them; seated on very costly seats, greatly amazed, they rejoiced in return. ॥58॥
4.17.59: Seeing the Śiva temple that had appeared through the grace of the cowherd's son, and the Śiva-liṅga, they fixed their minds supremely on Śiva. ॥59॥
4.17.60: Then all those kings, pleased and seeking Śiva's grace, gave many things to that cowherd boy. ॥60॥
4.17.61: All the kings made him alone the king of all the cowherds who dwell in great numbers in every land. ॥61॥
4.17.62: Meanwhile, the radiant Hanumān, lord of the monkeys, worshipped by all the gods, appeared. ॥62॥
4.17.63: At his very arrival those kings, filled with excitement, rose up and bowed, their bodies bent low in devotion. ॥63॥
4.17.64: Seated among them and honoured, the lord of the monkeys embraced the cowherd's son and, looking at the kings, said this. ॥64॥
4.17.65: Hanumān said: Let all of you listen — blessings upon you — you kings and all embodied beings: apart from Śiva there is no other refuge for embodied beings. ॥65॥
4.17.66: Thus, by good fortune, this cowherd's son, having watched the worship of Śiva and having worshipped Śiva even without mantras, has attained Śiva. ॥66॥
4.17.67: This foremost devotee of Śambhu, who enhances the fame of the cowherds, will enjoy all pleasures here and in the end attain liberation. ॥67॥
4.17.68: In his lineage, the eighth descendant will be the greatly renowned one named Nanda; Kṛṣṇa, Nārāyaṇa himself, will become his son. ॥68॥
4.17.69: From today onward in this world, this cowherd boy will attain great worldwide fame under the name Śrīkara. ॥69॥
4.17.70: Sūta said: Having spoken thus, Añjanī's son, the lord of monkeys, a form of Śiva, looked upon all the kings and Candrasena with a compassionate gaze. ॥70॥
4.17.71: Then, with great affection, he taught that wise cowherd's son Śrīkara the Śaiva discipline dear to Śiva. ॥71॥
4.17.72: Then, O brahmins, Hanumān, well pleased, having blessed Candrasena and Śrīkara, vanished right there while all looked on. ॥72॥
4.17.73: And all the kings, delighted and honoured in return, took leave of him and of Candrasena and went back as they had come. ॥73॥
4.17.74: Śrīkara too, of great splendour, instructed by Hanumān, performed the worship of Śambhu together with brahmins versed in dharma. ॥74॥
4.17.75: The great king Candrasena and the cowherd boy Śrīkara both worshipped Mahākāla with supreme love. ॥75॥
4.17.76: In time, that Śrīkara and King Candrasena, having fully worshipped Mahākāla, attained the supreme state. ॥76॥
4.17.77: Such is the Mahākāla Śiva-liṅga, the refuge of the good; Śaṅkara, ever the slayer of the wicked, is loving towards his devotees. ॥77॥
4.17.78: This narrative has been told — purifying, supremely secret, bestowing all happiness, leading to heaven, and increasing devotion to Śiva. ॥78॥
4.17.iti: Thus ends the seventeenth adhyāya, named The greatness of the Mahākāla jyotirliṅga, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥17॥
4.18.1: The sages said: O Sūta, O Sūta, most fortunate one, you have indeed narrated to us the wondrous story of the liṅga called Mahākāla, the protector of his own devotees. ॥1॥
4.18.2: And now, O best of the learned, kindly tell us about the fourth jyotirliṅga, that of the Supreme Lord at Oṃkāra, the remover of all sins. ॥2॥
4.18.3: Sūta said: O twice-born ones, I shall gladly tell you how the liṅga named Parameśa came to be at Oṃkāra. Listen, O great sages. ॥3॥
4.18.4: Once, at a certain time, the venerable sage Nārada, full of supreme devotion, went to Śiva named Gokarṇa and worshipped him there. ॥4॥
4.18.5: Then that best of sages came to Vindhya, lord of mountains; there he was worshipped by him with great honour. ॥5॥
4.18.6: Adopting the attitude, everything exists in me; nothing is ever lacking, he stood before Nārada. ॥6॥
4.18.7: Then Nārada, the destroyer of pride, having heard that pride of his, sighed and stood there. Hearing the sigh, Vindhya said this: ॥7॥
4.18.8: Vindhya said: What deficiency have you seen in me, the cause of your sighing? Hearing that, the great sage Nārada spoke these words: ॥8॥
4.18.9: Nārada said: Everything indeed exists in you, yet Meru is higher. He has a share even among the gods; you never have that. ॥9॥
4.18.10: Sūta said: Having said this, Nārada left that place as he had come. And Vindhya was deeply distressed: Fie upon my life and all else! ॥10॥
4.18.11: I shall worship Śambhu, the Lord of the universe, and perform austerities. Resolving thus in his mind, he took refuge in Śaṅkara. ॥11॥
4.18.12: Joyfully he went to the place where Oṅkāra himself is, and there he made an earthen image of Śiva. ॥12॥
4.18.13: Then, worshipping Śambhu continuously for six months, intent on meditation upon Śiva, he did not move from the place of his austerity. ॥13॥
4.18.14: Seeing Vindhya's austerity thus, the Lord of Pārvatī was pleased and revealed his own form, which is hard to attain even for yogins. ॥14॥
4.18.15: Pleased, he then said: Tell me what your mind desires. I am pleased with your austerity; I am the giver of what devotees desire. ॥15॥
4.18.16: Vindhya said: If you are pleased, O Lord of gods, grant me the understanding I desire, one that accomplishes my own purpose, O Śambhu; you are ever affectionate to your devotees. ॥16॥
4.18.17: Sūta said: Hearing that, the blessed Śambhu pondered long in his heart: This dull-witted Vindhya wants a boon that will cause distress to others. ॥17॥
4.18.18: What shall I do so that this gift of a boon to him becomes auspicious, so that a boon given by me does not bring suffering to others? ॥18॥
4.18.19: Sūta said: Nevertheless Śambhu granted him that excellent boon: O Vindhya, king of mountains, do as you wish. ॥19॥
4.18.20: At that time the gods and the pure-minded sages, having worshipped Śaṅkara, said: You must remain here. ॥20॥
4.18.21: Hearing the words of the gods, the Supreme Lord was pleased and gladly did just so, for the happiness of the worlds. ॥21॥
4.18.22: The single liṅga that was Oṅkāra became twofold: in the praṇava form that Sadāśiva came to be named Oṅkāra, ॥22॥
4.18.23: and that which arose in the earthen image became Parameśvara. O twice-born ones, both grant devotees their desires and bestow enjoyment and liberation. ॥23॥
4.18.24: Then the gods and likewise the sages performed their worship, and, having pleased the bull-bannered Śiva, they obtained many boons. ॥24॥
4.18.25: The gods went each to his own abode, and Vindhya too, greatly delighted, accomplished his own purpose and gave up his distress, O twice-born ones. ॥25॥
4.18.26: Whoever worships Śambhu thus will not dwell again in a mother's womb, and will obtain whatever fruit he desires; there is no doubt about this. ॥26॥
4.18.27: Sūta said: I have told you all this, the fruit connected with the origin of Oṅkāra. Next I shall describe the excellent liṅga Kedāra. ॥27॥
4.18.iti: Thus ends the eighteenth adhyāya, named The greatness of the Oṅkāreśvara jyotirliṅga, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥18॥
4.19.1: Sūta said: O twice-born ones, the two incarnations of Hari known as Nara and Nārāyaṇa performed austerities in the Bhārata region, at the Badarī hermitage itself. ॥1॥
4.19.2: Entreated by those two to be present for worship in an earthen liṅga, Śambhu, Śiva, comes every day into that liṅga, because he is subject to his devotees. ॥2॥
4.19.3: While those two incarnations of Viṣṇu, the Śaiva sons of Dharma, were thus worshipping Śambhu, a long time passed. ॥3॥
4.19.4: At one time there, the Supreme Lord, pleased, replied: I am pleased; let a boon be chosen from me. ॥4॥
4.19.5: When he had said this, Nara and Nārāyaṇa themselves then spoke there, desiring the welfare of the worlds. ॥5॥
4.19.6: Nara and Nārāyaṇa said: O Lord of gods, if you are pleased, if a boon is to be given by you, then, O Śaṅkara, remain here yourself in your own form for the sake of worship. ॥6॥
4.19.7: Sūta said: Thus addressed by the two, Śaṅkara, the Great Lord, himself then took his stand at Kedāra in the Himālaya, in the form of light. ॥7॥
4.19.8: And worshipped by those two, he who removes all sorrow and fear remained there for the benefit of the worlds and so that devotees might see him. ॥8॥
4.19.9: Śambhu then stood there himself, bearing the name Kedāreśvara, ever granting the desires of devotees through being seen and worshipped. ॥9॥
4.19.10: The gods and the ancient sages worship him here; each of them obtains the fruit desired by the mind from the well-pleased Maheśvara. ॥10॥
4.19.11: Those dwelling at the Badarī hermitage obtain it by constantly worshipping Bhava, since he always grants the desires of devotees. ॥11॥
4.19.12: From that day onward, for one by whom Kedāreśvara has been worshipped with devotion, sorrow is hard to find even in a dream. ॥12॥
4.19.13: He who, on seeing the Pāṇḍavas, assumed the form of a buffalo and, resorting to his māyā, set about fleeing right there, ॥13॥
4.19.14: and was caught there by the Pāṇḍavas, remaining with face turned downward; his tail was held by them, and he was entreated again and again. ॥14॥
4.19.15: He, bearing the name affectionate to devotees, remained there in that form; the head portion went to Nepal and abides there in that form. ॥15॥
4.19.16: Likewise he gave the command for daily worship; and Śambhu himself, being worshipped, remained there and bestowed boons. ॥16॥
4.19.17: Having worshipped him, the Pāṇḍavas then departed joyfully, having obtained all that their hearts desired, freed from all sorrow. ॥17॥
4.19.18: There, in the sacred field called Kedāra, Hara is directly present always, and is likewise worshipped by the people of Bhārata. ॥18॥
4.19.19: He who, dear to Hara, offers a bracelet there near the form of Hara — that bracelet endowed with Hara's form — ॥19॥
4.19.20: and likewise, having seen the form, is released from all sins. He too who has gone to the Badarī forest becomes liberated while living. ॥20॥
4.19.21: Having seen the form of Nara, and likewise of Nārāyaṇa, and of Śambhu as Kedāreśvara, one becomes a partaker of liberation; there is no doubt. ॥21॥
4.19.22: Those devotees of Kedāreśa who die while on the road to him — they too certainly become liberated; no deliberation is needed on this. ॥22॥
4.19.23: Having gone there full of love, having worshipped Kedāreśa and drunk the water there, one does not obtain rebirth. ॥23॥
4.19.24: O Brahmins, in this Bhārata region Kedāreśa, the Lord of Nara and Nārāyaṇa, is to be worshipped by all beings with great devotion. ॥24॥
4.19.25: Though he is the Lord of all, he is especially the master of this region — Śambhu named Kedāra, the granter of all desires; there is no doubt. ॥25॥
4.19.26: O best of sages, this account which you asked about has been narrated; on hearing it one would remove all sin; no deliberation is needed on this. ॥26॥
4.19.iti: Thus ends the nineteenth adhyāya, named The greatness of the Kedāreśvara jyotirliṅga, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥19॥
4.20.1: Sūta said: After this I shall relate the greatness of Bhaimaśaṅkara (Bhīmaśaṅkara), by merely hearing which a man obtains everything he desires. ॥1॥
4.20.2: In the land called Kāmarūpa, Śaṅkara, out of desire for the welfare of the world, descended himself in person — he who is the vessel of auspiciousness and happiness. ॥2॥
4.20.3: Listen attentively, O lords of sages; I shall tell you why that Śaṅkara, the benefactor of the worlds, descended. ॥3॥
4.20.4: Long ago, O brahmins, there was a rākṣasa named Bhīma, of great valour, who caused suffering to all beings and was always destroying dharma. ॥4॥
4.20.5: Very mighty, he was born of Kumbhakarṇa in Karkaṭī, and he lived with his mother on the Sahya mountain. ॥5॥
4.20.6: When Kumbhakarṇa, the terror of the worlds, had been slain by Rāma, the rākṣasī remained by herself on the Sahya with her son. ॥6॥
4.20.7: One day, O brahmins, that boy Bhīma — wicked, a tormentor of the world, of fearsome prowess — questioned his mother Karkaṭī. ॥7॥
4.20.8: Bhīma said: Mother, who is my father, and where is he? Why do you live alone? I wish to know all this; tell me truly now. ॥8॥
4.20.9: Sūta said: Asked thus by her son, that wicked rākṣasī said to him: Listen, I shall tell you. ॥9॥
4.20.10: Karkaṭī said: Your father was Kumbhakarṇa, the younger brother of Rāvaṇa. That mighty one was killed by Rāma together with his brother. ॥10॥
4.20.11: Once, dear son, that rākṣasa Kumbhakarṇa came here and, being strong, enjoyed me by force long ago. ॥11॥
4.20.12: That mighty one went to Laṅkā, leaving me right here. I have never seen that Laṅkā; I live here alone. ॥12॥
4.20.13: My father was named Karkaṭa, and my mother is known as Puṣkasī. My husband was Virādha, who was slain by Rāma earlier. ॥13॥
4.20.14: When my dear husband was slain, I stayed by my parents' side; and my parents died here, burnt to ashes by a sage. ॥14॥
4.20.15: They had gone there to devour him, and were burnt then by the enraged, great-souled Sutīkṣṇa, rich in austerity, the disciple of Agastya. ॥15॥
4.20.16: So I became alone and grief-stricken, and I lived on the mountain, afflicted with sorrow, without support or shelter. ॥16॥
4.20.17: At that time the rākṣasa, Rāvaṇa's younger brother, came here and united with me; then he left me and went away. ॥17॥
4.20.18: Then you were born, of great strength and valour; and relying on you, I pass my time. ॥18॥
4.20.19: Sūta said: Hearing these words of hers, Bhīma of terrible prowess grew angry and reflected: What shall I do against Hari? ॥19॥
4.20.20: By him my father was slain, and likewise my maternal grandparents; Virādha too was killed by him — great sorrow has he caused. ॥20॥
4.20.21: If I am truly his son, I shall torment that Hari. Having so resolved, Bhīma went off to perform great austerity. ॥21॥
4.20.22: Directing himself to Brahmā, resorting to meditation with his mind, he then performed great austerity for a thousand years. ॥22॥
4.20.23: With arms raised, standing on one foot, fixing his gaze on the sun, Bhīma, the rākṣasa's son, remained thus. ॥23॥
4.20.24: From his head arose an extremely fierce radiance; scorched by it, the gods then went to Brahmā for refuge. ॥24॥
4.20.25: Bowing to the Creator with devotion, they praised him with various hymns; and they, along with Vāsava (Indra), made known their distress to Brahmā. ॥25॥
4.20.26: The gods said: O Brahmā, the radiance of the rākṣasa is set to torment the worlds. Whatever boon the wicked one asks for, grant it, O Ordainer. ॥26॥
4.20.27: Otherwise, burnt today by his intense radiance, we shall all go to destruction; therefore grant him what he asks. ॥27॥
4.20.28: Sūta said: Hearing their words, Brahmā, grandsire of the worlds, went to grant the boon and spoke these words: ॥28॥
4.20.29: Brahmā said: I am pleased; ask for the boon that is in your mind. Hearing this speech of the Ordainer, that rākṣasa spoke. ॥29॥
4.20.30: Bhīma said: If you are pleased, O lord of gods, and if a boon is to be given by you, then grant me today incomparable strength, O lotus-seated one. ॥30॥
4.20.31: Sūta said: Having said this, that rākṣasa bowed to Brahmā; and Brahmā, having granted him the boon, then returned to his abode. ॥31॥
4.20.32: The rākṣasa Bhīma, having obtained immense strength from Brahmā, came home, quickly bowed to his mother, and arrogantly said: ॥32॥
4.20.33: Bhīma said: Behold my strength now, mother. I shall bring great destruction upon the gods headed by Śakra, and upon Hari, their helper. ॥33॥
4.20.34: Sūta said: Having said this, Bhīma of terrible prowess first conquered the gods along with Vāsava, and drove them out of their respective abodes. ॥34॥
4.20.35: Then he defeated in battle Hari, who had been entreated for help by the gods; thereafter the daitya gleefully began to conquer the earth. ॥35॥
4.20.36: First he went there to conquer Sudakṣiṇa, the mighty lord of Kāmarūpa; then a fearful battle took place with him. ॥36॥
4.20.37: Then the asura Bhīma, by Brahmā's power — by the potency of the boon — defeated that great king, a mighty hero who had taken refuge in Śiva. ॥37॥
4.20.38: Having then conquered that mighty lord of Kāmarūpa, Bhīma of terrible prowess bound and beat him. ॥38॥
4.20.39: O brahmins, all the possessions of that king, the servant of Śiva — his kingdom with all its equipment — were seized by that wicked Bhīma. ॥39॥
4.20.40: And the king — most righteous, a lover of dharma, dear to Hara — was seized by him in fetters and placed in a solitary place. ॥40॥
4.20.41: There, at that time, having made an excellent earthen image of Śiva, he began the worship of Śiva alone, out of desire to please him. ॥41॥
4.20.42: Then he praised the Gaṅgā in many ways; and having performed mental bathing and the other rites, he performed the worship of Śaṅkara. ॥42॥
4.20.43: The best of kings performed it by the procedure for the earthen liṅga; and having duly done the meditation on him as it should be, ॥43॥
4.20.44: and having done all that with prostrations and hymns, preceded by mudrās and postures, he worshipped Śaṅkara with joy. ॥44॥
4.20.45: He repeated the five-syllabled mantra joined with the Praṇava (Oṃ); he then found no opportunity to do any other work. ॥45॥
4.20.46: His wife too, the chaste lady renowned by the name Dakṣiṇā, the king's beloved, lovingly performed the earthen liṅga rite. ॥46॥
4.20.47: The couple, with one mind, constantly worshipped there Śaṅkara, who brings welfare to devotees, both devoted to the adoration of Śiva. ॥47॥
4.20.48: The demon, deluded by pride in his boon, abolished all sacrificial rites and the like, saying, let it be given to me. ॥48॥
4.20.49: Accompanied by a great army of wicked demons, he brought the whole earth under his control, O best of sages. ॥49॥
4.20.50: Abolishing all the dharma of the Vedas, of the śāstras, of the smṛtis and that born of the Purāṇas, the mighty one enjoyed everything himself. ॥50॥
4.20.51: The gods with Śakra (Indra) and likewise the sages were oppressed by him; they fell into extreme misery, and the Brahmins were driven out of the world. ॥51॥
4.20.52: Then all of them, distressed, gods and sages together with Vāsava, placing Brahmā and Viṣṇu at their head, went to Śaṅkara for refuge. ॥52॥
4.20.53: Praising with many hymns Śaṅkara, the benefactor of the worlds, they pleased him on the auspicious bank of the Mahākośī. ॥53॥
4.20.54: Having made an earthen image and worshipped it according to rule, they praised him in due order with various hymns, salutations and so on. ॥54॥
4.20.55: Thus praised then by the gods' hymns and the like, Śambhu became exceedingly pleased and said this to those gods. ॥55॥
4.20.56: Śiva said: O Hari, O Vidhi (Brahmā), O gods and all you sages, I am pleased. Ask for a boon: what task shall I do for you? ॥56॥
4.20.57: Sūta said: When these words had been spoken thus by Śiva, O Brahmins, the gods bowed deeply, joined their palms, and then spoke to Śiva. ॥57॥
4.20.58: The gods said: O Lord of gods, you know everything that lies in the minds of all; you are the inner controller of all; nothing is unknown to you. ॥58॥
4.20.59: Nevertheless, O Lord, let it be heard: at your command we tell our own sorrow. O Mahādeva, look on us with a compassionate glance. ॥59॥
4.20.60: The mighty demon, son of Karkaṭī, born of Kumbhakarṇa, empowered by the boon given by Brahmā, oppresses the gods incessantly. ॥60॥
4.20.61: Slay this demon named Bhīma, the giver of sorrow. Show mercy, O Maheśāna; do not delay, O Lord. ॥61॥
4.20.62: Sūta said: Thus addressed by all the gods, Śambhu, affectionate to his devotees, said, I shall bring about his death, and then spoke to the gods. ॥62॥
4.20.63: Śambhu said: The king, lord of Kāmarūpa, is my excellent devotee. Tell him this, O gods: the task will soon be accomplished. ॥63॥
4.20.64: Say: O Sudakṣiṇa, great king, lord of Kāmarūpa, master, you are especially my devotee; perform my worship with love. ॥64॥
4.20.65: I shall slay the wicked Daitya named Bhīma, empowered by the boon obtained from Brahmā, who has insulted you; there is no doubt. ॥65॥
4.20.66: Sūta said: Then all those immortals, filled with joy, went there and told that great king what Śambhu had said. ॥66॥
4.20.67: Having spoken thus to him, the gods attained supreme bliss, and all those great sages quickly went to their own hermitages. ॥67॥
4.20.iti: Thus ends the twentieth adhyāya, named The troubles caused by the demon Bhīma, in the Bhīmeśvara Jyotirliṅga Māhātmya, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥20॥
4.21.1: Sūta said: Śiva too, together with his gaṇas, went there out of a wish for his devotee's welfare; hidden, he stood near his own devotee, attentively, in order to protect him. ॥1॥
4.21.2: Meanwhile, there, the lord of Kāmarūpa then began an intense meditation in front of the earthen liṅga. ॥2॥
4.21.3: Someone went there and reported to the rākṣasa: The king is doing something like this — a hostile rite (ābhicārika) aimed at you. ॥3॥
4.21.4: Sūta said: Hearing that, the rākṣasa grew angry and, wishing to kill him, seized a sword and went toward the king. ॥4॥
4.21.5: Seeing there what was set up — the earthen liṅga and the rest — and observing its form and its purpose, the rākṣasa thought: This man is up to something. ॥5॥
4.21.6: Therefore I shall kill this king today by force, together with his ritual implements. Having reflected thus, the rākṣasa, furious, spoke to the king. ॥6॥
4.21.7: Bhīma said: Hey, hey, king, wicked soul, what are you doing now? Tell the truth and I will not kill you; otherwise I will certainly kill you. ॥7॥
4.21.8: Sūta said: Hearing his words, the lord of Kāmarūpa, filled with faith in Śiva, quickly reflected thus in his mind: ॥8॥
4.21.9: What is destined will surely happen; there is nothing to turn it back. Here everything depends on prārabdha (destiny already set in motion), and that prārabdha is declared to be Śiva himself. ॥9॥
4.21.10: The compassionate Śaṅkara is surely present here in the earthen liṅga. Will he not act here for my sake? Who then is this rākṣasa, and from where could he harm me? ॥10॥
4.21.11: He will surely make true his own promise, befitting himself; for it is heard in the Veda that the Lord Śiva is true to his vow. ॥11॥
4.21.12: His vow is: Whenever someone exceedingly cruel torments my devotee, I then kill that wicked one to protect the devotee; there is no doubt. ॥12॥
4.21.13: Thus taking hold of courage and meditating on the god Śaṅkara, the lord of the earth prayed with true devotion, in his mind alone: ॥13॥
4.21.14: I am yours, O great king; do as you wish. I am about to speak the truth here — do what is good for me. ॥14॥
4.21.15: Having meditated thus in his mind, the king, bound by the noose of truth, spoke truthful words, scorning the rākṣasa. ॥15॥
4.21.16: The king said: I worship the god Śaṅkara, protector of his devotees, lord of all moving and unmoving beings, the changeless one. ॥16॥
4.21.17: Sūta said: Hearing these words of the lord of Kāmarūpa, Bhīma, his limbs trembling with rage, spoke: ॥17॥
4.21.18: Bhīma said: I know your Śaṅkara. What will he do to me — he who was installed by my own paternal uncle like a servant? ॥18॥
4.21.19: Relying on his strength you hope to conquer me? Then you have conquered everything — no need to think about it. ॥19॥
4.21.20: As long as Śaṅkara, your protector, has not been seen by me, only so long do you serve him, deeming him your master — not otherwise at all. ॥20॥
4.21.21: Once I have seen him, O king, all that will become entirely clear. So keep this form of Śiva far away. ॥21॥
4.21.22: Otherwise, there will be danger for you today, no doubt. I, of terrible valour, will deal your master a sharp blow (lit. hand). ॥22॥
4.21.23: Sūta said: Hearing those words, King Kāmarūpeśvara, firm in his faith in Śaṅkara, quickly replied to him: ॥23॥
4.21.24: The king said: Lowly and faulty though I am, I will never abandon Śaṅkara; and my master, supreme above all, never abandons me. ॥24॥
4.21.25: Sūta said: Hearing these words of that king devoted to Śiva, the rākṣasa Bhīma laughed at him and quickly said to the king: ॥25॥
4.21.26: Bhīma said: He is an intoxicated one who constantly goes begging — does he even know his own form? And what commitment do yogins have to protecting devotees? ॥26॥
4.21.27: Make up your mind to this and stand completely aside; I and that master of yours will fight it out. ॥27॥
4.21.28: Sūta said: Addressed thus, that best of kings, a devotee of Śambhu firm in his vow, fearlessly replied to Bhīma, who was ever a source of misery to the worlds: ॥28॥
4.21.29: The king said: Listen, wicked rākṣasa: I cannot do what you ask. If anything is to be changed, let it be done by you — though whence do you have such power? ॥29॥
4.21.30: Sūta said: Addressed thus, he gathered his army, reviled the king, and then hurled his dreadful sword at the earthen liṅga. ॥30॥
4.21.31: Now behold this very day your master's might that brings joy to his devotees; so the mighty one said, laughing, together with the rākṣasas. ॥31॥
4.21.32: O brāhmaṇas, even before the sword touched the earthen liṅga, Hara himself manifested from that earthen liṅga. ॥32॥
4.21.33: Śiva said: Behold, I am Bhīmeśvara, manifested for protection. This is my vow of old: my devotee is always to be protected by me. ॥33॥
4.21.34: Therefore behold quickly my might that brings joy to devotees. Having said this, he split the sword in two with his Pināka. ॥34॥
4.21.35: Then the rākṣasa hurled his own trident; that trident of the wicked one too was shattered into a hundred pieces by Śambhu. ॥35॥
4.21.36: Again, O brāhmaṇas, he hurled a spear (śakti) at Śambhu; that too Śambhu swiftly cut into a hundred thousand pieces with his arrows. ॥36॥
4.21.37: Then he hurled a paṭṭiśa (sharp-edged spear) at Śiva; Śiva with his trident instantly cut it into pieces as small as sesame seeds. ॥37॥
4.21.38: Then a terrible battle took place between Śiva's gaṇas and the rākṣasas, bringing distress to those who watched. ॥38॥
4.21.39: Then in an instant the whole earth was thrown into turmoil, and all the oceans, together with the mountains, were agitated. ॥39॥
4.21.40: All the gods and sages became greatly distressed and said to one another: Śiva has been entreated in vain. ॥40॥
4.21.41: Nārada also came up to Śaṅkara, the consumer of sorrow, and right there, with joined palms and bowed head, entreated him. ॥41॥
4.21.42: Nārada said: Forgive, forgive, O Lord, O causer of bewilderment. What need is there of an axe for grass? Let them be slain quickly indeed. ॥42॥
4.21.43: Thus entreated, Lord Śambhu then reduced all the hosts of demons to ashes with the mere weapon of his roar huṃ. ॥43॥
4.21.44: O sage, all those demons were burnt up by Śaṅkara in a moment, swiftly, there, while all the gods looked on. ॥44॥
4.21.45: Just as fire turned into a forest blaze would burn up a forest, so the enraged Śiva burnt up the army of the demons in an instant. ॥45॥
4.21.46: And as for Bhīma himself, what became of his ashes was not known to anyone then. Burnt along with his retinue, his very name is heard nowhere. ॥46॥
4.21.47: Then, by Śiva's grace, the lords of sages attained peace, as did all the gods headed by Śakra, and the whole world regained well-being. ॥47॥
4.21.48: The flame of Maheśa's wrath spread forth from forest to forest, and those ashes of the demons pervaded the entire forest. ॥48॥
4.21.49: Then herbs sprang up that accomplish various purposes; through them men may attain a different form and likewise a different appearance. ॥49॥
4.21.50: Bhūtas, pretas, piśācas and the like would flee far away from them. There is no task, O brāhmaṇas, that is not accomplished through them. ॥50॥
4.21.51: Śambhu was entreated by those gods, and especially by the sages: The Lord should remain here for the happiness of the worlds. ॥51॥
4.21.52: This region is indeed a vile one, causing distress to the people of Ayodhyā; but now, by seeing you, welfare will come about. ॥52॥
4.21.53: You shall be known by the name Bhīmaśaṅkara, the accomplisher of all. This liṅga is ever to be worshipped, the warder-off of all calamities. ॥53॥
4.21.54: Sūta said: Thus entreated, Śambhu, the benefactor of the worlds, independent and loving toward his devotees, gladly remained right there. ॥54॥
4.21.iti: Thus ends the twenty-first adhyāya, named The origin of the Bhīmeśvara jyotirliṅga and its greatness, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥21॥
4.22.1: Sūta said: Next I shall tell you — listen, O best of sages — the greatness of Viśveśvara, which destroys the great sins. ॥1॥
4.22.2: Whatever is seen here in the world, as a mere object, is in truth of the nature of consciousness and bliss, changeless and eternal. ॥2॥
4.22.3: In him alone, who delights in absolute oneness, there then arose the desire for a second. He himself became endowed with attributes and is called Śiva. ॥3॥
4.22.4: He indeed became twofold, through the distinction of male and female forms. The male is known as Śiva; the female is called Śakti. ॥4॥
4.22.5: By those two, whose nature is consciousness and bliss, two persons were also created — ॥5॥
4.22.6: — by those two who were then unseen, spontaneously, O best of sages. Then those two, not seeing their own mother and father, O brahmins, ॥6॥
4.22.7: — those two, Prakṛti and Puruṣa, fell into great doubt. Then a voice arose from the attributeless Supreme Self: Austerity must be performed; from it will come the most excellent creation. ॥7॥
4.22.8: Prakṛti and Puruṣa said: But there is no place for austerity. Where now, O Lord, should we two stay and perform austerity at your command, O Śiva? ॥8॥
4.22.9: Then, the essence of radiance, auspicious, measuring five krośas, a beautiful city furnished with all requisites — ॥9॥
4.22.10: — having been fashioned, was sent as his own by the attributeless Śiva; and it stood in the sky near the Puruṣa. ॥10॥
4.22.11: Then, occupying it, Hari, with the desire for creation, performed austerity for a long time, resorting to meditation on him. ॥11॥
4.22.12: From the exertion, various streams of water then arose; that void was pervaded by them, and nothing else was seen. ॥12॥
4.22.13: Then Viṣṇu looked: What is this wonder that is seen? Seeing this marvel, he shook his head. ॥13॥
4.22.14: Then a jewel fell from his ear in front of the Lord; that became the great tīrtha named Maṇikarṇikā. ॥14॥
4.22.15: When that Pañcakrośī was being swept away in the flood of waters, it was then swiftly held up by the attributeless Śiva on his trident. ॥15॥
4.22.16: Viṣṇu slept right there with Prakṛti, his consort. From his navel-lotus Brahmā was born at Śaṅkara's command. ॥16॥
4.22.17: Having received Śiva's command, he then made a wondrous creation, in which fourteen worlds were fashioned within the cosmic egg. ॥17॥
4.22.18: The extent of the cosmic egg has been declared by the sages to measure fifty crores of yojanas. ॥18॥
4.22.19: How will beings in the cosmic egg, bound by karma, attain me again? Reflecting thus, Śiva kept the Pañcakrośī separate. ॥19॥
4.22.20: And this is held to be the bestower of auspiciousness in the world, the destroyer of karma. Kāśī reveals liberation, grants knowledge, and is very dear to me. ॥20॥
4.22.21: The Avimukta liṅga has been installed by the Supreme Self himself. This holy field must never be abandoned by you, O portion of mine. ॥21॥
4.22.22: Having said this, Hara himself took Kāśikā down from his trident and released it into the world, into the realm of mortals. ॥22॥
4.22.23: Even at the end of Brahmā's day it certainly does not perish; then, O sages, Śiva holds it up on his trident. ॥23॥
4.22.24: And when creation is made again by Brahmā, it is set back in place, O brahmins. Because it drags away (karṣaṇa) karmas, it is called Kāśī. ॥24॥
4.22.25: The Avimukteśvara liṅga abides in Kāśī always, granting liberation to people, even to great sinners. ॥25॥
4.22.26: Elsewhere liberation such as sārūpya is attained, O lords of sages; here alone souls attain the supreme liberation of sāyujya. ॥26॥
4.22.27: For those who have no refuge anywhere, the city of Vārāṇasī is the refuge: the Pañcakrośī, most holy, destroyer of crores of killings. ॥27॥
4.22.28: All the immortals long for death here — what then of others? This city, ever dear to Śaṅkara, grants both enjoyment and liberation. ॥28॥
4.22.29: Brahmā praises it, and Viṣṇu, the Siddhas and yogins, the sages likewise, and other people dwelling in the three worlds, always. ॥29॥
4.22.30: I cannot describe the whole glory of Kāśī even in hundreds of years; therefore I speak as far as I am able. ॥30॥
4.22.31: He who is the lord of Kailāsa — sattva within, tamas without, renowned by the name Kālāgni, Bhava, attributeless yet possessed of attributes — with many prostrations spoke these words: ॥31॥
4.22.32: Rudra said: O Viśveśvara, O Maheśāna, I am yours, no doubt. Show grace, O Mahādeva, you who are with Ambā, to me, your son. ॥32॥
4.22.33: You should always remain right here, out of desire for the welfare of the worlds. Deliver them, O Lord of the world — I pray, O Master of the universe. ॥33॥
4.22.34: Sūta said: Avimukta too, self-controlled, having entreated him again and again and shedding tears, joyfully spoke to Śaṅkara. ॥34॥
4.22.35: Avimukta said: O God of gods, O Mahādeva, excellent remedy for the disease of time (death), you are truly the lord of the three worlds, to be served by Brahmā, Acyuta and others. ॥35॥
4.22.36: O God, let your capital be established by you in the city of Kāśī. I, absorbed in meditation, shall dwell here for the sake of inconceivable bliss. ॥36॥
4.22.37: You alone here are the giver of liberation and the granter of desires, no other. Therefore, for the world's benefit, remain here always together with Umā. ॥37॥
4.22.38: Carry all souls across the ocean of worldly existence, O Sadāśiva. Accomplish the purpose of your devotees, O Hara — I pray again and again. ॥38॥
4.22.39: Sūta said: Thus entreated by that Viśvanātha, Śaṅkara, the sovereign of all, stayed there too for the benefit of the worlds. ॥39॥
4.22.40: From the very day Hara came to Kāśī, from then on Kāśī became the most excellent of all. ॥40॥
4.22.iti: Thus ends the twenty-second adhyāya, named Rudra's coming to Kāśī, in the Viśveśvara Māhātmya, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥22॥
4.23.1: The sages said: O Sūta, if the great city Vārāṇasī is so holy, then tell us its power, and also that of Avimukta, O lord. ॥1॥
4.23.2: Sūta said: I shall tell you properly, in brief, the most splendid greatness of Vārāṇasī and of Viśveśvara; listen, O lords of sages. ॥2॥
4.23.3: Once the goddess Pārvatī, with supreme joy and out of concern for the world, asked Śaṅkara about the greatness of the two Avimuktas, the sacred field and its liṅga. ॥3॥
4.23.4: Pārvatī said: Please tell the greatness of this sacred field in full, showing kindness to me, out of a wish for the welfare of the worlds. ॥4॥
4.23.5: Sūta said: Hearing those words of the goddess, the god of gods, lord of the world, replied to Bhavānī for the good of living beings. ॥5॥
4.23.6: The Supreme Lord said: Well asked by you, O gracious one — a question auspicious and bringing happiness to the worlds. I shall truly tell you, as it is, the greatness of the two Avimuktas. ॥6॥
4.23.7: This Vārāṇasī is ever my most secret sacred field, in every way the cause of liberation for all beings. ॥7॥
4.23.8: In this field siddhas always dwell, having taken up my vow, bearing various emblems, constantly longing for my world. ॥8॥
4.23.9: Self-controlled and with senses subdued, they practise the great yoga, the supreme Vedic Pāśupata discipline, which yields the fruits of enjoyment and liberation. ॥9॥
4.23.10: Dwelling in Vārāṇasī always pleases me, O Maheśvarī, leaving all other places; hear for certain the reason why. ॥10॥
4.23.11: He who is my devotee and he who has true knowledge — both of them share in liberation. They have no need of holy places; for them what is enjoined and what is not enjoined are alike. ॥11॥
4.23.12: Those two should be known as liberated while living; wherever they die, they attain liberation at once — this is a definite word spoken by me. ॥12॥
4.23.13: There is something special about this supreme holy place called Avimukta; listen to it attentively, O goddess, O supreme Śakti. ॥13॥
4.23.14: All castes and all stages of life, the young, the youthful and the old — if they die in this city, they are liberated; there is no doubt. ॥14॥
4.23.15: Whether impure or pure, a maiden or a married woman, a widow or a barren woman, or one afflicted with menstrual impurity, ॥15॥
4.23.16: one who has just given birth, one without the sacraments — whatever kind she may be, O brahmins — if she dies in this field she partakes of liberation; there is no doubt here. ॥16॥
4.23.17: Whether sweat-born, egg-born, sprout-born or womb-born, a being that dies here attains liberation as nowhere else. ॥17॥
4.23.18: Here there is no need of knowledge, nor again of devotion; here, O goddess, there is no need of ritual action, nor indeed of charity. ॥18॥
4.23.19: Here there is no need of sacraments at all, never any need of meditation; likewise here there is no need of the divine name, of worship, or of noble birth. ॥19॥
4.23.20: Whatever man dwells in my liberation-giving field, if he dies in whatever way, he certainly attains liberation. ॥20॥
4.23.21: This divine city of mine, O beloved, is more secret than the secret; even Brahmā and the others do not know its greatness, O Pārvatī. ॥21॥
4.23.22: Therefore this great field is known as Avimukta; superior to all holy places such as Naimiṣa, it grants liberation upon death. ॥22॥
4.23.23: Truth is the secret essence of dharma, equanimity the secret essence of liberation; the wise know Avimukta as the secret essence of sacred fields and holy places. ॥23॥
4.23.24: Even while eating as he pleases, sleeping, playing and doing various acts, a being who gives up his life in Avimukta becomes fit for liberation. ॥24॥
4.23.25: For men, even having committed thousands of sins, the state of a piśāca in Kāśī is better — but not the fruit of a thousand sacrifices in heaven away from the city of Kāśī. ॥25॥
4.23.26: Therefore the city of Kāśī is resorted to with every effort, and Sadāśiva, the unmanifest liṅga, is meditated upon by the sages. ॥26॥
4.23.27: Whatever fruit men aim at when they perform austerities here, O beloved, that very fruit I surely grant them fully. ॥27॥
4.23.28: And afterwards I grant union with myself and the desired abode; for those who give up the body here there is no bondage of karma from any source. ॥28॥
4.23.29: Brahmā with the divine sages, Viṣṇu, and the Sun too, and all other great souls worship me here. ॥29॥
4.23.30: Even a man whose mind is attached to sense objects and who has lost his taste for dharma — if he dies in this field, he does not enter saṃsāra again. ॥30॥
4.23.31: How much more, then, those who are free of possessiveness, steadfast, established in sattva, free from hypocrisy, accomplished and without worldly undertakings — all of them are absorbed in me. ॥31॥
4.23.32: What a yogī might attain only after thousands of births, that supreme liberation he attains right here through death. ॥32॥
4.23.33: Here many liṅgas have been installed by devotees; here they grant all desires and liberation as well, O Pārvatī. ॥33॥
4.23.34: This field is declared to extend five krośas in the four directions; all around, likewise, it bestows immortality on a being at the time of death. ॥34॥
4.23.35: One who dies sinless attains liberation immediately; one who dies with sins undergoes a series of bodies. ॥35॥
4.23.36: Only after experiencing torment would he then attain liberation. He who commits a sin in this field called Avimukta, certainly, ॥36॥
4.23.37: undergoes the torment of Bhairava for ten thousand years, and then, having exhausted his sin, attains liberation, O beautiful one. ॥37॥
4.23.38: Thus I have described to you the destiny of those of sinful conduct. Knowing this, a man should properly serve Avimukta. ॥38॥
4.23.39: There is no destruction of deeds done, even in hundreds of crores of kalpas; karma done, good or bad, must inevitably be experienced. ॥39॥
4.23.40: Purely bad karma here leads to hell; good karma leads to heaven; from both together human birth is said to result. ॥40॥
4.23.41: Here in this world, birth is favourable or unfavourable according to the deficiency or excess of merit and demerit; and the destruction of both is liberation. This is truly so, O Pārvatī. ॥41॥
4.23.42: Karma is declared in the section on ritual action to be threefold, O Maheśvarī: the accumulated (sañcita), that being done (kriyamāṇa), and that which has begun to bear fruit (prārabdha); all cause bondage. ॥42॥
4.23.43: That which has arisen from previous births is called sañcita; that which is being experienced through the body is called prārabdha. ॥43॥
4.23.44: And the karma, auspicious or inauspicious, that is being done now in this birth, O Queen of the gods, the wise know as kriyamāṇa. ॥44॥
4.23.45: Prārabdha karma is destroyed only through being experienced, not otherwise; the destruction of the other two karmas comes by means such as worship. ॥45॥
4.23.46: There is no destruction of all karmas without the city of Kāśī. Every other holy place is easy to reach; the city of Kāśikā is hard to attain. ॥46॥
4.23.47: If the sight of Kāśī was obtained with reverence in a previous birth, then, having reached Kāśī, one attains death there, and not otherwise. ॥47॥
4.23.48: The man who, having reached Kāśī, bathes in the Gaṅgā—then there is destruction of his kriyamāṇa and also his sañcita karma. ॥48॥
4.23.49: It is firmly established that prārabdha does not perish without being experienced; when his death has occurred, then its destruction takes place. ॥49॥
4.23.50: If Kāśī has been visited earlier and afterwards one commits sin, then by that powerful seed he is led to Kāśī again. ॥50॥
4.23.51: Then all sins indeed turn to ashes. Therefore a man should resort to Kāśī, which surely uproots karma. ॥51॥
4.23.52: He by whom even a single brahmin has been settled to live in Kāśī, O beloved, himself obtains residence in Kāśī and thereby attains liberation. ॥52॥
4.23.53: He who dies in Kāśī has no birth again. And for one who dies at Prayāga with a specific intention, there is the fruit of that desire. ॥53॥
4.23.54: If there should be a conflict of the two, the fruit born of Kāśī non-rebirth would be in vain; and if that desired rebirth is not obtained, the fruit of the king of holy places Prayāga would be in vain. ॥54॥
4.23.55: Therefore, by my command, Viṣṇu directly fashions a new creation and surely grants the fulfilment of what was intended in the mind. ॥55॥
4.23.56: Sūta said: Such and more, O best of sages, is the great glory of Kāśī, and likewise of Viśveśvara, granting enjoyment and liberation to the good. ॥56॥
4.23.57: Next I shall relate the glory of Tryambaka, hearing which a man is freed from all sins in an instant. ॥57॥
4.23.iti: Thus ends the twenty-third adhyāya, named The greatness of the Kāśī Viśveśvara jyotirliṅga, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥23॥
4.24.1: Sūta said: Listen, O excellent sages, to a story that destroys sin; I shall tell it as I heard it from Vyāsa, my true teacher. ॥1॥
4.24.2: Long ago there was a renowned excellent sage named Gautama; his wife was named Ahalyā, supremely righteous. ॥2॥
4.24.3: In the southern direction is the mountain called Brahma giri; there he performed austerity for ten thousand years. ॥3॥
4.24.4: Once, O you of good vows, a terrible drought occurred there for a hundred years, and the people fell into misery. ॥4॥
4.24.5: Not even a moist leaf was seen on the face of the earth; how then could water, which sustains the life of beings, be seen? ॥5॥
4.24.6: Then the sages, men, cattle, birds and wild animals there went away in the ten directions. ॥6॥
4.24.7: Seeing that drought, some sages and brahmins, devoted to breath-control, passed that very terrible time in meditation. ॥7॥
4.24.8: Gautama himself also, devoted to breath-control, performed an auspicious austerity there for six months for the sake of Varuṇa. ॥8॥
4.24.9: Then Varuṇa came to grant him a boon and spoke these words: I am pleased; ask a boon and I shall give it. ॥9॥
4.24.10: Then Gautama asked him for rain; and then Varuṇa replied to the sage, O brahmins. ॥10॥
4.24.11: Varuṇa said: How could I, transgressing the command of God, bring that rain? Ask something else that I may do for you; you are wise. ॥11॥
4.24.12: Sūta said: Having heard these words of the great-souled Varuṇa, Gautama, benefactor of others, spoke. ॥12॥
4.24.13: Gautama said: If you are pleased, O lord of gods, if a boon is to be given to me, then what I ask today must be done by you accordingly. ॥13॥
4.24.14: Since you are the lord of the waters, give me water, O lord of all gods — inexhaustible, divine, and bestowing perpetual fruit. ॥14॥
4.24.15: Sūta said: Thus entreated by Gautama, Varuṇa said to him: Let a pit be dug by you. ॥15॥
4.24.16: When this was said, he dug a pit a hand's measure deep, and Varuṇa filled it with divine water. ॥16॥
4.24.17: Then the god Varuṇa, lord of waters, spoke to the sage Gautama, tiger among sages, rich in helping others. ॥17॥
4.24.18: Varuṇa said: May your water be inexhaustible and become a holy place (tīrtha), O great sage; it will be renowned on earth by your name. ॥18॥
4.24.19: Whatever is given here, offered in fire, performed as austerity, sacrifice made to the gods, and śrāddha done for the ancestors — all will become inexhaustible. ॥19॥
4.24.20: Sūta said: Having said this, the god, praised by that great seer, vanished; and the sage Gautama too attained happiness, having done a service to others. ॥20॥
4.24.21: Taking refuge with the great leads to greatness for men; the great perceive the true nature of that, not the other, inauspicious ones. ॥21॥
4.24.22: As is the man one serves, such is the fruit one reaps: by serving the great comes loftiness, and by serving the petty, pettiness. ॥22॥
4.24.23: Service in a lion's den is held to yield pearls; service in a jackal's den is known to yield bones. ॥23॥
4.24.24: This is the nature of the noble: inability to bear others' suffering. They consider it as their own suffering, and the other's suffering is warded off. ॥24॥
4.24.25: Trees, gold, sandalwood and sugarcane — these on earth are thus fit for others' benefit; no others are so. ॥25॥
4.24.26: The compassionate, one untouched by pride, the benefactor, and one who has conquered the senses — by these four pillars of merit the earth is upheld. ॥26॥
4.24.27: Then Gautama, having obtained that very rare water there, duly performed his daily and occasional rites. ॥27॥
4.24.28: Then the lord of sages had rice, barley and wild rice of many kinds sown right there for the fire-offerings. ॥28॥
4.24.29: Various grains, and likewise various trees, flowers and fruits, came to be there in abundance. ॥29॥
4.24.30: Hearing of that, other sages came there in thousands; cattle, birds and many other creatures also came. ॥30॥
