4.24.31: That forest became supremely beautiful in the whole sphere of the earth; through the presence of that inexhaustible water, the drought caused no distress. ॥31॥
4.24.32: Many sages too, devoted to auspicious deeds, took up residence in that forest, accompanied by their disciples, wives and sons. ॥32॥
4.24.33: They had grains sown to pass the time; and there was joy in that forest through the power of Gautama. ॥33॥
4.24.iti: Thus ends the twenty-fourth adhyāya, named The power of Gautama, in the Tryambakeśvara Māhātmya, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥24॥
4.25.1: Sūta said: Once, his own disciples, Brahmins with water-pots in their hands, were sent by Gautama for water, and they went there devotedly. ॥1॥
4.25.2: Seeing the disciples who had come near the water, the sages' wives, who had also come there in great numbers for water, stopped them. ॥2॥
4.25.3: We are the sages' wives; we shall draw water first. Keep away. The water is to be taken by you afterwards; thus they scolded them. ॥3॥
4.25.4: Turning back, they reported it to the sage's wife Ahalyā. She, taking them along and reassuring them, herself together with them— ॥4॥
4.25.5: the ascetic woman fetched the water and gave it to Gautama. With that water the best of sages carried out his daily rites. ॥5॥
4.25.6: Those sages' wives, angered, rebuked her in this way; then all of them, crooked-minded, turned back and went to their huts. ॥6॥
4.25.7: Then the whole incident was reported in a distorted way before their husbands by those evil-minded women. ॥7॥
4.25.8: Then, hearing their words, by the power of destined karma, those great sages became furious with Gautama. ॥8॥
4.25.9: In order to create an obstacle for Gautama, those enraged, ill-minded ones worshipped Gaṇeśa with various offerings of worship. ॥9॥
4.25.10: Then Gaṇeśvara, pleased, appeared, and there he who is subject to his devotees, the giver of fruits, spoke these words. ॥10॥
4.25.11: Gaṇeśa said: I am pleased. Tell me a boon — what shall I do for you? Hearing those words of his, the sages then said: ॥11॥
4.25.12: The sages said: If a boon is to be granted by you, then bring it about that Gautama, after being rebuked, is driven out of his own hermitage by the sages. ॥12॥
4.25.13: Sūta said: Thus entreated by them, the elephant-faced one, the refuge of the good, smiled and spoke again with affection, trying to enlighten them. ॥13॥
4.25.14: Gaṇeśa said: Listen, all you sages: what you are now doing is not proper. For those who are angry with him though he has committed no offence, there is only harm. ॥14॥
4.25.15: Causing pain to those who formerly rendered help is surely not beneficial; when pain is inflicted on them, ruin results here. ॥15॥
4.25.16: By performing such austerity a supreme fruit is attained; having yourselves cast away the auspicious fruit, one should not again pursue what is harmful. ॥16॥
4.25.17: Sūta said: Hearing these words of his, those best of sages, overcome then by delusion of mind, said only this: ॥17॥
4.25.18: The sages said: O lord, you must do exactly this and nothing else. Thus addressed, Lord Gaṇeśa then spoke these words: ॥18॥
4.25.19: Gaṇeśa said: The wicked never attains goodness, nor the good wickedness — this is declared by Brahmā and is certain. ॥19॥
4.25.20: When formerly you suffered distress from starvation, then happiness was given to you by the great sage Gautama. ॥20॥
4.25.21: Now pain is being given to him by you. This is by no means proper in the world; consider it carefully. ॥21॥
4.25.22: Deluded by the influence of your women, you will not heed my words. Yet this will turn out to be most beneficial for him, no doubt. ॥22॥
4.25.23: Again this best of sages will surely give you happiness. Driving him out would not be proper; choose another boon. ॥23॥
4.25.24: Sūta said: Although these words were spoken thus to the sages by the great-souled Gaṇeśa, they still did not accept them. ॥24॥
4.25.25: Then, out of his dependence on his devotees, Śiva's son spoke with an indifferent mind to those sages of wicked intellect. ॥25॥
4.25.26: Gaṇeśa said: What you request, I shall certainly do accordingly. What is to follow will surely happen. Having said this, he vanished again. ॥26॥
4.25.27: Gautama did not know the evil intent of the sages; with a joyful mind he continually performed his rites together with his wife. ॥27॥
4.25.28: O lords of sages, listen to the episode that occurred in the meantime through the effect of the boon, owing to the influence of those wicked sages. ॥28॥
4.25.29: In Gautama's field there were rice and barley. Gaṇeśa, becoming a feeble cow, went there, it is said. ॥29॥
4.25.30: Trembling, she went there and, by the force of that boon, devoured the rice and barley, O best of sages. ॥30॥
4.25.31: Meanwhile, by fate, Gautama arrived there; the compassionate one then tried to drive her away with a tuft of grass. ॥31॥
4.25.32: Touched by the tuft of grass, she fell to the ground and died at that very moment, as the sage looked on. ॥32॥
4.25.33: Those sages, in disguise, and likewise the inauspicious sages' wives, all said there then: What has Gautama done? ॥33॥
4.25.34: Gautama too, greatly astonished, called Ahalyā and, O Brahmins, spoke in sorrow with an anguished heart: ॥34॥
4.25.35: Gautama said: What has happened, O goddess, and how has the Supreme Lord become angry? What is to be done, where should we go? The sin of killing has befallen us. ॥35॥
4.25.36: Sūta said: Meanwhile the Brahmins reviled Gautama, and likewise the Brahmins' wives caused Ahalyā distress with harsh words. ॥36॥
4.25.37: Their evil-minded disciples and their sons likewise, reviling Gautama, repeatedly shouted words of reproach: ॥37॥
4.25.38: The sages said: Your face is not fit to be seen; go away, go away. On seeing the face of a cow-killer, one must at once bathe with one's clothes on. ॥38॥
4.25.39: As long as you remain in the hermitage, neither the gods who consume oblations nor the ancestors will accept anything offered by us. ॥39॥
4.25.40: Therefore go elsewhere with your household; make no delay, you cow-slayer, you sinner. ॥40॥
4.25.41: Sūta said: Having said this, they all struck him with stones, and they caused him great distress, and tormented Ahalyā too with harsh words. ॥41॥
4.25.42: Struck and reviled by the wicked ones, Gautama spoke these words: O sages, I am going away from here; I shall dwell elsewhere. ॥42॥
4.25.43: Having said this, Gautama then left that place, and having gone the distance of a krośa, he then made a hermitage there with their permission. ॥43॥
4.25.44: As long as the curse remains, so long nothing is to be done; there is no entitlement to any rite — divine, ancestral, or Vedic. ॥44॥
4.25.45: Then, having passed half a month, that excellent sage Gautama, afflicted by that sorrow, earnestly entreated the sages. ॥45॥
4.25.46: Gautama said: I am to be pitied by you; let it be told to me — it will be done by me. Let it be made known how my sin may go away. ॥46॥
4.25.47: Sūta said: Thus addressed, those Brāhmaṇas did not then speak to him; but being asked with great deference, they assembled and stood together in one place. ॥47॥
4.25.48: Gautama, standing at a distance and bowing to those best of sages, full of humility, asked: What indeed should be done by me now? ॥48॥
4.25.49: When this had been said by that great-souled sage Gautama, all those sages, assembled together, spoke these words. ॥49॥
4.25.50: The sages said: Without expiation, purity never arises. Therefore, for the purification of your body, perform an atonement. ॥50॥
4.25.51: Go around the whole earth three times, proclaiming your sin; and coming back right here, observe a month-long vow likewise. ॥51॥
4.25.52: And having likewise performed one hundred and one circumambulations of this Brahma mountain, your purification will come about. ॥52॥
4.25.53: Or else, having brought Gaṅgā here, perform a bath in the Gaṅgā; and likewise, having made a crore of earthen liṅgas, worship the god. ॥53॥
4.25.54: Then, having bathed in the Gaṅgā, you will be purified. But first perform ten and one (eleven) circumambulations of the mountain. ॥54॥
4.25.55: And having likewise bathed the earthen liṅga with a hundred pots of water, expiation would come about. Thus addressed by those sages, Gautama accepted their word and said, so be it, Oṃ. ॥55॥
4.25.56: O best of sages, by the command of your honoured selves, I shall perform here the worship of the earthen liṅgas and likewise the circumambulation of the mountain. ॥56॥
4.25.57: Having said this, that best of seers, the most excellent sage, performed the circumambulation of the mountain and, having fashioned earthen liṅgas, worshipped them. ॥57॥
4.25.58: Then the virtuous Ahalyā too did all that; and the disciples and the disciples' disciples then rendered service to the two of them. ॥58॥
4.25.iti: Thus ends the twenty-fifth adhyāya, named The ruling given to Gautama, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥25॥
4.26.1: Sūta said: O brahmins, when the sage together with his wife had done this, Śiva, pleased, then appeared together with Śivā and with his attendants (gaṇas). ॥1॥
4.26.2: Then the pleased one, with Śivā, the treasure-house of compassion, said: O great sage, ask for a boon; I am pleased with your fine devotion. ॥2॥
4.26.3: Then, having seen that beautiful form of the great-souled Śambhu, he bowed to Śaṅkara with devotion and, filled with joy, offered a hymn of praise. ॥3॥
4.26.4: Having praised him much and bowed to the Lord, he stood with joined palms; that Gautama said: O God, make me free of sin. ॥4॥
4.26.5: Sūta said: Having heard these words of the great-souled Gautama, Śiva became even more pleased and began to speak. ॥5॥
4.26.6: Śiva said: You are blessed, you have fulfilled your purpose, you are ever free of sin, O sage. You have indeed been deceived by these wicked, evil-minded men. ॥6॥
4.26.7: By the sight of you people indeed become free of sin; how then could you, ever devoted to me, be sinful? ॥7॥
4.26.8: O sage, those evil-souled ones by whom this harm was done to you—they themselves are sinful, of wicked conduct, and guilty of killing. ॥8॥
4.26.9: By seeing them, may others become most sinful. They have likewise become ungrateful; for them there is no atonement anywhere. ॥9॥
4.26.10: Sūta said: Having said this, O brahmins, Lord Śaṅkara—giver of good to the good and of punishment to the wicked—then told him at length of their misdeeds. ॥10॥
4.26.11: Having heard what Śarva said, the sage, his mind greatly astonished, bowed deeply to Śiva with devotion and, with joined palms, spoke again. ॥11॥
4.26.12: Gautama said: O Maheśāna, those sages have done me a great favour; had they not acted thus, how could I have gained the sight of you? ॥12॥
4.26.13: Blessed are those sages, by whom something most auspicious has been done for me; through their very misconduct a great good of my own has come about. ॥13॥
4.26.14: Sūta said: Hearing these words of his, Maheśvara, greatly pleased, looked at Gautama with a compassionate gaze and quickly replied. ॥14॥
4.26.15: Śiva said: O best of brahmins, you are a blessed sage, truly the most excellent of sages. Knowing me to be well pleased, choose an excellent boon. ॥15॥
4.26.16: Sūta said: Gautama too reflected thus: it is well known in the world that what has been decided cannot turn out otherwise; therefore one should act according to what has been declared. ॥16॥
4.26.17: Having resolved thus, Gautama, best of sages and devoted to Śiva, with joined palms and bowed head, spoke these words to Śaṅkara. ॥17॥
4.26.18: Gautama said: O Lord, you speak the truth; nevertheless, what has been determined by five people does not turn out otherwise. So here, let what has happened remain as it is. ॥18॥
4.26.19: If you are pleased, O Lord of gods, let Gaṅgā be given to me; do this good for the world. Salutations to you, salutations to you. ॥19॥
4.26.20: Sūta said: Having spoken these words, Gautama, desiring the good of the world, clasped the lotus feet of the Lord of gods and bowed to him. ॥20॥
4.26.21: Then Lord Śaṅkara drew forth the essence of earth and heaven which had been preserved from before— ॥21॥
4.26.22: —that little which had remained of what Brahmā had given at the wedding; Śambhu, loving to his devotees, gave it to the sage. ॥22॥
4.26.23: Then and there the Gaṅgā water took on a supreme female form; and the best of sages praised her and bowed to her. ॥23॥
4.26.24: Gautama said: You are blessed, you have fulfilled your purpose; the world has been purified by you. O Gaṅgā, purify me too, who am surely falling into hell. ॥24॥
4.26.25: Then Śambhu too, the benefactor of all, said: listen, O Gaṅgā: by my command, purify this Gautama. ॥25॥
4.26.26: Having heard these words of Śambhu and of Gautama, Gaṅgā—the purifying power of Śiva—spoke to Śiva. ॥26॥
4.26.27: Gaṅgā said: O Lord, having purified the sage together with his family, I shall go to my own abode; I speak the truth. ॥27॥
4.26.28: Sūta said: When Gaṅgā had said this there, Maheśa, loving to his devotees, for the benefit of the world spoke again to Gaṅgā. ॥28॥
4.26.29: Śiva said: You must stay right here until the Kali age arrives, the Kali age of the twenty-eighth cycle of Vaivasvata Manu, O goddess. ॥29॥
4.26.30: Sūta said: Having heard these words of her lord Śaṅkara, Gaṅgā, that purifying best of rivers, replied again. ॥30॥
4.26.31: Gaṅgā said: O lord Maheśvara, O destroyer of Tripura, if my glory is to be greater than that of all others, then I shall remain on earth. ॥31॥
4.26.32: And hear something more, O lord: you too, O Master, remain near me in a beautiful form, with your attendants and with Ambikā. ॥32॥
4.26.33: Sūta said: Having heard her words thus, Śaṅkara, loving to his devotees, for the benefit of the world spoke again to Gaṅgā. ॥33॥
4.26.34: Śiva said: You are blessed; listen, O Gaṅgā: I am not separate from you. Even so, I shall stay here, and you too should stay. ॥34॥
4.26.35: Sūta said: Having heard these words of the Supreme Lord, her master, Gaṅgā became glad at heart and worshipped him in return. ॥35॥
4.26.36: Meanwhile the gods, the ancient sages, and many holy tīrthas and various sacred sites— ॥36॥
4.26.37: —all came, crying Victory, victory! and reverently worshipped Gautama, Gaṅgā and Giriśa. ॥37॥
4.26.38: Then all those immortals, headed by Hari and Brahmā, with joined hands and bowed shoulders, joyfully offered praise to them. ॥38॥
4.26.39: Then the pleased Gaṅgā and Giriśa said to them: ask for a boon, O best of gods; we two will grant it out of desire to please you. ॥39॥
4.26.40: The gods said: If you are pleased, O Lord of gods, and you, O best of rivers, are pleased, then please stay here out of compassion, for our sake and likewise for the good of humankind. ॥40॥
4.26.41: Gaṅgā said: Why should you all not also stay here, for the sake of what is dear to everyone? Otherwise, after purifying Gautama, I shall go back the way I came. ॥41॥
4.26.42: O gods, how is my special distinction among you here to be known? If that is proven, then I shall stay without doubt. ॥42॥
4.26.43: They all said: When Jupiter (Guru), the best friend of all, is in the sign of Leo, then all of us will come here; there is no doubt. ॥43॥
4.26.44: For eleven years the sin of people here is washed off by us; in this way we become impure, O best of rivers. ॥44॥
4.26.45: To wash away that very impurity, O dear one, we shall certainly come into your presence, O great goddess; this truth is spoken with respect. ॥45॥
4.26.46: For the favour of the worlds and out of the wish to please us, Śaṅkara too, and you as well, should remain here, O best of rivers. ॥46॥
4.26.47: As long as Jupiter is in Leo, just so long shall we stay; bathing in you three times a day and beholding Śaṅkara, ॥47॥
4.26.48: having done these, we shall cast off all our sin, no doubt; and we shall go to our own regions by your command. ॥48॥
4.26.49: Sūta said: Thus entreated by them and by the great sage Gautama, Śaṅkara remained there with pleasure, and that best of rivers also remained. ॥49॥
4.26.50: That Gaṅgā became known by the name Gautamī, and the liṅga was called Tryambaka; it then became most renowned, the destroyer of great sins. ॥50॥
4.26.51: From that day onward, whenever Jupiter is in Leo, all the sacred fords, holy fields and deities come there. ॥51॥
4.26.52: Lakes such as Puṣkara, likewise rivers such as Gaṅgā, and gods such as Vāsudeva are present on the bank of the Gautamī. ॥52॥
4.26.53: As long as they remain there, for that long there is no fruit from them in their own places; only when they have returned to their own regions does their fruit arise. ॥53॥
4.26.54: This is declared the Jyotirliṅga renowned by the name Tryambaka, standing on the bank of the Gautamī, the destroyer of great sins. ॥54॥
4.26.55: Whoever with devotion beholds the Jyotirliṅga named Tryambaka, worships it, praises it and bows to it, is freed from all sins. ॥55॥
4.26.56: The Jyotirliṅga Tryambaka, worshipped by Gautama, grants all desires here and bestows supreme liberation in the hereafter. ॥56॥
4.26.57: Thus I have narrated to you what I was asked, O lords among sages. What else do you wish to hear? That I shall tell you, without doubt. ॥57॥
4.26.iti: Thus ends the twenty-sixth adhyāya, named The description of the glory of Tryambakeśvara, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥26॥
4.27.1: The sages said: How did Gaṅgā come into being in the form of water? Tell us, O lord. And from where did her greatness especially arise? Tell us, O lord. ॥1॥
4.27.2: And what then happened to those wicked brahmins by whom suffering was given to Gautama? Let it be told, O you who have Vyāsa as your true teacher. ॥2॥
4.27.3: Sūta said: Thus entreated by Gautama at that time, Gaṅgā herself, O brahmins, quickly descended from that mountain of Brahmā. ॥3॥
4.27.4: Her stream issued forth from a branch of an udumbara tree. There the renowned sage Gautama joyfully bathed. ॥4॥
4.27.5: Gautama's disciples and other great sages too gathered there and bathed full of joy. ॥5॥
4.27.6: Then that place became famous by the name Gaṅgādvāra, delightful and removing all sins by its mere sight, O best of sages. ॥6॥
4.27.7: Those sages who were Gautama's rivals also came there to bathe; seeing them, she quickly vanished. ॥7॥
4.27.8: Do not, do not, Gautama quickly cried out there, praising Gaṅgā again and again with folded hands and bowed head. ॥8॥
4.27.9: Gautama said: These men are blinded by the intoxication of prosperity; whether they are good or wicked, by the power of this merit of mine let your sight be granted to them by you. ॥9॥
4.27.10: Sūta said: Then a voice of Gaṅgā arose from the vault of the sky. Hear that excellent speech of Gaṅgā, O best of sages. ॥10॥
4.27.11: Gaṅgā said: These are most wicked, ungrateful, traitors to their master, base and heretical; they are always to be avoided from seeing me. ॥11॥
4.27.12: Gautama said: O Mother, let this be heard — these are indeed the words of the great. Therefore the Lord's word must be made true by you. ॥12॥
4.27.13: He in this world who does good to those who harm him, by him I am purified here: this is the word of the Lord. ॥13॥
4.27.14: Sūta said: Having heard these words of the great-souled sage Gautama, again a voice of Gaṅgā arose from the vault of the sky. ॥14॥
4.27.15: True and auspicious words are indeed spoken by you, O sage Gautama; even so, for the sake of their acceptance, let them perform expiation. ॥15॥
4.27.16: Here a hundred and one circumambulations of the mountain must be performed by these men, at your command, being especially subject to you. ॥16॥
4.27.17: And then the evil-doers will gain eligibility, especially for seeing me. I have spoken the truth, O sage. ॥17॥
4.27.18: Hearing her words, they all did so, humbly entreating Gautama: our offence should be forgiven. ॥18॥
4.27.19: When this was done, Gautama then, at her command, made a pool named Kuśāvarta, situated below Gaṅgādvāra. ॥19॥
4.27.20: Then she appeared there again for his pleasure, and Kuśāvarta became a famous, unsurpassed holy place (tīrtha). ॥20॥
4.27.21: Whoever bathes there becomes fit for liberation, at once casting off all sins and attaining rare knowledge. ॥21॥
4.27.22: Gautama and the other sages met with one another; and those who had formerly been ungrateful were then ashamed. ॥22॥
4.27.23: The sages said: O Sūta, we have heard it otherwise, and we relate that: let it be understood that Gautama, in anger, cursed those brahmins. ॥23॥
4.27.24: Sūta said: O brahmins, that too is true, owing to the difference of aeons (kalpa). I shall narrate that story too in detail, O you of good vows. ॥24॥
4.27.25: Gautama, seeing the sages then afflicted by famine, performed very great austerity directed to the great-souled Varuṇa. ॥25॥
4.27.26: By Varuṇa's gift he produced inexhaustible water; then he had rice and barley sown in abundance. ॥26॥
4.27.27: Thus Gautama, the best of sages, devoted to helping others, provided food for them by the power of his own austerity. ॥27॥
4.27.28: Once their wicked wives, feeling slighted over fetching water, angrily spoke to their husbands words that stirred up jealousy against Gautama. ॥28॥
4.27.29: Then those brahmins, of perverted minds and crooked intent, fashioned an artificial cow and set it to eating his grain. ॥29॥
4.27.30: Seeing the cow eating his grain, Gautama then struck it with a blade of grass, gently driving it away. ॥30॥
4.27.31: By the mere touch of the grass that cow fell to the ground and instantly died, O brahmins, by the force of destined karma. ॥31॥
4.27.32: A cow has been killed by Gautama: so then all the sages living there, of crooked intent, gathered together and declared. ॥32॥
4.27.33: Then Gautama became afraid, thinking, a cow has been killed; that follower of Śiva, together with his wife Ahalyā and disciples, was astonished. ॥33॥
4.27.34: Then Gautama, the best of sages, understanding the truth about that cow and filled with anger, cursed all those sages. ॥34॥
4.27.35: Gautama said: You are all wicked, especially causing grief to me, a constant devotee of Śiva; may you be ever averse to the Veda. ॥35॥
4.27.36: From today onward may you have no faith in the good rites taught in the Veda, and especially not in the Śaiva path that grants liberation. ॥36॥
4.27.37: From today onward may your faith be in an evil path, one devoid of the way to liberation and ever turned away from the Veda. ॥37॥
4.27.38: From today onward may your foreheads be smeared with clay; fall into hell, you brahmins with clay-smeared foreheads. ॥38॥
4.27.39: May you not be those for whom Śiva alone is the supreme deity; may you regard the non-dual Śiva as merely equal to other gods. ॥39॥
4.27.40: May you never have love for the worship of Śiva and related rites, for devotees steadfast in Śiva, or for the festivals of Śiva. ॥40॥
4.27.41: However many sorrow-giving curses I have pronounced today, may that many befall your descendants too, always. ॥41॥
4.27.42: O brahmins, may your sons, grandsons and the rest be non-Śaivas; and may you, together with your sons, surely dwell in hell. ॥42॥
4.27.43: Then may you all become caṇḍālas, afflicted by sorrow and poverty, deceitful, slanderers, ever marked with heated brands. ॥43॥
4.27.44: Sūta said: Having thus cursed all the sages, Gautama went to his own hermitage. He practised intense devotion to Śiva and became exceedingly pure. ॥44॥
4.27.45: Then all those brahmin sages, sick at heart because of those curses, took up residence in Kāñcī, excluded from the Śaiva dharma. ॥45॥
4.27.46: Their sons too all became excluded from the Śaiva dharma; likewise in the future, in the Kali age, many people will be wicked. ॥46॥
4.27.47: Thus, O best of sages, that account has been told in full; and, O wise ones, the earlier account too has been heard by you all with reverence. ॥47॥
4.27.48: Thus the origin of the Gautamī has been narrated to you, and also its supreme, excellent glory that removes all sins. ॥48॥
4.27.49: And the glory of the Tryambaka jyotirliṅga has been proclaimed; hearing it one is freed from all sins—there is no doubt about this. ॥49॥
4.27.50: After this I shall tell the glory of the Vaidyanātheśvara jyotirliṅga, which removes sin; let it be heard. ॥50॥
4.27.iti: Thus ends the twenty-seventh adhyāya, named The description of the glory of the Tryambakeśvara jyotirliṅga, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥27॥
4.28.1: Sūta said: Rāvaṇa, the foremost of the rākṣasas, proud and wholly given to pride, worshipped Hara with devotion on Kailāsa, the best of mountains. ॥1॥
4.28.2: When Hara, though worshipped for some time, was not pleased, he then undertook another austerity to win Śiva's favour. ॥2॥
4.28.3: Then this glorious Rāvaṇa, the descendant of Pulastya, went to a grove of trees to the south of the Himavat mountain, the place of spiritual attainment, ॥3॥
4.28.4: There, O brahmins, having made an excellent pit in the ground and set up the fire in it, and having installed Śiva near it, he performed fire-offerings. ॥4॥
4.28.5: In summer he stood amid five fires, in the rains he lay on the bare ground, and in winter he stayed within water; thus he performed austerity in three ways. ॥5॥
4.28.6: Thus he performed much austerity, yet even then the Supreme Self, Maheśāna, hard to propitiate by the wicked, was not pleased. ॥6॥
4.28.7: Then the great-spirited Rāvaṇa, lord of the demons, began the worship of Śaṅkara by cutting off his heads. ॥7॥
4.28.8: One head after another was cut off according to rule in the worship of Śiva; when in this proper sequence nine had been cut off by him, ॥8॥
4.28.9: then, when only one remained, Śaṅkara, affectionate to his devotees, became pleased and, satisfied, appeared right there. ॥9॥
4.28.10: The Lord restored the heads as before, free from injury, and granted him his desire, incomparable and supreme strength. ॥10॥
4.28.11: Having obtained his favour, Rāvaṇa the rākṣasa, with bowed shoulders and joined palms, replied to Śiva Śambhu: ॥11॥
4.28.12: Rāvaṇa said: Be gracious, O Lord of gods; I shall take you to Laṅkā. Make my wish fruitful; I have come to you for refuge. ॥12॥
4.28.13: Sūta said: Thus addressed then by Rāvaṇa, Śambhu, perplexed and having fallen into great difficulty, replied: ॥13॥
4.28.14: Śiva said: Listen, O best of rākṣasas, to my words in their essence: take my excellent liṅga to your home with true devotion. ॥14॥
4.28.15: Wherever you place the liṅga on the ground, there it will remain, no doubt. Do as you wish. ॥15॥
4.28.16: Sūta said: Thus addressed by Śambhu, Rāvaṇa, lord of the rākṣasas, said, so be it, took it up and went toward his own abode. ॥16॥
4.28.17: On the way, by Śiva's māyā, he felt the urge to pass urine; the mighty Rāvaṇa, descendant of Pulastya, was unable to restrain it. ॥17॥
4.28.18: Seeing a cowherd there, he requested him and gave him the liṅga. When a short while had passed, the cowherd became distressed. ॥18॥
4.28.19: Greatly oppressed by its weight, he set it down on the ground. Right there that liṅga, born of the essence of diamond, remained — granting all desires and removing sins by its very sight. ॥19॥
4.28.20: That liṅga, O sage, became known by the name Vaidyanātheśvara, famed in the three worlds, granting enjoyment and liberation to the good. ॥20॥
4.28.21: This excellent jyotirliṅga, by sight and by worship, removes all sins; it is divine, supreme, and increases liberation. ॥21॥
4.28.22: When that liṅga had become established there for the welfare of all worlds, Rāvaṇa, having gone home with the supreme boon obtained, the great demon joyfully told everything to his beloved. ॥22॥
4.28.23: Hearing that, all the gods led by Śakra, and likewise the sages, pure and with minds fixed on Śiva, consulted one another. ॥23॥
4.28.24: At that time, O sage, all the gods headed by Hari and Brahmā came there with great joy and performed worship in a special manner. ॥24॥
4.28.25: Then, seeing him manifest, those gods consecrated him, named him Vaidyanātha, bowed and praised, and went to heaven. ॥25॥
4.28.26: The sages said: When that liṅga was established there and Rāvaṇa had gone home, what happened then, dear one? Tell that in detail. ॥26॥
4.28.27: Sūta said: Rāvaṇa, having gone home with the supreme boon obtained, told everything to his beloved, and the great demon rejoiced exceedingly. ॥27॥
4.28.28: Hearing all that, the gods led by Śakra and likewise the sages, those lords of sages, deeply alarmed, spoke to one another: ॥28॥
4.28.29: The gods and the others said: This Rāvaṇa is wicked-souled, hostile to the gods, vile and evil-minded; having obtained a boon from Śiva, he will cause us great suffering. ॥29॥
4.28.30: What shall we do, where shall we go, and what will happen next? The wicked one has gained power; what all will he not accomplish against us? ॥30॥
4.28.31: Thus fallen into distress, the gods and sages led by Śakra, agitated, summoned Nārada and then questioned him. ॥31॥
4.28.32: The gods said: You are able to accomplish every task, O best of sages. Devise a means, O divine sage, for destroying the gods' distress. ॥32॥
4.28.33: This Rāvaṇa is extremely wicked; what will he not do? Where shall we go? We here are oppressed by the wicked one. ॥33॥
4.28.34: Nārada said: Give up your distress, O gods; having devised a plan, I go. By Śaṅkara's grace I shall accomplish the gods' task. ॥34॥
4.28.35: Sūta said: Having said this, the divine sage went to Rāvaṇa's abode, and having received hospitality, spoke all this with affection: ॥35॥
4.28.36: Nārada said: O best of rākṣasas, you are blessed, foremost of Śaiva devotees, rich in austerity. Seeing you today, O Rāvaṇa, my mind is greatly delighted. ॥36॥
4.28.37: Tell me fully your story arising from the worship of Śiva. Thus questioned by him, Rāvaṇa then spoke these words: ॥37॥
4.28.38: Rāvaṇa said: Having gone to Kailāsa for austerity, O great sage, I performed there a very severe austerity for a long time. ॥38॥
4.28.39: When Śaṅkara was not pleased, I then changed course; coming to a grove of trees, O sage, I again performed austerity. ॥39॥
4.28.40: In summer I stood amid five fires, in the rains I lay on the bare ground, and in winter I stayed within water; thus was austerity performed in three ways. ॥40॥
4.28.41: O lord of sages, I performed extremely severe austerity there in this way; yet Śaṅkara did not become even slightly pleased with me. ॥41॥
4.28.42: Then, angered, I dug a pit in the ground, set up a fire there, and fashioned an earthen liṅga. ॥42॥
4.28.43: Then Śambhu was worshipped with fragrances, sandal-paste, various incenses and food-offerings, following the rite of ārati (waving of lamps). ॥43॥
4.28.44: Śaṅkara was propitiated by me with prostrations and holy hymns, with songs, dances and instrumental music, and with offerings made by mouth and fingers. ॥44॥
4.28.45: With these and many other various means, O sage, the blessed Hara was worshipped according to the procedure laid down in the scriptures. ॥45॥
4.28.46: When the blessed Hara was not pleased and did not appear before me, I became sorrowful, not having obtained the true fruit of my austerity. ॥46॥
4.28.47: Fie on my body and my strength! Fie on my practice of austerity! Saying this, I made many oblations into the fire established there. ॥47॥
4.28.48: And again, resolving, I shall give up my own body in the fire, I cut off my heads to offer in that blazing, pure fire. ॥48॥
4.28.49: Cutting them off one by one and purifying them thoroughly, I offered nine of them to Śaṅkara. ॥49॥
4.28.50: And just as I began to cut off the tenth, O best of sages, Hara himself appeared there in the form of light. ॥50॥
4.28.51: Lovingly and swiftly the one tender to his devotees cried, don't, don't, and, being pleased, said: ask a boon; I shall give what your mind desires. ॥51॥
4.28.52: When he had said this, I beheld Maheśvara, bowed to him and praised him, joining my palms with deep devotion. ॥52॥
4.28.53: Then I chose this: give me incomparable strength. If you are pleased, O lord of gods, what could be difficult for me to obtain? ॥53॥
4.28.54: The compassionate Śiva, fully pleased, saying aloud, so be it, gave me everything my mind desired. ॥54॥
4.28.55: With his unfailing, gracious glance the Supreme Self, like a physician, rejoined my heads; having set them together, he looked upon them. ॥55॥
4.28.56: When this was done there, my body became as before, and by his grace I obtained every fruit. ॥56॥
4.28.57: Then, entreated by me, that bull-bannered god stayed there, and became famous in the three worlds by the name Vaidyanātheśvara. ॥57॥
4.28.58: Maheśvara in the form of the jyotirliṅga, by being seen and worshipped, bestows enjoyment and liberation in the world and brings welfare to all. ॥58॥
4.28.59: Having specially worshipped that jyotirliṅga and bowed to it, I have come here to conquer the three worlds. ॥59॥
4.28.60: Sūta said: Hearing those words of his, the divine sage Nārada was agitated, and laughing inwardly, he spoke to Rāvaṇa. ॥60॥
4.28.61: Nārada said: Listen, O best of Rākṣasas, I shall tell you what is good for you. You must do exactly what I say, never otherwise. ॥61॥
4.28.62: What you said, that Śiva himself has now granted you what is good, you should never take all that as true. ॥62॥
4.28.63: He has become deranged; what does he not say? That may well not be true — how can it be known? You are dear to me, so I tell you. ॥63॥
4.28.64: So go back and do the deed again — he said this, in truth, for your harm: you must again make an effort to lift up Kailāsa. ॥64॥
4.28.65: If this Kailāsa is lifted up, then indeed everything will be fruitful; there is no doubt. ॥65॥
4.28.66: Set it back as before and then return happily. Having reached complete certainty, do as you wish. ॥66॥
4.28.67: Sūta said: Thus addressed, Rāvaṇa, deluded by fate, thought it beneficial; taking the sage's words as true, he then went to Kailāsa. ॥67॥
4.28.68: Going there, he lifted up that mountain, and everything situated on it was thrown into confusion, one thing upon another. ॥68॥
4.28.69: Seeing this, Girīśa said, what has happened? Then Girijā, laughing, replied to Śambhu. ॥69॥
4.28.70: Girijā said: The fruit of having a good disciple has come about; it has turned out properly from the disciple — the incomparable strength that was given to that tranquil-souled, most heroic one. ॥70॥
4.28.71: Sūta said: Hearing Girijā's pointed words, Maheśvara, regarding Rāvaṇa as ungrateful and proud of his strength, cursed him. ॥71॥
4.28.72: Mahādeva said: Ho, Rāvaṇa, wicked devotee, evil-minded one, do not carry such pride. Soon there shall arise here one who crushes the pride of your arms. ॥72॥
4.28.73: Nārada then heard what had happened there; and Rāvaṇa, pleased at heart, went back to his own abode as he had come. ॥73॥
4.28.74: Having made a firm resolve, the mighty Rāvaṇa, deluded by his strength and destroyer of others' pride, brought the world under his control. ॥74॥
4.28.75: With the greatly powerful divine weapon obtained by Śiva's command, no opponent was then able to match Rāvaṇa. ॥75॥
4.28.76: Thus has the greatness of Vaidyanātheśvara been narrated; the sin of men who hear it is reduced to ashes. ॥76॥
4.28.iti: Thus ends the twenty-eighth adhyāya, named The description of the glory of the Vaidyanātheśvara jyotirliṅga, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥28॥
4.29.1: Sūta said: Now, therefore, I shall narrate how the supreme and most excellent liṅga of the Supreme Self, called Nāgeśa, in the form of light, came into being. ॥1॥
4.29.2: There was a certain rākṣasī named Dārukā, made arrogant by a boon from Pārvatī; and her husband was Dāruka, exceedingly mighty. ॥2॥
4.29.3: With many rākṣasas he wrought slaughter of the virtuous there; he then destroyed the sacrifices and the dharma of the people. ॥3॥
4.29.4: On the western sea he had a forest rich in every abundance, extending sixteen yojanas in every direction. ॥4॥
4.29.5: That forest, where Dārukā goes for her own pleasure, was furnished there with land, trees and all requisites. ॥5॥
4.29.6: The Goddess granted Dārukā the power of overseeing that forest; indeed she would go to that forest with her husband at will. ॥6॥
4.29.7: Staying there, the rākṣasa Dāruka, together with his wife Dārukā, then struck fear into everyone. ॥7॥
4.29.8: All those afflicted people went for refuge to Aurva; bowing with great devotion, with heads bent, they spoke to him. ॥8॥
4.29.9: The people said: O great sage, grant us refuge; otherwise we are killed by the wicked. You are able to do everything; you are radiant with spiritual power. ॥9॥
4.29.10: On earth there is no one but you as our refuge, to whose presence we may go and, staying there, find happiness. ॥10॥
4.29.11: On seeing you, all the rākṣasas flee far away; in you the radiance of Śiva ever shines like fire. ॥11॥
4.29.12: Sūta said: Thus entreated by the people, Aurva, best of sages, grieving and a giver of refuge, spoke words for their protection. ॥12॥
4.29.13: Aurva said: If the rākṣasas harm living beings on earth, then those mighty rākṣasas shall themselves be separated from their lives. ॥13॥
4.29.14: When sacrifices are destroyed by them, then let all the rākṣasas be deprived of life. This truth is spoken by me. ॥14॥
4.29.15: Sūta said: Having spoken these words to them and comforted the people again, Aurva, bringer of happiness to the world, performed various austerities. ॥15॥
4.29.16: Then the gods, knowing that this was the reason given by the curse, made preparations for war with the enemies of the gods. ॥16॥
4.29.17: With every effort, all the gods led by Śakra, bearing various weapons, arrived there for battle. ॥17॥
4.29.18: Seeing them, all the wicked rākṣasas there, wherever they were stationed, again became intent on deliberating among themselves. ॥18॥
4.29.19: The demons said: What is to be done? Where shall we go? We have fallen into a crisis. If we fight, we die; and if we fight, the foe is not slain. ॥19॥
4.29.20: If we just remain as we are, what is to be eaten—each other? Misery has come upon us in every way; who could avert it? ॥20॥
4.29.21: Sūta said: Having deliberated thus, the rākṣasas there, Dāruka and the rest, not finding a remedy, fell into constant misery. ॥21॥
4.29.22: The rākṣasī Dārukā too, knowing the misery that had come, then told them of that boon of Bhavānī. ॥22॥
4.29.23: Dārukā said: Formerly the consort of Bhava, worshipped by me, granted a boon: go with your own people to the forest, wherever you wish to go. ॥23॥
4.29.24: Since that boon was obtained by me, why should misery be endured? Taking the forest into the water, the rākṣasas may live happily. ॥24॥
4.29.25: Sūta said: Hearing those words of the rākṣasī, all the rākṣasas became joyful and, now fearless, spoke among themselves. ॥25॥
4.29.26: Blessed is she, she has fulfilled her purpose; by the queen herself we are saved. Bowing to her, they respectfully told her all that. ॥26॥
4.29.27: If there is power to go, let us go; why deliberate? Going there into the water, O lady, we shall live happily forever. ॥27॥
4.29.28: Meanwhile the people, formerly afflicted by the rākṣasas with various miseries, arrived together with the gods for battle. ॥28॥
4.29.29: Then, the rākṣasas being hard pressed, she, relying on the power of that Bhavānī, carried off the entire city together with its water and land, ॥29॥
4.29.30: the rākṣasī, uttering the praise of the Goddess, Victory, victory! then flew up like a winged king of mountains. ॥30॥
4.29.31: She then settled fearlessly in the middle of the ocean; with all her retinue, that follower of Śivā rejoiced. ॥31॥
4.29.32: Living there in the ocean and in the city, the pleasure-loving rākṣasas attained happiness and sported fearlessly. ॥32॥
4.29.33: The rākṣasas never came onto the earth; out of fear of the sage's curse alone, they then roamed about on the water. ॥33॥
4.29.34: Seizing people who were in boats, they then carried them to that city and threw them into prison; some of them they killed. ॥34॥
4.29.35: Again and again those rākṣasas then caused affliction, dwelling there fearless because of Bhavānī's granting of the boon. ॥35॥
4.29.36: Just as formerly there was incessant fear among people on land, so now, O lords of sages, there was constant fear of them on the water. ॥36॥
4.29.37: Once that rākṣasī came out of the city onto the water and stood blocking the route, near the shore, in order to harass the people. ॥37॥
4.29.38: Meanwhile, very many fine boats arrived there from all sides in various ways, crowded with people. ॥38॥
4.29.39: Seeing those boats, the wicked rākṣasas were delighted; going there quickly, they forcibly seized those aboard. ॥39॥
4.29.40: Taking them, those mighty ones came to the city and, binding them with strong fetters, threw them into prison. ॥40॥
4.29.41: Those people, bound with fetters, remained in the prison; threatened again and again, they fell into extreme misery. ॥41॥
4.29.42: Among them, the one who was the chief was a vaiśya named Supriya; dear to Śiva, of virtuous conduct, he was always a devotee of Śiva. ॥42॥
4.29.43: He would never remain without the worship of Śiva; he was wholly devoted to Śiva's dharma, adorned with sacred ash and rudrākṣa beads. ॥43॥
4.29.44: If the worship had not been done, then he would not eat; therefore even there that vaiśya performed the worship of Śiva. ॥44॥
4.29.45: Though confined in the prison, he then taught many others the Śiva mantra and the worship of the earthen liṅga, O best of sages. ॥45॥
4.29.46: Then all of them there performed, according to rule, the worship of Śiva that grants one's desires, as they had seen and as they had heard. ॥46॥
4.29.47: Some there, having assumed an excellent posture, remained in meditation, and some, filled with joy, performed mental worship of Śiva. ॥47॥
4.29.48: Then, right there, the chief performed the visible worship of Śiva by the very rite of the earthen liṅga, O lords of sages. ॥48॥
4.29.49: And others, who did not know the rite, practised the supreme remembrance: they remained meditating on Śaṅkara with the mantra namaḥ śivāya. ॥49॥
4.29.50: And the one named Supriya, the best of vaiśyas, dear to Śiva, meditating in his mind there, performed the worship of Śiva. ॥50॥
4.29.51: And Śambhu, in the form as described in meditation, visibly accepted everything; yet he himself did not know that it was being accepted by Śiva. ॥51॥
4.29.52: While the vaiśya was thus performing the worship of Śiva, six months passed there without obstacle, O lords of sages. ॥52॥
4.29.53: Hear now, O best of sages, with an attentive mind, the deed of the moon-crested Śiva that took place after this. ॥53॥
4.29.iti: Thus ends the twenty-ninth adhyāya, named The description of the harassment by the rākṣasas of the Dāruka forest, in the Māhātmya of the Nāgeśvara jyotirliṅga, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥29॥
4.30.1: Sūta said: Once a servant of that evil-minded Rākṣasa saw, in front of him the merchant, the beautiful form of Śaṅkara. ॥1॥
4.30.2: Then he reported to that king of the Rākṣasas, exactly as it was, that whole event, wondrous and astonishing. ॥2॥
4.30.3: That king of the Rākṣasas, Dāruka, coming there quickly with his forces, agitated, questioned that devotee of Śiva. ॥3॥
4.30.4: Dāruka said: What are you meditating on, O Vaiśya? Speak the truth before me. If so, there will be no death for you—and my word is not otherwise. ॥4॥
4.30.5: Sūta said: He replied, I do not know. Hearing that, Dāruka became angry and urged the Rākṣasas: O Rākṣasas, let this one be killed. ॥5॥
4.30.6: Thus ordered by him, they, bearing various weapons, went swiftly to kill that tiger among Vaiśyas, whose mind was fixed on Śaṅkara. ॥6॥
4.30.7: Seeing them arrive, his eyes trembling with fear, he remembered Śiva with great love and sang his names again and again. ॥7॥
4.30.8: The merchant lord said: Protect me, O Śaṅkara, Lord of gods; protect me, O Śambhu, O Śiva. Save me from this wicked one, O Lord of the three worlds, slayer of the wicked, lover of devotees. ॥8॥
4.30.9: You alone, O God, are my all today. I am dependent on you, I am yours, you are my life always, O Lord. ॥9॥
4.30.10: Sūta said: Thus entreated, Śambhu then emerged from a cleft in the earth, with an excellent shrine having four doors. ॥10॥
4.30.11: Seeing in its midst that wondrous form of Śiva, of the nature of light, accompanied by his retinue, he worshipped him. ॥11॥
4.30.12: Worshipped thus, Śambhu himself became pleased; giving him the weapon called Pāśupata, he struck the chief Rākṣasas. ॥12॥
4.30.13: He quickly slew all of them along with their equipment and their hosts; and that Śaṅkara, the destroyer of the wicked, protected his own devotee. ॥13॥
4.30.14: Having then slain them all, Śambhu, doer of utter wonders, who assumes a fine body through his own play, granted a boon to the forest as well. ॥14॥
4.30.15: In this forest may the duties of the varṇas always prevail—of Brāhmaṇas, Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas, and likewise of Śūdras. ॥15॥
4.30.16: May there be here excellent sages, never tāmasic ones—expounders and promoters of Śiva's dharma. ॥16॥
4.30.17: Sūta said: At this time the Rākṣasī named Dārukā, dejected in mind, offered praise to the Goddess Pārvatī. ॥17॥
4.30.18: Then the Goddess, pleased, said, what shall I do? She in turn said there, let my lineage be protected by you. ॥18॥
4.30.19: I will protect your lineage; truly this is said by me. Having said this, Pārvatī entered into a dispute with Śiva himself. ॥19॥
4.30.20: Śiva too, the Lord, seeing the Goddess angry and being bound by her boon, replied with great affection: do as you wish. ॥20॥
4.30.21: Sūta said: Hearing these words of her own husband Śaṅkara, Pārvatī, much pleased, laughed and quickly spoke. ॥21॥
4.30.22: Pārvatī said: Your word will come true at the end of the yuga; until then, let there be a tāmasic creation—this is my view. ॥22॥
4.30.23: Otherwise there would be dissolution. What I have said is true, O Śiva; let it be made valid, O Lord—I am yours, I take refuge in you. ॥23॥
4.30.24: And this Rākṣasī, the goddess Dārukā, is a śakti of mine, the strongest of Rākṣasīs; let her rule the kingdom of the Rākṣasas. ॥24॥
4.30.25: These wives of the Rākṣasas will give birth to sons; all of them together are approved by me to dwell in the forest. ॥25॥
4.30.26: Sūta said: Hearing these words of Pārvatī, his own wife, the Lord Śaṅkara, pleased at heart, spoke. ॥26॥
4.30.27: Śaṅkara said: If you say so, then hear my word, beloved: I shall gladly abide in this forest for the protection of devotees. ॥27॥
4.30.28: Whoever, abiding in the duties of his varṇa, beholds me here with love, he will become a universal emperor. ॥28॥
4.30.29: Further, at the turn of the Kali age, at the start of the Satya age, there will be a lord of kings, son of Mahāsena, renowned as Vīrasena. ॥29॥
4.30.30: He, most valiant through devotion to me, will behold me; having beheld me, he will become a universal emperor. ॥30॥
4.30.31: Sūta said: Thus that divine couple, having jested with each other, remained there themselves in person, O Brāhmaṇas, as bestowers of great aid. ॥31॥
4.30.32: Śiva, in the form of a jyotirliṅga, became by name Nāgeśvara, and the Goddess Śivā became Nāgeśvarī—both dear to the virtuous. ॥32॥
4.30.33: The sages said: How will Vīrasena go there to the Dārukā forest? How will he worship Śiva? Tell us that, O wise one. ॥33॥
4.30.34: Sūta said: In the beautiful land of Niṣadha, in a family of Kṣatriyas, was Vīrasena, son of Mahāsena, dear to Śiva. ॥34॥
4.30.35: Worshipping the Lord in an earthen liṅga, Vīrasena performed extremely difficult austerity for a period of twelve years. ॥35॥
4.30.36: Then Śaṅkara, Lord of gods, pleased, appeared before him and said: having made a fish of wood, coated with tin, ॥36॥
4.30.37: and having endowed it with yogic power, I shall give it to you, O dear Vīrasena. Taking it, entering this water, go now along with boats. ॥37॥
4.30.38: Then, going there and entering the cleft made by me, and worshipping Nāgeśvara, ॥38॥
4.30.39: then obtaining the Pāśupata weapon and slaying the chief Rākṣasīs—once I have been seen, nothing will then be lacking for you. ॥39॥
4.30.40: And the strength of Pārvatī too will be complete; and others who will be in the forest in the form of Mlecchas will be auspicious. ॥40॥
4.30.41: Having spoken thus to Vīrasena there, Śaṅkara, the Lord, the remover of sorrow, showed great compassion and vanished right there. ॥41॥
4.30.42: Thus granted a boon by Śiva, the Supreme Self, he too then became able to accomplish everything; there is no doubt. ॥42॥
4.30.43: Thus the god Nāgeśvara, lord of the luminous ones (jyotis), arose in the form of a liṅga, ever granting all desires to the three worlds. ॥43॥
4.30.44: The wise one who listens daily and with reverence to this account of the manifestation of Nāgeśa attains all desires, and the account is destructive of great sins. ॥44॥
4.30.iti: Thus ends the thirtieth adhyāya, named The description of the glory of the manifestation of the Nāgeśvara jyotirliṅga, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥30॥
4.31.1: Sūta said: Next I shall describe the liṅga named Rāmeśvara and how it arose in former times. O sages, listen with attention. ॥1॥
4.31.2: Long ago Viṣṇu, dear to the virtuous, descended upon the earth. ॥2॥
4.31.3: There, O brahmins, Sītā was abducted by Rāvaṇa, a master of great deception; the daughter of Janaka was taken to his own house in Laṅkā. ॥3॥
4.31.4: Intent on searching for her, he went to the city called Kiṣkindhā; becoming the benefactor of Sugrīva, he slew Vālin. ॥4॥
4.31.5: Staying there for some time, devoted to searching for her, he deliberated with Sugrīva and the others and with Lakṣmaṇa. ॥5॥
4.31.6: Rāma, the king's son, sent forth the monkeys headed by Hanumat in the four directions for the purpose of finding her. ॥6॥
4.31.7: Then, learning from the mouth of the foremost monkey that Sītā had been taken to Laṅkā, and receiving Sītā's crest-jewel, Rāghava rejoiced greatly. ॥7॥
4.31.8: Then, O twice-born, Rāma, with the monkey-lord and accompanied by Lakṣmaṇa, together with the virtuous and very mighty monkeys headed by Sugrīva, ॥8॥
4.31.9: and with troops numbering eighteen padmas, went to the shore of the ocean — the salt-mine that is seen in the southern sea. ॥9॥
4.31.10: Having come there, Rāma himself, beloved of Śiva, stood on the shore, attended by the monkeys and by Lakṣmaṇa. ॥10॥
4.31.11: Alas, Jānakī! Where has she gone, and when will she be united with me? The ocean is fathomless, and the monkey army cannot cross it. ॥11॥
4.31.12: The rākṣasa is a lifter of mountains, of great strength and valour; his fortress called Laṅkā is hard to reach; and Indrajit is his son. ॥12॥
4.31.13: Thus reflecting, he stood on the shore with Lakṣmaṇa and was consoled by the forest-dwellers led by Aṅgada and others. ॥13॥
4.31.14: Meanwhile Rāghava, the best of Śaivas, wanting water, affectionately spoke to his brother named Lakṣmaṇa. ॥14॥
4.31.15: Śrī Rāma said: Brother Lakṣmaṇa, lord of heroes, I am thirsty and want water. So bring water quickly by means of some monkeys. ॥15॥
4.31.16: Sūta said: Hearing that, the monkeys there ran in the ten directions; bringing water, they bowed, stood before him and said: ॥16॥
4.31.17: The monkeys said: Master, please take the water brought at your command — most excellent, very sweet, cool and refreshing to life. ॥17॥
4.31.18: Sūta said: Hearing that, Rāmacandra, greatly pleased, looked at them with a compassionate gaze and himself took that water. ॥18॥
4.31.19: When that Śaiva took the water and began to drink, then, by Śiva's will, this recollection arose in him: ॥19॥
4.31.20: I have not had the sight (darśana) of Śambhu, my own master, the supreme lord, the giver of all bliss; how can water be taken? ॥20॥
4.31.21: Saying this, the best of the Raghus set the water aside; and afterwards the joy of the Raghus performed worship of Śiva with an earthen liṅga. ॥21॥
4.31.22: Arranging the services beginning with invocation (āvāhana), he lovingly worshipped Lord Śaṅkara according to rule with the sixteenfold offerings. ॥22॥
4.31.23: Having diligently pleased Śiva with prostrations and divine hymns, Rāma joyfully entreated Śaṅkara with true devotion. ॥23॥
4.31.24: Śrī Rāma said: O master, Śambhu, Mahādeva, ever affectionate to devotees, protect me, your devotee, who has come for refuge and is dejected in mind. ॥24॥
4.31.25: O you who carry beings across worldly existence, this water of the ocean is fathomless; and the rākṣasa named Rāvaṇa is a great hero, exceedingly powerful. ॥25॥
4.31.26: This force of monkeys, my means of war, is fickle. How will my task of recovering my beloved be accomplished? ॥26॥
4.31.27: In that, O god of good vows, you must give me help; without your help, O lord, my task is hard to achieve. ॥27॥
4.31.28: Rāvaṇa too is yours, your devotee; here he is in every way unconquerable by all; proud of the boon given by you, he is a great hero, conqueror of the three worlds. ॥28॥
4.31.29: Yet I too am your servant and wholly dependent on you. Considering this, O Sadāśiva, you should take my side. ॥29॥
4.31.30: Sūta said: Having entreated thus and bowed again and again, he then cried aloud with loud shouts, Victory, victory, O Śaṅkara! ॥30॥
4.31.31: Having thus praised Śiva there, devoted to mantra and meditation, and having again performed worship, he danced before the Lord. ॥31॥
4.31.32: When, his heart melting with love, he made the cheek-sound (gallanāda), then Lord Śaṅkara became exceedingly pleased. ॥32॥
4.31.33: Maheśvara, in the form of light, with his limbs and his retinue, assuming the spotless form as described in scripture, quickly became manifest. ॥33॥
4.31.34: Then Maheśvara, his heart gratified by Rāma's devotion, said: may there be good fortune. Choose a boon, Rāma. ॥34॥
4.31.35: Seeing that form then, all became purified. Thereupon Rāghava, devoted to the dharma of Śiva, himself performed worship. ॥35॥
4.31.36: Having offered various praises and joyfully bowed to Śiva, he then asked for his own victory in the battle with Rāvaṇa. ॥36॥
4.31.37: Then Maheśvara, his heart pleased by Rāma's devotion, lovingly said again: may victory be yours, great king. ॥37॥
4.31.38: Having obtained the victory granted by Śiva and received his permission, he entreated again with joined palms and bowed head. ॥38॥
4.31.39: Śrī Rāma said: O master, if you are pleased, O Śaṅkara, you should remain here for the purification of the worlds and for the benefit of others. ॥39॥
4.31.40: Sūta said: Thus addressed, Śiva then took the form of a liṅga there, and became renowned on the face of the earth by the name Rāmeśvara. ॥40॥
4.31.41: Rāma, by its power, swiftly crossed the ocean, quickly slew Rāvaṇa and the other Rākṣasas, and regained his beloved. ॥41॥
4.31.42: The glory of Rāmeśvara became wondrous and unequalled on earth; it grants enjoyment and liberation, and always fulfils the desires of devotees. ॥42॥
4.31.43: Whoever, with true devotion, bathes Śiva as Rāmeśvara with the divine water of the Gaṅgā is indeed liberated while living. ॥43॥
4.31.44: Having enjoyed here all pleasures, even those hard for the gods to obtain, at the end, attaining supreme knowledge, he would surely attain kaivalya (final liberation). ॥44॥
4.31.45: Thus has been narrated to you the divine jyotirliṅga of Śiva named Rāmeśvara, which removes the sins of those who hear of it. ॥45॥
4.31.iti: Thus ends the thirty-first adhyāya, named The description of the glory of Rāmeśvara, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥31॥
4.32.1: Sūta said: After this, the jyotirliṅga Ghuśmeśa is declared. O best of sages, listen to its great glory. ॥1॥
4.32.2: In the southern direction there is an excellent mountain named Deva Devagiri. Wondrous to behold and endowed with great beauty, it always shines. ॥2॥
4.32.3: Near it lived a brahmin named Sudharmā, born in the lineage of Bharadvāja, foremost among knowers of Brahman. ॥3॥
4.32.4: His beloved wife Sudehā was devoted to the dharma of Śiva, always intent on serving her husband, and skilled in household work. ॥4॥
4.32.5: And Sudharmā, the best of the twice-born, worshipped the gods and guests, was always devoted to the Vedic path, and intent on tending the sacred fire. ॥5॥
4.32.6: He performed the sandhyā rites at the three junctures of the day, had radiance equal to the sun's form, taught students, and was learned in the Vedas and śāstras. ॥6॥
4.32.7: He was wealthy, a supreme giver, a vessel of the virtue of kindliness, always delighting in Śiva's rites, a Śaiva, and fond of Śaiva people. ॥7॥
4.32.8: Much of his life passed as he practised dharma, yet no son was born to him; the fertile season of his wife proved fruitless. ॥8॥
4.32.9: Devoted as he was to knowledge of reality, he did not grieve, thinking: the self is the saviour of the self, and it is the purifier of the self. ॥9॥
4.32.10: Holding such a thought in mind, he did not grieve then; but Sudehā grieved over having no son. ॥10॥
4.32.11: Every day she entreated her husband, expert in all branches of learning, to make efforts for begetting a son. ॥11॥
4.32.12: He too then rebuked his wife: what will a son do? Who is mother, who father, who son? Who is kinsman, and who is dear? ॥12॥
4.32.13: O lady, everything in the three worlds is bent on its own interest; there is no doubt of this. Understand this well with your intellect and do not grieve. ॥13॥
4.32.14: Therefore, O lady, you must surely give up your grief. O you of auspicious vows, you should not speak of this to me again and again. ॥14॥
4.32.15: Having thus restrained her, he, intent on the dharma of the Lord, remained supremely content and abandoned the sorrow of the pairs of opposites. ॥15॥
4.32.16: Once Sudehā went to a neighbour's house for friendly conversation, and a quarrel arose there. ॥16॥
4.32.17: His wife, out of a woman's nature, then reviled her; Sudehā, the brahmin's beloved, was addressed by her with harsh words thus: ॥17॥
4.32.18: The neighbour's wife said: O sonless woman, how can you be proud? I am the one with a son. My son will enjoy my wealth; who will enjoy yours? ॥18॥
4.32.19: Surely the king will seize your wealth; there is no doubt of this. Shame, shame on you! Shame on your wealth, and shame on your pride, O barren woman! ॥19॥
4.32.20: Sūta said: Reviled thus by those women, she came home distressed and respectfully told her husband all that had been said. ॥20॥
4.32.21: The wise brahmin did not grieve then either: let what has been said be said; whatever is to be will be, my dear. ॥21॥
4.32.22: Though consoled by him again and again in this way, she did not give up her grief then; she persisted in her insistence. ॥22॥
4.32.23: Sudehā said: By whatever means, you must beget a son; you are dear to me. Otherwise, O best of the embodied, I shall give up my body. ॥23॥
4.32.24: Sūta said: Hearing what she said, Sudharmā, the best of brahmins, distressed by her insistence, then remembered Śiva in his mind. ॥24॥
4.32.25: The brahmin, alert, placed two flowers before the fire, and in his mind regarded the right-hand flower as the one granting the wish for a son. ॥25॥
4.32.26: Having made this wager, the brahmin said to his wife: for the fruit of a son, you must pick one of these two flowers. ॥26॥
4.32.27: She resolved in her mind: may I have a son, and may the flower my husband has fixed upon come to me. ॥27॥
4.32.28: Having said this, she bowed there to Śiva, bowed to the fire, prayed again, and took a single flower. ॥28॥
4.32.29: But Sudehā did not take the one her husband had thought of, owing to a delusion arising from Śiva's will. ॥29॥
4.32.30: Seeing that, the man heaved a sigh, and remembering the lotus feet of Śiva, said to his wife: ॥30॥
4.32.31: Sudharmā said: It has been ordained by the Lord; how could it be otherwise? Give up hope, my dear, and serve the Lord. ॥31॥
4.32.32: Having said this, the brahmin himself gave up hope and became engaged in dharmic duties, intent on meditation on Śaṅkara. ॥32॥
4.32.33: But Sudehā, out of desire for a child, did not give up her insistence. With folded hands and bowed head, she lovingly replied to her husband: ॥33॥
4.32.34: Sudehā said: Let there be no son from me; take another wife at my bidding. Through her a son will surely be born; there is no doubt. ॥34॥
4.32.35: Sūta said: Thus entreated, that brahmin, the best of Śaivas, intent on dharma, then spoke to his beloved Sudehā: ॥35॥
4.32.36: Sudharmā said: All your sorrow and mine has surely gone. Therefore, my dear, do not now create an obstacle to dharma. ॥36॥
4.32.37: Sūta said: Though restrained thus, she then brought her own mother's daughter, her sister, to the house and said this to her husband: take her as wife. ॥37॥
4.32.38: Sudharmā said: Now you say, she is dear to me, but later, when she becomes the mother of a son, you will feel rivalry with her. ॥38॥
4.32.39: Sūta said: Addressed thus by her husband, Sudehā, his beloved, again spoke with joined hands to her husband Sudharmā, O brahmins: ॥39॥
4.32.40: I will not feel rivalry with my sister, O best of the twice-born. Marry her for the sake of a son; this is my bidding. ॥40॥
4.32.41: Thus entreated by that beloved wife of his, the brāhmaṇa Sudharmā married that Ghuśmā according to the rite of marriage. ॥41॥
4.32.42: Then, having married her, the brāhmaṇa entreated her, Sudehā: this younger one is truly yours; she should always be cared for, O sinless beloved. ॥42॥
4.32.43: Having spoken thus, the righteous-souled Sudharmā, foremost among Śaiva devotees, quickly undertook his own observance of dharma as was fitting. ॥43॥
4.32.44: And she, the beloved Sudehā, behaved toward that daughter of her mother like a friend; giving up hostility, she cared for her day and night. ॥44॥
4.32.45: And the younger wife, having obtained her sister's permission, promptly made one hundred and one earthen liṅgas every day. ॥45॥
4.32.46: Ghuśmā, having worshipped them according to the prescribed rite together with the offerings, cast them into the pond situated nearby. ॥46॥
4.32.47: Thus every day she performed the worship of Śiva that grants one's desires, dismissing the deity and invoking him again according to the rules of that worship. ॥47॥
4.32.48: As she thus performed the worship of Śaṅkara daily, the count of a hundred thousand was completed, bestowing the fruit of all desires. ॥48॥
4.32.49: By the grace of Śaṅkara alone, a son was born to her—handsome, fortunate, and a vessel of auspicious qualities. ॥49॥
4.32.50: Seeing him, that brāhmaṇa, the foremost knower of dharma, was supremely delighted; yet, unattached and devoted to knowledge and dharma, he enjoyed happiness. ॥50॥
4.32.51: Meanwhile Sudehā developed a fierce rivalry toward her; her heart, at first cool, then became like a sword. ॥51॥
4.32.52: What vile, sorrow-giving deed took place after that—listen to it with attentive mind, O lords of sages. ॥52॥
4.32.iti: Thus ends the thirty-second adhyāya, named The description of the doings of Sudehā and Sudharmā, in the Māhātmya of Ghuśmeśvara, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥32॥
4.33.1: Sūta said: Seeing the son of the younger wife, the elder fell into sorrow. Unable to bear that happiness, she quickly turned hostile. ॥1॥
4.33.2: Everyone constantly praised her for bearing a son; she could not bear that, nor likewise the child's beauty and other qualities. ॥2॥
4.33.3: Seeing that dearly loved son, the vessel of good qualities, beloved of his parents, her heart then burned like fire. ॥3॥
4.33.4: Meanwhile brāhmaṇas came to give their daughter in marriage, and he performed his son's marriage right there according to rule. ॥4॥
4.33.5: Sudharmā, together with Ghuśmā, attained supreme joy; all the relatives showed honour to that Ghuśmā. ॥5॥
4.33.6: Seeing that, Sudehā then burned in her mind; falling into extreme sorrow, she kept saying, Alas, I am ruined! ॥6॥
4.33.7: Sudharmā, coming home, presented the bride and his married son to his two dear wives, showing his joy as if to delight them. ॥7॥
4.33.8: Ghuśmā was delighted, but Sudehā fell into grief; unable to bear that happiness, she, in her distress, fell to the ground. ॥8॥
4.33.9: Ghuśmā said, the bride and son are yours, not mine. And the bride and son affectionately regarded her as mother and mother-in-law. ॥9॥
4.33.10: The husband too regarded the elder as dear, not so the younger; even so, the elder then remained impure within her heart. ॥10॥
4.33.11: One day the elder, the sorrowful Sudehā, pondered thus in her heart: how may my sorrow be quelled? ॥11॥
4.33.12: Sudehā said: The fire in my heart will surely be quenched only by the water of Ghuśmā's eyes, tears born of grief—not otherwise. ॥12॥
4.33.13: Therefore today I shall kill her sweet-spoken son; whatever is to come hereafter, let it be. This is my firm resolve. ॥13॥
4.33.14: Sūta said: The wicked have no discrimination between what should and should not be done. O brāhmaṇas, the feeling of co-wife rivalry is generally harsh and self-destructive. ॥14॥
4.33.15: One day, at night, the elder took a knife and cut at the limbs of the son sleeping with his bride. ॥15॥
4.33.16: That night she hacked every limb of Ghuśmā's son into pieces; and, arrogant and very strong, she carried them and threw them into the lake right there. ॥16॥
4.33.17: Where Ghuśmā daily cast her liṅgas, there she threw them, came back, and slept at ease, content. ॥17॥
4.33.18: Rising at dawn, Ghuśmā did her daily rite as usual, and the excellent Sudharmā himself performed his daily duties. ॥18॥
4.33.19: Meanwhile the elder went about the household work, full of joy, the fire in her heart now well quenched. ॥19॥
4.33.20: The bride, rising at daybreak, saw the bed wet with blood and strewn with pieces of the body, and fell into grief. ॥20॥
4.33.21: She told her mother-in-law: where has your son gone? The bed is wet with blood, and pieces of a body are seen. ॥21॥
4.33.22: Alas, I am ruined! Who has done this wicked deed, O you of pure vows? Uttering this, his beloved wept bitterly in many ways. ॥22॥
4.33.23: The elder then feigned grief, crying, Alas, I am ruined indeed! She made a show of sorrow outwardly while full of joy in her mind. ॥23॥
4.33.24: Ghuśmā too, hearing then the grief of her daughter-in-law, did not swerve from that vow of hers, the daily worship of earthen liṅgas. ॥24॥
4.33.25: Her mind did not become agitated in the least; and her husband too remained the same until the vow's rite was completed. ॥25॥
4.33.26: At midday, at the end of the worship, though she saw the dreadful bed, even then Ghuśmā showed no grief at all. ॥26॥
4.33.27: She thought: he by whom this son was given will surely protect him. He is renowned as fond of his devotees, the Death of Death, the refuge of the good. ॥27॥
4.33.28: If Śambhu, the Lord, the sole master, is our protector, what is there to fear? Like a garland-maker, those whom he joins he also separates. ॥28॥
4.33.29: What good will my worrying do now? Reflecting on this truth, she did not grieve then, having attained steadfastness in Śiva. ॥29॥
4.33.30: Taking the earthen liṅgas, calm-minded as before, she went to the bank of the lake, reciting the names of Śambhu. ॥30॥
4.33.31: When, having cast the earthen liṅgas there, she turned back, then she saw her son, risen from the pond, standing on the bank. ॥31॥
4.33.32: The son said: Mother, come, let me embrace you. I was dead and am now alive, through the power of your merit and by the grace of Śaṅkara. ॥32॥
4.33.33: Sūta said: Seeing her son alive, Ghuśmā, his mother, O brāhmaṇas, did not become elated there, just as earlier she had not been grieved. ॥33॥
4.33.34: At that moment Śiva swiftly manifested himself there in the form of light, and Maheśa, well pleased, spoke. ॥34॥
4.33.35: Śiva said: I am pleased; ask a boon. This son was killed by the wicked woman; and I shall kill her with my trident, O lovely-faced one. ॥35॥
4.33.36: Sūta said: Then Ghuśmā, bowing deeply to Śiva, humbly asked a boon: O Lord, this Sudehā, my sister, should be protected by you. ॥36॥
4.33.37: Śiva said: Harm was done by her; how can you do good to her? Sudehā, the evildoer, deserves to be slain. ॥37॥
4.33.38: Ghuśmā said: By the mere sight of you no sin remains. Now that she has seen you, that sin of hers would be reduced to ashes. ॥38॥
4.33.39: He who does good in return for wrongs—by the mere sight of him, sin goes far away. ॥39॥
4.33.40: This wondrous saying of the Lord I have heard, O God. Therefore, O Sadāśiva, let kindness be shown to her by whom this was done. ॥40॥
4.33.41: Sūta said: Thus addressed by her there, Maheśvara, the ocean of compassion, affectionate to his devotees, became exceedingly pleased once again and spoke to her. ॥41॥
4.33.42: Śiva said: O Ghuśmā, ask for another boon, and I shall grant what is beneficial to you. I am well pleased with your devotion and with you, by your nature free from perturbation. ॥42॥
4.33.43: Having heard his words, she said: O Lord, if a boon is to be given by you, then for the protection of the worlds you should dwell here under a name derived from mine. ॥43॥
4.33.44: Then Śiva, the Great Lord, well pleased, said there: I shall dwell here by your name, called Ghuśmeśa, the giver of happiness. ॥44॥
4.33.45: May my auspicious liṅga, named Ghuśmeśa, become well renowned. May this lake always become the abode of liṅgas. ॥45॥
4.33.46: Therefore it will be famed in the three worlds by the name Śivālaya. This lake will always grant all desires through its mere sight. ॥46॥
4.33.47: O lady of good vows, in your lineage, up to a hundred and one generations, such excellent sons will be born; there is no doubt. ॥47॥
4.33.48: They will have good wives and good wealth, long life, discernment, learning and generosity, for attaining the fruits of enjoyment and liberation. ॥48॥
4.33.49: A hundred and one sons abounding in virtues will be born; such a very splendid extension of the lineage will come about. ॥49॥
4.33.50: Sūta said: Having said this, Śiva then took the form of a liṅga there, renowned by the name Ghuśmeśa, and the lake became known as Śivālaya. ॥50॥
4.33.51: Sudharmā, Ghuśmā and Sudehā came together and quickly performed a hundred and one circumambulations of Śiva. ॥51॥
4.33.52: Having worshipped Maheśa and embraced one another, and having cast off the impurity within, they attained supreme happiness there. ॥52॥
4.33.53: Seeing the son alive, Sudehā became ashamed. Having sought forgiveness from the two, O brahmins, she performed a vow that removes her own sins. ॥53॥
4.33.54: Thus, O lords of sages, did this liṅga named Ghuśmeśa come into being. By seeing it and worshipping it, happiness ever increases. ॥54॥
4.33.55: Thus I have narrated to you the series of Jyotirliṅgas, twelve in number, which grant all desires and bestow enjoyment and liberation. ॥55॥
4.33.56: Whoever reads or even hears this story of the Jyotirliṅgas is freed from all sins and obtains enjoyment and liberation. ॥56॥
4.33.iti: Thus ends the thirty-third adhyāya, named The description of the glory of the origin of the Ghuśmeśa jyotirliṅga, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥33॥
4.34.1: Vyāsa said: Having heard these words of that Sūta, the lords among sages praised him highly and spoke to him, out of a wish for the welfare of the worlds. ॥1॥
4.34.2: The sages said: O Sūta, you know everything; therefore we ask you. O lord, tell us the greatness of the Harīśvara liṅga. ॥2॥
4.34.3: We have heard before that the discus Sudarśana was obtained by Viṣṇu through worship of him; O dear one, tell us that story too in detail. ॥3॥
4.34.4: Sūta said: Listen, O best of sages, to the auspicious story of Harīśvara, from which Viṣṇu formerly obtained Sudarśana from Śaṅkara. ॥4॥
4.34.5: At a certain time the Daityas became exceedingly powerful; they oppressed the worlds and brought about the destruction of dharma. ॥5॥
4.34.6: Those gods, oppressed by the Daityas of great strength and valour, told their sorrow to Viṣṇu, the protector of the immortals. ॥6॥
4.34.7: The gods said: O lord, show compassion; we are sorely oppressed by the Daityas. Where shall we go and what shall we do? We have taken refuge in you, the giver of shelter. ॥7॥
4.34.8: Sūta said: Having heard these words of the gods, distressed in heart, Viṣṇu remembered the lotus feet of Śiva and spoke. ॥8॥
4.34.9: Viṣṇu said: O gods, I shall accomplish your task by worshipping Giriśa. These enemies are very strong indeed and must be conquered with great effort. ॥9॥
4.34.10: Sūta said: Thus addressed by the mighty Viṣṇu, all those gods, considering the wicked Daityas as already slain, went each to his own abode. ॥10॥
4.34.11: Viṣṇu, for the victory of the immortals, worshipped Śiva, the overlord of all the immortals, the witness of all, the imperishable. ॥11॥
4.34.12: Going near Kailāsa, Hari himself performed austerities, having made a fire-pit and installed the fire in front. ॥12॥
4.34.13: With the rite of the earthen liṅga, with mantras of many kinds and with numerous hymns, he joyfully worshipped Giriśa. ॥13॥
4.34.14: O lords of sages, worshipping with lotuses born from the lake called Mānasa, Hari himself, having fixed his posture there, did not move. ॥14॥
4.34.15: Until his grace is granted, I must by all means remain here. Having made this resolve, Hari worshipped Śiva. ॥15॥
4.34.16: O brahmins, when Hara did not become pleased with Hari, then the blessed Viṣṇu became absorbed in reflection. ॥16॥
4.34.17: He reflected thus in his own mind: service has been rendered in many ways, yet Hara, the grace-bestowing lord, has not become pleased. ॥17॥
4.34.18: Then Viṣṇu, greatly astonished and filled with supreme devotion, lovingly praised the Supreme Lord with a thousand names. ॥18॥
4.34.19: Uttering a name-mantra for each, he offered him a lotus, and so worshipped Śambhu, who is tender toward those who come to him for refuge. ॥19॥
4.34.20: Then, to test Viṣṇu's devotion, Śaṅkara took away one lotus from the thousand lotuses. ॥20॥
4.34.21: Viṣṇu did not perceive that wondrous act caused by Śiva's māyā; but realising that the number was short, he became intent on searching for it. ॥21॥
4.34.22: Firm in his vow, he wandered the whole earth to please him; not finding it, he of pure soul offered one of his eyes. ॥22॥
4.34.23: Seeing that, Śaṅkara, the remover of all sorrows, became pleased; he appeared right there and spoke words to Hari. ॥23॥
4.34.24: Śiva said: O Hari, I am pleased with you; ask for whatever boon you desire. I grant what your heart longs for; there is nothing that cannot be given to you. ॥24॥
4.34.25: Sūta said: Hearing those words of Śambhu, Keśava, delighted in mind and filled with great joy, spoke to Śiva with folded hands. ॥25॥
4.34.26: Viṣṇu said: What need I say before you, for you abide as the inner controller? Still, O Lord, it is spoken out of respect for your command. ॥26॥
4.34.27: The universe is oppressed by the Daityas; there is no happiness for us, O Sadāśiva. O master, my own weapon does not prevail in slaying the Daityas. ॥27॥
4.34.28: What shall I do? Where shall I go? I have no other supreme protector. Therefore, O Supreme Lord, I have come to you for refuge. ॥28॥
4.34.29: Sūta said: Having said this and bowed to Śiva, the Supreme Self, he himself, greatly afflicted, stood before Śambhu. ॥29॥
4.34.30: Sūta said: Hearing these words of Viṣṇu, Maheśvara, God of gods, gave him his own discus Sudarśana, a mass of radiance. ॥30॥
4.34.31: Obtaining it, the blessed Viṣṇu swiftly slew with that discus all those very powerful Daityas, without effort. ॥31॥
4.34.32: The world attained supreme well-being, the gods became happy, and Hari, much pleased at obtaining his weapon, was supremely joyful. ॥32॥
4.34.33: The sages said: What is that thousand-name hymn of Śaṅkara? Tell us, by which Maheśvara, being pleased, gave the discus to Hari. ॥33॥
4.34.34: Tell me its glory, together with the dialogue with Śiva, and Śambhu's compassion toward Viṣṇu, exactly as it was. ॥34॥
4.34.35: Vyāsa said: Hearing these words of those sages of purified minds, Sūta remembered the lotus feet of Śiva and spoke. ॥35॥
4.34.iti: Thus ends the thirty-fourth adhyāya, named The description of Viṣṇu's obtaining the Sudarśana discus, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥34॥
4.35.1: Sūta said: Listen, O best of sages: today I shall recite the thousand names of Śiva, by which Maheśvara was pleased. ॥1॥
4.35.2: Śrī Viṣṇu said: Śiva, Hara, Mṛḍa, Rudra, Puṣkara, the Lotus-eyed, he who is reached by those who seek, he of good conduct, Śarva, Śambhu, Maheśvara; ॥2॥

4.35.13: Dwelling in the cremation ground, the Subtle, abiding in the cremation ground, the Great Lord, maker of the worlds, lord of beasts, the great Maker, the great Remedy; ॥13॥
4.35.14: The Higher, lord of cows, the Protector, reachable by knowledge, the Primeval, Policy, good Policy, pure-souled, Soma, delighting in Soma, the Happy One; ॥14॥

4.35.23: Hard to obtain, hard to reach, the Fortress, skilled in all weapons, abiding in the yoga of the self, the fine thread, increaser of the lineage; ॥23॥

4.35.25: Unattainable, yet attainable by the good, assuming the form of a monkey-servant, golden-seeded, the Ancient, taker of the life of foes, the Mighty; ॥25॥
4.35.26: The great lake, the great abyss, praised by hosts of siddhas and gods, wearing a tiger-skin garment, adorned with serpents, the great Being, the great Treasure; ॥26॥
