4.35.116: He is the strong-spirited, the sāttvic, the one of true fame, the one who made the scriptures out of love, the unshaken, the appreciator of virtues, the many-selved, the doer of many deeds. ॥116॥
4.35.117: He is the well-pleased, the fair-faced, the subtle, the easy of access, the southern breeze, the one carried on Nandī's shoulder, the burden-bearer, the manifest, the increaser of love. ॥117॥
4.35.118: He is the unconquered, the essence of all beings, Govinda, the one whose vehicle is sattva, the unsupported, the self-supported, the perfected, the one of pure form, the one whose wealth is fame. ॥118॥
4.35.119: He is the bearer of the boar's tusk, the horned one, the mighty, the sole leader, the illuminator of the Veda, the one possessed of the Veda, the sole kinsman, the doer of many deeds. ॥119॥
4.35.120: He is the one fond of Śrī whose undertakings are auspicious, the calm and blessed, the impartial, fame, the one lying on the ground, the ornament, prosperity, the maker of beings, the sustainer of beings. ॥120॥
4.35.121: He is the Unshakable, the one whose body is devotion, the Slayer of Time, the Blue-and-Red one; the great renouncer whose vow is truth, wholly devoted to eternal peace. ॥121॥
4.35.122: He whose activity is for the sake of others, the Giver of boons, the Dispassionate, the Skilled; the Giver of good, the Doer of good, whose name is auspicious, who is himself the Auspicious. ॥122॥
4.35.123: He who asks for nothing, the Attributeless, the Witness, indeed the Non-doer, golden in splendour; good by his very nature, the Impartial one standing in the middle, the Slayer of enemies, the Destroyer of obstacles. ॥123॥
4.35.124: The one with a crest, the armoured one, the Trident-bearer, the one with matted locks, the shaven one, and the one with earrings; the Deathless, the All-seeing, the Lion, the Mass of radiance, the Great Jewel. ॥124॥
4.35.125: The Innumerable, whose self is immeasurable, the Mighty, the Knower of valour; the one to be known, whose nature is detachment, the Lord of sages both high and low. ॥125॥
4.35.126: The Unsurpassed, the Invincible, sweet and pleasing to behold; the Lord of the gods, the Refuge, the All, Brahman as sound (the Word), the goal of the good. ॥126॥
4.35.127: The one on the side of Time, the Death of Death, who has made Vāsuki into a bracelet; the great archer, the Sustainer of the earth, the Stainless, the Unfettered. ॥127॥
4.35.128: The Jewel of the sky (the sun), the Saviour, the Blessed, the Giver of accomplishments, the Means of accomplishment; enveloping on every side, the Praiseworthy, the broad-chested, the mighty-armed. ॥128॥
4.35.129: The Source of all, the Fearless, dear to Nara and Nārāyaṇa; the Untainted, whose self is beyond the manifold world, the Flawless, the Remover of defects. ॥129॥
4.35.130: The one to be praised, fond of praise, the Praiser himself, embodied as Vyāsa, the Unrestrained; whose means are faultless, the Treasury of knowledge, fond of rasa (essence/delight). ॥130॥
4.35.131: Of tranquil intellect, the Unimpaired, the Gatherer of all, ever beautiful; foremost among those clad in tiger-skin, Lord of the earth, Śākalya, Lord of the night (the moon). ॥131॥
4.35.132: The Teacher of the highest truth, Datta (the Given), the Wise one, affectionate to those who take refuge in him; Soma (united with Umā), the Knower of rasa, the Giver of rasa, the Support of all beings. ॥132॥
4.35.133: Thus with a thousand names Hari praised Hara; he entreated Śambhu and worshipped him with lotuses. ॥133॥
4.35.134: Then that playful Śambhu performed a deed, O Brahmins, most wonderful and delightful; listen to that very deed with reverence. ॥134॥
4.35.iti: Thus ends the thirty-fifth adhyāya, named The description of the thousand names of Śiva, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥35॥
4.36.1: Sūta said: Having heard the divine hymn of his own thousand names composed by Viṣṇu, adorned with supreme names, Maheśvara became pleased. ॥1॥
4.36.2: To test Hari, the Lord Maheśvara, ruler of the worlds, then hid one lotus among the lotuses. ॥2॥
4.36.3: Then, among those thousand lotuses, one was found missing; and then Viṣṇu became distressed in his worship of Śiva. ॥3॥
4.36.4: He reflected in his heart: where indeed has the lotus gone? Let what has gone be gone, gladly; is my eye not a lotus? ॥4॥
4.36.5: Resolving thus, he plucked out his eye, relying on all his fortitude, and worshipped Śiva with devotion, and praised him with it. ॥5॥
4.36.6: Then Hara, the guru of the world, seeing Hari who had praised him and was in such a state, appeared, crying out, don't, don't. ॥6॥
4.36.7: Maheśvara swiftly descended from the maṇḍala of his own earthen liṅga that had been installed by Hari. ॥7॥
4.36.8: Bowing to Śambhu, who bore the form as described and had arisen from a mass of radiance, and standing before him, he praised him in a special way. ॥8॥
4.36.9: Then Mahādeva, pleased and as if smiling, looking with compassion at Viṣṇu who stood with joined palms, spoke. ॥9॥
4.36.10: Śaṅkara said: O Hari, all this that your mind desires is known to me — especially the task of the gods, since your self is devoted to the gods' task. ॥10॥
4.36.11: For the accomplishment of the gods' task and for the destruction of the Daityas, I give you a refuge and the splendid discus named Sudarśana. ॥11॥
4.36.12: The form you have seen, which brings happiness to all the worlds and was assumed for your good, O lord of the gods — meditate on it steadfastly. ॥12॥
4.36.13: When remembered on the battlefield, it destroys the sorrows of the gods. This discus, this form, this hymn of a thousand names — ॥13॥
4.36.14: those who always listen to them with devotion will have unfailing fulfilment of all desires through my grace, O you of good vows. ॥14॥
4.36.15: Sūta said: Having said this, he gave the discus Sudarśana, brilliant as ten thousand suns, arisen from his own foot, destroyer of all enemies. ॥15॥
4.36.16: Viṣṇu too, after duly consecrating it, received it then facing north; and having bowed to Mahādeva, Viṣṇu spoke these words. ॥16॥
4.36.17: Viṣṇu said: Listen, O God: what should I meditate on and what should I recite, O Lord, for the destruction of sorrows? Tell me, O Śaṅkara, benefactor of the world. ॥17॥
4.36.18: Sūta said: Thus asked by him, Śiva, satisfied and with a pleased mind, then spoke to Viṣṇu, the helper of the gods. ॥18॥
4.36.19: Śiva said: O Hari, my form is to be meditated on for the calming of all misfortunes; for the destruction of many sorrows, recite the thousand names. ॥19॥
4.36.20: My discus is always to be borne by you with care, O Viṣṇu, for the attainment of all you desire; this indeed is the best of all discuses. ॥20॥
4.36.21: And others who will recite it or have it recited daily — sorrow does not arise for them even in a dream; there is no doubt of this. ॥21॥
4.36.22: When a crisis arising from kings has come, if a man performs a hundred recitations, complete with their accessory rites and according to rule, he obtains well-being. ॥22॥
4.36.23: This indeed destroys disease, is supreme in granting learning and wealth, bestows all desires, is holy, and always grants devotion to Śiva. ॥23॥
4.36.24: Whatever excellent fruit men here recite it with in view, they will obtain that fruit truly and in the highest degree; there is no doubt of this. ॥24॥
4.36.25: And whoever, rising early in the morning and performing my worship, recites it daily in my presence — success is not far from him. ॥25॥
4.36.26: He obtains complete worldly success fulfilling all desires, and at the end he attains liberation in the form of union (sāyujya); there is no doubt here. ॥26॥
4.36.27: Sūta said: Having thus spoken to Viṣṇu, Śaṅkara, with a delighted mind, touched him with both hands, and Giriśa spoke to him again. ॥27॥
4.36.28: Śiva said: I am the giver of boons, O best of gods; choose boons as you wish. Surely I have been won over by your devotion and by this hymn, O you of good vows. ॥28॥
4.36.29: Sūta said: Thus addressed by the God of gods, Viṣṇu, greatly delighted, bowed to that God of gods and with joined palms spoke these words. ॥29॥
4.36.30: Viṣṇu said: Just as grace is being shown now, O Lord, so too hereafter supreme grace should be shown by you, especially, out of your compassion, O master. ॥30॥
4.36.31: Devotion to you, O Mahādeva — be gracious — is the highest boon; I desire no other, since for your devotees there are no afflictions at all, O Lord. ॥31॥
4.36.32: Sūta said: Hearing those words of his, Bhava, exceedingly compassionate, touched his body, and the moon-crested one spoke. ॥32॥
4.36.33: Śiva said: O Hari, may your devotion to me always be unfailing; and be ever worthy of salutation and worship in the world, even by the gods. ॥33॥
4.36.34: Your name Viśvambhara will be supreme and remove all sins, by my grace, O best of gods; there is no doubt. ॥34॥
4.36.35: Sūta said: Having said this, Rudra, the Lord, master of all gods, vanished right there while Viṣṇu looked on, O great sages. ॥35॥
4.36.36: The blessed Janārdana too, having obtained that auspicious discus by Śaṅkara's word, rejoiced greatly in his heart. ॥36॥
4.36.37: Meditating on that form of Śambhu, he recited this hymn continually, taught it, and imparted it to devotees. ॥37॥
4.36.38: What you asked I have thus narrated, which removes the sins of those who hear it. What more, O excellent ones, do you wish to ask again? ॥38॥
4.36.iti: Thus ends the thirty-sixth adhyāya, named The description of the fruit of the hymn of the thousand names of Śiva, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥36॥
4.37.1: The sages said: O Sūta, O Sūta, most fortunate one, you are full of knowledge, O you of good vows. Tell us once more, in detail, the deeds of Śiva alone. ॥1॥
4.37.2: Tell how the ancient kings, sages and gods too performed the worship of him alone, the best of gods. ॥2॥
4.37.3: Sūta said: Well asked, O best of sages. Listen; I shall tell you the delightful story of Śaṅkara, which grants enjoyment and liberation to those who hear it. ॥3॥
4.37.4: Long ago, the Grandfather Brahmā, asked this very thing by Nārada, replied with a pleased mind to Nārada, the best of sages. ॥4॥
4.37.5: Brahmā said: Listen with great delight, O Nārada, to the excellent story of Śaṅkara, which destroys great sins; out of affection for you I shall narrate it. ॥5॥
4.37.6: Viṣṇu, together with Ramā, performed the worship of Śiva, and by the grace of the Supreme Lord he obtained all his desires. ॥6॥
4.37.7: I too, the Grandfather, am a worshipper of Śiva; by his grace alone, dear son, I am ever the creator of the universe. ॥7॥
4.37.8: My sons, the supreme sages, constantly worship Śiva; and the other sages too are worshippers of Śiva. ॥8॥
4.37.9: You, Nārada, are especially a worshipper of Śiva; the seven sages, Vasiṣṭha and the rest, are worshippers of Śiva. ॥9॥
4.37.10: Arundhatī, the great chaste lady, likewise Lopāmudrā, and Ahalyā, the wife of Gautama, are worshippers of Śiva. ॥10॥
4.37.11: Durvāsas, Kauśika, Śakti, Dadhīca and Gautama, Kaṇāda, Bhārgava, Jīva (Bṛhaspati) and Vaiśampāyana too— ॥11॥
4.37.12: all these sages are regarded as worshippers of Śiva; likewise Parāśara and Vyāsa are ever devoted to Śiva's worship. ॥12॥
4.37.13: Upamanyu is a great devotee of Śiva, the Supreme Self; Yājñavalkya is a great Śaiva, and so are Jaimini and Garga. ॥13॥
4.37.14: Śuka and Śaunaka and the others are ardent worshippers of Śaṅkara; there are many other sages too, O best of sages. ॥14॥
4.37.15: Aditi, the mother of the gods, together with her daughters-in-law, intent on love, constantly and gladly performed the worship of Śiva in an earthen liṅga. ॥15॥
4.37.16: Śakra (Indra) and the other guardians of the worlds, the Vasus and the gods, the Mahārājika gods and the Sādhyas are worshippers of Śiva. ॥16॥
4.37.17: The Gandharvas, Kinnaras and other demigods are worshippers of Śiva; likewise the great-souled asuras are regarded as worshippers of Śiva. ॥17॥
4.37.18: The Daitya Hiraṇyakaśipu, with his younger brother and his sons, O sage, constantly worshipped Śiva; so did Virocana and Bali. ॥18॥
4.37.19: Bāṇa is remembered as a great Śaiva, and likewise the sons of Hiraṇyākṣa; Vṛṣaparvan, Danu, dear son, and the Dānavas are worshippers of Śiva. ॥19॥
4.37.20: Śeṣa, Vāsuki, Takṣaka and other great serpents are devotees of Śiva, as are the birds headed by Garuḍa. ॥20॥
4.37.21: The two gods Sun and Moon, founders of dynasties on earth, are ever devoted to the service of Śiva together with their descendants, O lord of sages. ॥21॥
4.37.22: Likewise the Manus, headed by Svāyambhuva, performed the worship of Śiva in particular, wearing the garb of Śiva, O sage. ॥22॥
4.37.23: Priyavrata and his sons, and likewise the son of Uttānapāda, and the kings of their lineages were worshippers of Śiva. ॥23॥
4.37.24: Dhruva, Ṛṣabha, Bharata, the nine Yogins, their brothers and others too were worshippers of Śiva. ॥24॥
4.37.25: The sons of Vaivasvata, O Tārkṣya, the kings headed by Ikṣvāku, with minds devoted to Śiva's worship, always enjoyed happiness. ॥25॥
4.37.26: Kakutstha too, Māndhātṛ, Sagara the best of Śaivas, Mucukunda, Hariścandra and likewise Kalmāṣāṅghri— ॥26॥
4.37.27: the rulers headed by Bhagīratha, and many excellent kings, should be known as worshippers of Śiva, adopting the garb of Śiva. ॥27॥
4.37.28: The great king Khaṭvāṅga, who gave help to the gods, always worshipped an earthen image of Śiva according to the rules. ॥28॥
4.37.29: His son Dilīpa always performed the worship of Śiva; his son Raghu, a Śaiva, worshipped Śiva with great delight. ॥29॥
4.37.30: Aja was a worshipper of Śiva; his son, who fought righteous battles, was Daśaratha, born as an especially great king. ॥30॥
4.37.31: That Daśaratha, for the sake of a son, specially worshipped an earthen image of Śiva at the command of the sage Vasiṣṭha. ॥31॥
4.37.32: And that king, devoted to Bhava, the best of kings, having received the command of the sage Ṛṣyaśṛṅga, performed the sacrifice for a son (putreṣṭi). ॥32॥
4.37.33: His beloved Kausalyā, instructed by Ṛṣyaśṛṅga, joyfully worshipped an earthen image of Śaṅkara to obtain a son. ॥33॥
4.37.34: Sumitrā, and Kaikeyī the king's beloved, lovingly worshipped Śiva to obtain good sons, O best of sages. ॥34॥
4.37.35: By Śiva's grace they obtained sons who brought auspiciousness, of great valour, heroic, devoted to the righteous path, O sage. ॥35॥
4.37.36: Then, by Śiva's command, Hari himself became manifest in four forms in them the queens from that king, as the king's sons. ॥36॥
4.37.37: Kausalyā's son was Rāma, Sumitrā's Lakṣmaṇa and Śatrughna, and Kaikeyī's Bharata—all of good vows. ॥37॥
4.37.38: That Rāma, together with his brothers, constantly worshipped the earthen liṅga, wearing ash and rudrākṣa and following the Virajā rite. ॥38॥
4.37.39: The kings born in his lineage, with their followers, O sage, all worshipped the earthen liṅga of Śiva. ॥39॥
4.37.40: The great king Sudyumna, a Śaiva and son of Manu, O sage, became a woman together with his attendants through Śiva's curse, on account of Śiva's beloved. ॥40॥
4.37.41: Through worship of the Lord in the earthen liṅga (pārthiveśa), he again became an excellent man: a woman for a month and a man for a month; in this way his womanhood was partly removed. ॥41॥
4.37.42: Then, giving up the kingdom, devoted to Śiva's dharma and wearing the garb of a Śaiva, he attained through devotion the liberation that is hard to obtain. ॥42॥
4.37.43: And Purūravas, his son, a great king, was a fine worshipper of Śiva, the god of gods; his son too was a worshipper of Śiva. ॥43॥
4.37.44: Bharata always performed great worship of Śiva alone; and Nahuṣa was a great Śaiva, devoted to the worship of Śiva. ॥44॥
4.37.45: Yayāti, through worship of Śiva, obtained all his desires; he begot five sons devoted to Śiva's dharma. ॥45॥
4.37.46: His sons, headed by Yadu, all five of them, were worshippers of Śiva, and by the power of Śiva's worship they obtained all their desires. ॥46॥
4.37.47: Other highly fortunate ones too, both of their lineage and of other lineages, worshipped Śiva, the giver of enjoyment and liberation, O sage. ॥47॥
4.37.48: And Kṛṣṇa himself performed daily worship of Śiva alone on Badarī, the best of mountains, for a period of seven months. ॥48॥
4.37.49: Having obtained many divine boons from that gracious Śaṅkara, the Lord Kṛṣṇa brought the whole world under his control. ॥49॥
4.37.50: His son Pradyumna, dear one, always performed Śiva's worship; and other eminent sons of Kṛṣṇa, Sāmba and the rest, were worshippers of Śiva. ॥50॥
4.37.51: Jarāsandha was a great Śaiva, and so were the kings of his line; Nimi was a Śaiva, and Janaka and his sons were worshippers of Śiva. ॥51॥
4.37.52: And worship of Śiva was performed by Nala, the son of Vīrasena, who in a former birth was a Bhilla hunter in the forest, a protector of travellers. ॥52॥
4.37.53: Formerly he protected an ascetic near a shrine of Hara; he himself was devoured at night by tigers and other beasts and died for the sake of dharma. ॥53॥
4.37.54: By the power of that merit, that Bhilla became Nala, a great emperor, beloved of Damayantī. ॥54॥
4.37.55: Thus, dear one, sinless one, I have told you what you asked: the divine deeds of Śaṅkara. What else do you wish to ask? ॥55॥
4.37.iti: Thus ends the thirty-seventh adhyāya, named The description of the Śaiva faith of gods, sages and kings, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥37॥
4.38.1: The sages said: You are blessed, you have fulfilled your purpose, your life is fruitful, since, dear one, you make us hear the auspicious story of Maheśvara. ॥1॥
4.38.2: O Sūta, although the true matter has been heard by many sages, our doubt has not gone; therefore I put this to you. ॥2॥
4.38.3: By which vow is Śiva pleased and grants true happiness? You are skilled in matters concerning Śiva; therefore we ask you. ॥3॥
4.38.4: By which vow may devotees attain both enjoyment and liberation? Tell that in particular, O disciple of Vyāsa; salutation to you. ॥4॥
4.38.5: Sūta said: O best of sages, you compassionate ones have asked well. Remembering the lotus feet of Śiva, I shall narrate as I have heard. ॥5॥
4.38.6: Just as it is asked by you, so indeed was it asked of Śaṅkara by Brahmā, by Hari and by Śivā. ॥6॥
4.38.7: At some time it was asked by them of the Supreme Self: pleased by which vow do you grant enjoyment and liberation? ॥7॥
4.38.8: Thus was he asked then by them, by that Hari; that reply, which removes the sins of those who listen, I now narrate. ॥8॥
4.38.9: Śiva said: I have many vows that grant enjoyment and liberation; among them the principal ones should be known to be ten in number. ॥9॥
4.38.10: Those versed in the Jābāla Śruti speak of ten Śaiva vows; those vows should always be performed with effort by the twice-born. ॥10॥
4.38.11: On every eighth lunar day, eating only at night should be carefully observed; on Kālāṣṭamī especially, O Hari, eating by day is to be given up. ॥11॥
4.38.12: On the bright eleventh, O Viṣṇu, eating by day is to be given up; on the dark eleventh, O Hari, one should eat at night after worshipping me. ॥12॥
4.38.13: On the bright thirteenth, eating should be done at night; but on the dark fourteenth (bhūtā), that should not be done by observers of Śiva's vow. ॥13॥
4.38.14: On Monday, O Viṣṇu, in both fortnights, in every week, those devoted to Śiva should carefully eat at night. ॥14॥
4.38.15: In all these vows, excellent twice-born Śaivas should be fed with care, according to one's capacity, for the completion of the vow. ॥15॥
4.38.16: These vows must be observed regularly by the twice-born; twice-born who abandon these vows become thieves. ॥16॥
4.38.17: They should be performed regularly also by those skilled in the path of liberation. A set of four has been declared as that which leads to liberation: ॥17॥
4.38.18: Worship of Śiva, japa of Rudra's mantras, fasting, and death in Vārāṇasī, the abode of Śiva: this is the eternal way to liberation. ॥18॥
4.38.19: The eighth day, Monday, and the fourteenth of the dark fortnight: this pleases Śiva; there need be no deliberation about it. ॥19॥
4.38.20: Among even the four, O Hari, the Śivarātri vow is the most powerful; therefore that alone should be performed by those desiring the fruits of enjoyment and liberation. ॥20॥
4.38.21: There is nothing other than this vow that brings benefit to men; this vow is the supreme means of dharma for all. ॥21॥
4.38.22: For the desireless and the desirous, for all men likewise, for the classes and the life-stages, and for women and children, O Hari, ॥22॥
4.38.23: for male and female servants, and likewise for gods and others, for all embodied beings, this excellent vow is beneficial. ॥23॥
4.38.24: In the dark fortnight of Māgha, that fourteenth is proclaimed as especially distinguished; the one extending through midnight should be adopted; it destroys crores of sins of killing. ॥24॥
4.38.25: Hear, O Keśava, with attention, what is to be done on that day beginning from morning; I tell it to you with great affection. ॥25॥
4.38.26: Rising in the morning, the wise one, filled with supreme bliss, should diligently perform the daily duties such as bathing. ॥26॥
4.38.27: Then, going to a Śiva temple and worshipping according to rule, and bowing to Śiva, he should afterwards properly make the resolve. ॥27॥
4.38.28: O God of gods, Mahādeva, Nīlakaṇṭha, salutation to you. O Lord, I wish to perform your Śivarātri vow. ॥28॥
4.38.29: By your power, O Lord of gods, may it be without obstacles; may the enemies, desire and the rest, cause me no affliction at all. ॥29॥
4.38.30: Having made the resolve thus, he should gather the articles of worship. And the liṅga that is in an excellent place and renowned in the Āgamas — ॥30॥
4.38.31: going there himself at night and carrying out the excellent procedure, on the southern side of Śiva, or on the western, in an auspicious spot, ॥31॥
4.38.32: and placing those articles for worship near Śiva, the excellent man should then bathe again there according to rule. ॥32॥
4.38.33: Wearing a clean garment and likewise a clean undergarment, and sipping water three times, he should begin the worship. ॥33॥
4.38.34: Whatever article belongs to a given mantra, with that mantra he should perform the worship; the worship of Hara should not be done without mantras. ॥34॥
4.38.35: Having performed worship in the first watch with songs, instrumental music and dances imbued with devotion, the wise one should repeat the mantra. ॥35॥
4.38.36: If he knows the mantras, he should then make an excellent earthen liṅga; having completed his daily rites, he should afterwards worship the earthen liṅga. ॥36॥
4.38.37: First making the earthen liṅga, he should afterwards perform its installation, and please the bull-bannered God with hymns of various kinds. ॥37॥
4.38.38: The glorification arising from the vow should be recited by the wise one and listened to by the excellent devotee, desiring the completion of the vow. ॥38॥
4.38.39: And in all four watches, worshipping the set of four forms in order, beginning with invocation and ending with dismissal, ॥39॥
4.38.40: A night vigil should be kept with love, accompanied by a great festival. In the morning, having bathed, he should again install Śiva there and worship him. ॥40॥
4.38.41: Then, with bowed shoulders and joined palms, having completed the vow and bowing to him again and again, he should earnestly pray to Śambhu: ॥41॥
4.38.42: O Mahādeva, the observance that was undertaken at your command is now released by me, O Lord; the vow has been accomplished, unsurpassed. ॥42॥
4.38.43: By this vow, O Lord of gods, performed according to my ability, be pleased today, O Śarva, and show compassion upon me. ॥43॥
4.38.44: Having offered a handful of flowers to Śiva, he should give gifts according to rule; and having bowed to Śiva, he should conclude that observance. ॥44॥
4.38.45: According to his ability, having fed Śaiva brahmins and especially ascetics and having fully satisfied them, he himself should then take food. ॥45॥
4.38.46: How worship is to be performed by the best devotees in each watch of the night, O Hari, especially on Śivarātri — that I shall tell you. ॥46॥
4.38.47: In the first watch, O Hari, he should worship the installed earthen liṅga with supreme devotion and with many excellent offerings. ॥47॥
4.38.48: Hara is always to be worshipped first with the five substances; he should offer each substance separately with its own mantra. ॥48॥
4.38.49: Having offered that substance, he should pour a stream of water; and afterwards the wise one should wash off the substances with streams of water. ॥49॥
4.38.50: Having recited the mantra one hundred and eight times with a stream of water, he should worship Śiva there, who is without attributes yet takes the form of attributes. ॥50॥
4.38.51: He should worship the bull-bannered god with the mantra given by his guru; otherwise he should worship Sadāśiva with the name-mantra. ॥51॥
4.38.52: Worship of Śambhu, the supreme Self, should be done with variegated sandal-paste, with unbroken rice grains, and with black sesame seeds. ॥52॥
4.38.53: With flowers — hundred-petalled lotuses and also oleanders — he should offer the flowers to Śaṅkara with eight name-mantras. ॥53॥
4.38.54: Bhava, Śarva, Rudra, then Paśupati, Ugra, Mahān, Bhīma and Īśāna — these indeed are they. ॥54॥
4.38.55: He should worship Śiva with these names preceded by Śrī and ending in the dative; afterwards offer incense and lamp, and after that the food-offering. ॥55॥
4.38.56: In the first watch the wise one should have cooked food prepared as the food-offering; having given arghya and a bilva fruit, he should offer betel. ॥56॥
4.38.57: Then prostration, then meditation; japa of the guru's mantra is prescribed; otherwise he should please Śaṅkara with the five-syllabled mantra. ॥57॥
4.38.58: Then, having shown the cow-gesture (dhenu-mudrā), he should perform a libation with pure water, and arrange the feeding of five brahmins according to his means. ॥58॥
4.38.59: A great festival should be held here as long as the watch lasts; then, having offered the fruit of the worship to him, he should conclude it. ॥59॥
4.38.60: Again, in the second watch he should duly make the resolve (saṅkalpa); or, having made the resolve only once, he should perform worship of that same kind. ॥60॥
4.38.61: Having likewise worshipped with the previous substances, he should offer the stream of water; reciting the mantra twice as many times as before, he should worship Śiva. ॥61॥
4.38.62: Then he should worship Śiva with the previous items, sesame and barley, and with lotuses; especially with bilva leaves should he worship the Supreme Lord. ॥62॥
4.38.63: The arghya is to be made with a citron, and the food-offering likewise with milk-rice; and the repetition of the mantra twice that of before, O Janārdana. ॥63॥
4.38.64: Then he should make the resolve to feed brahmins, and do everything else likewise up to the end of the second watch. ॥64॥
4.38.65: When the third watch has come, he should perform worship as before; but in place of barley, wheat, and flowers of the arka plant. ॥65॥
4.38.66: He should worship there with various incenses and lamps of many kinds, O Viṣṇu, with food-offerings of cakes and with vegetables of many kinds. ॥66॥
4.38.67: Having done thus, he should then perform the rite of ārati with camphor; he should give arghya with a pomegranate and perform double the japa. ॥67॥
4.38.68: Then he should make the resolve for feeding brahmins, with gifts of fees (dakṣiṇā), and hold a festival as before until the limit of the watch is reached. ॥68॥
4.38.69: When the fourth watch has arrived, he should perform its concluding rite; and having again performed the preliminary procedure and the rest, he should carry out the worship according to rule. ॥69॥
4.38.70: With black gram, foxtail millet and green gram, or else with the seven grains, with śaṅkhī flowers and bilva leaves, he should worship the Supreme Lord. ॥70॥
4.38.71: There he should give the food-offering with various sweets; or else he should please Sadāśiva with dishes of black gram. ॥71॥
4.38.72: He should give arghya with the fruit of the plantain, O Hari, or else give arghya to Śiva with various fruits. ॥72॥
4.38.73: The best of men should perform mantra-japa double that of before; the wise one should make the resolve for feeding brahmins according to his ability. ॥73॥
4.38.74: With songs, instrumental music and dances he should pass the time devoutly, with great festivities and with devotees, until dawn breaks. ॥74॥
4.38.75: When sunrise has come, having bathed again, he should worship Śiva, and then perform an excellent ablution of the deity with various offerings of worship. ॥75॥
4.38.76: Various kinds of gifts and various kinds of food should be given to brahmins and ascetics in accordance with the number of watches. ॥76॥
4.38.77: Having bowed to Śaṅkara, he should then offer a handful of flowers; and the discerning one, having uttered fine praises, should pray with these mantras: ॥77॥
4.38.78: I am yours; my life-breath rests in you; my mind is always on you, O Mṛḍa. O treasure of compassion, knowing this, do as is fitting. ॥78॥
4.38.79: Whatever japa, worship and the like I have done, whether in ignorance or with knowledge — since you are a treasure of compassion, take it as known, O Lord of beings, and be gracious to me. ॥79॥
4.38.80: Whatever fruit has arisen from this very fast, by that may the god Śaṅkara, the giver of happiness, be pleased. ॥80॥
4.38.81: O Mahādeva, may there always be worship of you in my family. May there be no birth in the family of one where you are not the deity worshipped. ॥81॥
4.38.82: Having thus offered a handful of flowers, one should receive the tilaka mark and blessings from the brāhmaṇas, and then one should ceremonially dismiss Śambhu. ॥82॥
4.38.83: Hara is certainly not far from the one by whom the vow has been performed in this way. Its fruit cannot be described; there is nothing that I would not give to him. ॥83॥
4.38.84: Even if this supreme vow is performed effortlessly, without deliberate intent, the seed of liberation is surely produced for that person; there is no doubt about this. ॥84॥
4.38.85: The vow should also be performed every month by people with devotion; afterwards, having carried out the rite of concluding the vow (udyāpana), one obtains the complete fruit. ॥85॥
4.38.86: Certainly, because of the performance of the vow, I, Śiva, the destroyer of all sorrows, give enjoyment and liberation, and every desired fruit. ॥86॥
4.38.87: Sūta said: Having heard these words of Śiva, most beneficial and wonderful, Viṣṇu went to his abode. Thereafter he practised this excellent vow and made this very vow known among people devoted to their own welfare. ॥87॥
4.38.88: Then, on one occasion, Keśava narrated to Nārada this divine Śivarātri vow, which grants enjoyment and liberation. ॥88॥
4.38.iti: Thus ends the thirty-eighth adhyāya, named The exposition of the greatness of the Śivarātri vow, in the Māhātmya of Vyādheśvara, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥38॥
4.39.1: The sages said: Tell us also the procedure for the concluding rite (udyāpana) of the Śivarātri vow, by performing which Śaṅkara himself surely becomes pleased. ॥1॥
4.39.2: Sūta said: Listen, O sages, with devotion and respect, to that concluding rite, by whose performance the vow surely becomes complete. ॥2॥
4.39.3: The auspicious Śivarātri vow should be observed for fourteen years: a single meal on the thirteenth lunar day and fasting on the fourteenth. ॥3॥
4.39.4: When the day of Śivarātri arrives, having completed the daily rites, then going to the Śiva temple and performing worship according to rule, ॥4॥
4.39.5: and then he should carefully have a divine maṇḍala made there, renowned in the three worlds by the name Gaurītilaka. ॥5॥
4.39.6: In its middle he should have the divine Liṅgatobhadra maṇḍala drawn, or else he should arrange a Sarvatobhadra maṇḍala inside the pavilion. ॥6॥
4.39.7: There pitchers should be prepared, as designated for the Prājāpatya rite, auspicious, with cloths, with fruits, and accompanied by fees (dakṣiṇā). ॥7॥
4.39.8: They should be carefully placed beside the maṇḍala, and in the middle one more pitcher, golden or otherwise, should be set up. ॥8॥
4.39.9: There the observer of the vow should make a golden image of Śambhu together with Umā, of one pala of gold, or half that, or according to his means. ॥9॥
4.39.10: Placing the image of Śivā on the left side and mine, the image of Śiva, on the right side, he should diligently worship at night. ॥10॥
4.39.11: There he should choose a pure ācārya together with officiating priests (ṛtvij), and, permitted by them, he should perform Śiva's worship with devotion. ॥11॥
4.39.12: He should keep vigil at night, performing the worship proper to each watch (yāma); the observer should pass the whole night with singing, dancing and the like. ॥12॥
4.39.13: Having thus worshipped duly and gratified the Lord, in the morning he should again perform worship and then perform the fire-offering (homa) according to rule. ॥13॥
4.39.14: According to his ability he should perform the Prājāpatya observance; he should feed brāhmaṇas with affection and give gifts with devotion. ॥14॥
4.39.15: Having adorned the officiating priests together with their wives with clothes, ornaments and decorations according to rule, he should give gifts to each separately. ॥15॥
4.39.16: He should give to the ācārya, according to rule, a cow with her calf, furnished with the proper accessories, saying: may Śiva be pleased with me. ॥16॥
4.39.17: Then he should offer to the ācārya that image together with the pitcher, clothed, set upon a bull, with all ornaments. ॥17॥
4.39.18: Then, with joined palms and bowed shoulders, with great love and a voice choked with emotion, he should pray to the god Maheśāna, the great Lord: ॥18॥
4.39.19: O God of gods, O Mahādeva, affectionate to those who seek refuge, O Lord of gods, through this vow show compassion upon me. ॥19॥
4.39.20: O Śiva, I have performed this vow according to the measure of my devotion; whatever is deficient, may it attain completeness by your grace, O Śaṅkara. ॥20॥
4.39.21: Whether out of ignorance or with knowledge, whatever japa, worship and so on I have done, may that by your compassion be fruitful, O Śaṅkara. ॥21॥
4.39.22: Having thus offered a handful of flowers to Śiva, the supreme Self, he should then make obeisance and pray once again. ॥22॥
4.39.23: For one who has performed the vow in this way, there is no deficiency; he then obtains the accomplishment desired by his mind—there is no doubt about this. ॥23॥
4.39.iti: Thus ends the thirty-ninth adhyāya, named The concluding rite of the Śivarātri vow, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥39॥
4.40.1: The sages said: O Sūta, having heard your words we have attained supreme bliss. Kindly narrate in detail that same excellent vow. ॥1॥
4.40.2: O Sūta, by whom was this excellent vow performed here in former times? And having performed it even unknowingly, what excellent fruit was obtained? ॥2॥
4.40.3: Sūta said: Listen, all you sages: I shall narrate the ancient history of a Niṣāda, which destroys all sins. ॥3॥
4.40.4: Formerly in a forest there was a certain Bhilla named Gurudruha—a householder with a family, strong, cruel, and devoted to cruel deeds. ॥4॥
4.40.5: Going constantly into the forest, he used to kill deer every day; and living in the forest, he committed various kinds of theft there. ॥5॥
4.40.6: From childhood onward he never did anything auspicious here. A long time passed for that wicked one in the forest. ॥6॥
4.40.7: Once the auspicious Śivarātri arrived there, but the wicked one, dwelling in the great forest, did not know of it. ॥7॥
4.40.8: At this time the Bhilla was implored by his mother, father and wife, overcome with hunger: give us food, O forest-dweller. ॥8॥
4.40.9: Thus implored, he too quickly took up his bow and went off to kill deer, and roamed the whole forest. ॥9॥
4.40.10: By the turn of fate, he then obtained nothing at all. Then the sun set, and he became distressed. ॥10॥
4.40.11: What should I do? Where should I go? I have obtained nothing today. And the children who are at home—what will become of them, and of my parents? ॥11॥
4.40.12: And my wife—something bad will happen to her. I must go home only after getting something; it cannot be otherwise. ॥12॥
4.40.13: Having reflected thus, the hunter went near a lake, to the spot where animals descend to the water, and stationed himself there. ॥13॥
4.40.14: Surely some creature will come here. Having killed it, I will go home happily, my task accomplished. ॥14॥
4.40.15: Thinking thus, the Bhilla took some water, climbed a tree called bilva, and stayed there. ॥15॥
4.40.16: When will something come? When shall I kill it? Fixing his mind thus, he stayed there, afflicted by hunger and thirst. ॥16॥
4.40.17: That night, in the first watch, a doe came, tormented by thirst and frightened, leaping about. ॥17॥
4.40.18: Seeing her, he, delighted, then quickly fitted an arrow onto his own bow in order to kill her. ॥18॥
4.40.19: As he was doing this, water and bilva leaves fell down there; below was a Śiva-liṅga. ॥19॥
4.40.20: Thus the worship of Śiva for the first watch took place, and by its greatness his sin then melted away. ॥20॥
4.40.21: Hearing that sound there, the doe, in fear, saw the hunter and, agitated, spoke these words. ॥21॥
4.40.22: The doe said: What do you wish to do, hunter? Tell the truth before me. Hearing the doe's words, the hunter spoke. ॥22॥
4.40.23: The hunter said: My family is hungry today; by killing you I shall satisfy them. Hearing those cruel words and seeing that relentless wretch, ॥23॥
4.40.24: she thought: what shall I do? Where shall I go? I must devise a plan. Having reflected thus, she spoke these words there. ॥24॥
4.40.25: The doe said: May there be gratification for you through my flesh, the flesh of a body that is otherwise useless. What merit could be greater? I am blessed, there is no doubt of it. ॥25॥
4.40.26: The merit that arises here for one who does a kindness to others cannot be described even in hundreds of years. ॥26॥
4.40.27: But my children are all in my own dwelling today. After entrusting them to my sister or else to my husband, I shall come. ॥27॥
4.40.28: Know that my word is not false, O forest-dweller. I shall come back here again near you; there is no doubt. ॥28॥
4.40.29: By truth the earth stands firm, by truth the ocean, by truth the streams of water; on truth everything is established. ॥29॥
4.40.30: Sūta said: When, though addressed thus by her, the hunter did not accept her words, then she, greatly astonished and afraid, spoke again. ॥30॥
4.40.31: The doe said: Listen, hunter, I shall declare it; I swear an oath: if, having gone to my home, I do not come back to you, ॥31॥
4.40.32: the sin of a brāhmaṇa who sells the Veda, of one who omits the sandhyā rites at the three times of day, of women who perform rites in transgression of their husband's command, ॥32॥
4.40.33: the sin that lies in an ingrate, the sin in one averse to Hari, the sin of a traitor, the sin in violating dharma, ॥33॥
4.40.34: and that in a betrayer of trust, and likewise in a deceiver—with that sin may I be smeared if I do not come back. ॥34॥
4.40.35: When the doe, having sworn these and many other oaths, stood there, then the hunter, trusting her, said, go home. ॥35॥
4.40.36: The doe, delighted, drank water and went to her own dwelling place. Meanwhile the first watch passed for him without sleep. ॥36॥
4.40.37: Then her sister, also a doe, anxious about her, came searching for her path and seeking water. ॥37॥
4.40.38: Seeing her, the Bhilla himself drew back the arrow, and again water and leaves fell upon Śiva. ॥38॥
4.40.39: Thereby, incidentally, the worship of the great-souled Śambhu for the second watch took place, bringing happiness to the hunter. ॥39॥
4.40.40: Seeing him, that doe said, what are you doing, forest-dweller? He told her as before, and hearing that, the doe spoke again. ॥40॥
4.40.41: The doe said: I am blessed; listen, O hunter: my bearing of a body is fruitful, for through this impermanent body a benefit to another will come about. ॥41॥
4.40.42: But my young ones, my little children, are staying at home. Having entrusted them to my husband, I will surely come back again. ॥42॥
4.40.43: The hunter said: I do not believe what you have said; I will kill you, there is no doubt about it. Hearing that, the doe spoke, swearing an oath by Hari. ॥43॥
4.40.44: The doe said: Listen, O hunter, I shall declare: if I do not come back again, may I incur this: whoever wavers from his spoken word loses by that his merit. ॥44॥
4.40.45: The man who abandons his wedded wife and goes to another woman; and he who, transgressing the Vedic dharma, proceeds by a self-invented path; ॥45॥
4.40.46: he who, endowed with devotion to Viṣṇu, reviles Śiva; and he who, reaching the death-anniversary of his parents, lets it pass empty of rites here; ॥46॥
4.40.47: and he who, having caused distress, again makes false promises — with that sin may I be smeared, if I do not come back again. ॥47॥
4.40.48: Sūta said: Thus addressed by her, the hunter said to the doe, go. And the doe, having drunk water, went joyfully to her own dwelling. ॥48॥
4.40.49: Meanwhile the second watch of the night passed for him without sleep. At this time, when the third watch had arrived there, ॥49॥
4.40.50: realising the delay, alarmed, and intent on searching for her, in that watch he then saw a stag that had come along the path to the water. ॥50॥
4.40.51: Seeing that well-fed stag, the forest-dweller was delighted; fixing an arrow on his bow, he set about killing it. ॥51॥
4.40.52: Then, as he was doing so, O brahmins, by the force of his destiny some bilva leaves fell upon Śiva. ॥52॥
4.40.53: Thereby, that night, through his good fortune, the worship of Śiva for the third watch took place; Śiva's compassion was shown. ॥53॥
4.40.54: Hearing that sound there, the stag said, what are you doing? He replied, I am a hunter, and I will kill you for the sake of my family. ॥54॥
4.40.55: Hearing the hunter's words, the stag, glad at heart, quickly spoke these words to that hunter: ॥55॥
4.40.56: The deer said: I am blessed, being well-fed today; your satisfaction will come about. He whose body is not for the benefit of others — all of his life has passed in vain. ॥56॥
4.40.57: He who, though possessed of ability, does not do good to others — that ability of his becomes useless, and in the hereafter he goes to hell. ॥57॥
4.40.58: But having entrusted my own young ones to their mother and having comforted all those little ones, I will come back again. ॥58॥
4.40.59: Thus addressed by him, the hunter, greatly astonished in mind, his mind a little purified and his mass of sins destroyed, spoke these words: ॥59॥
4.40.60: The hunter said: Whoever came here, all of them, speaking just as you do, went away from here — and the deceivers have not come back even now. ॥60॥
4.40.61: You too, caught in a predicament, will go off with a falsehood. How, O deer, will my livelihood come about today? ॥61॥
4.40.62: The stag said: listen, O hunter, I shall declare: there is no untruth in me. By truth the whole universe, moving and unmoving, stands firm. ॥62॥
4.40.63: He whose speech is false — his merit drains away in a moment. Even so, O Bhil, hear my true vow: ॥63॥
4.40.64: the sin in sexual union at twilight or by day, in eating on Śivarātri, in false testimony, in seizing a deposit, and likewise that of a twice-born devoid of the sandhyā rites; ॥64॥
4.40.65: of one whose mouth is devoid of Śiva's name; of one who, though able, is no benefactor; in plucking bilva fruit on a festival day; in eating forbidden food; ॥65॥
4.40.66: and he who, without worshipping Śiva and without wearing sacred ash, eats food — may the sin of all these be mine, if I do not come back again. ॥66॥
4.40.67: Sūta said: Hearing his words thus, the hunter said, go, and come back quickly. Thus addressed by the hunter, the stag drank water and went away. ॥67॥
4.40.68: They all, having made firm pledges, met there in their own dwelling, and heard that whole account from one another properly. ॥68॥
4.40.69: Bound by the noose of truth, resolving, we must certainly go, they comforted the young ones there and then became eager to go. ॥69॥
4.40.70: The elder doe there spoke to her lord: without you, O stag, how will the young ones remain here? ॥70॥
4.40.71: It was I who first made the vow there, O lord; therefore I must go. Let you two stay here. ॥71॥
4.40.72: Hearing her words, the younger one said: I am your servant; I will go today. Let you stay. ॥72॥
4.40.73: Hearing that, the stag said: I will go there. You two should stay here, for the protection of the young comes from the mother. ॥73॥
4.40.74: Hearing their lord's words, the two did not consider it in accord with dharma; lovingly they said to their husband: Fie on living in widowhood! ॥74॥
4.40.75: Having comforted the young ones there and entrusted them to their fellow dwellers, they all went swiftly to where the excellent hunter was. ॥75॥
4.40.76: Those young ones too, all of them, seeing this, followed after, thinking: whatever fate befalls these, let that be ours too. ॥76॥
4.40.77: Seeing them, the hunter, delighted, fixed an arrow on his bow; and again water and leaves fell upon Śiva. ॥77॥
4.40.78: Thereby the auspicious worship of the fourth watch took place, and then all his sin was reduced to ashes in a moment. ॥78॥
4.40.79: The doe, the other doe, and the stag said: quickly, O best of hunters, make our bodies meaningful; show us this kindness. ॥79॥
4.40.80: Hearing their words, the hunter was filled with wonder; through the power of the worship of Śiva he attained rare knowledge. ॥80॥
4.40.81: Blessed indeed are these deer, though devoid of knowledge, and worthy of high esteem: they are devoted to helping others with their very own bodies. ॥81॥
4.40.82: Having obtained birth as a human, what have I accomplished now? By tormenting the bodies of others I have nourished my own body. ॥82॥
4.40.83: I have always sustained my family by committing sins in many ways. Alas, having committed sins thus, what will be my fate? ॥83॥
4.40.84: Or to what destination shall I go, having committed sin since birth? Now I reflect thus: fie, fie upon my life! ॥84॥
4.40.85: Having thus attained knowledge, he then withdrew his arrow and said, go, O best of deer; you are blessed. ॥85॥
4.40.86: When he had spoken thus, Śaṅkara, pleased, then revealed his revered form, the very one that had been worshipped. ॥86॥
4.40.87: Touching the hunter out of compassion, Śambhu said to him lovingly: ask for a boon; I am pleased with this vow, O Bhilla. ॥87॥
4.40.88: The hunter, seeing Śiva's form, became liberated in an instant and fell at Śiva's feet, saying, I have obtained everything. ॥88॥
4.40.89: Śiva too, very pleased at heart, gave him the name Guha, and, looking at him with a compassionate glance, bestowed divine boons upon him. ॥89॥
4.40.90: Śiva said: Listen, O hunter: from today enjoy divine pleasures as you wish, residing in the excellent royal capital at Śṛṅgaverapura. ॥90॥
4.40.91: Your lineage will grow without decline, and you will be praiseworthy even to the gods. Rāma will certainly come to your house, O hunter. ॥91॥
4.40.92: He, who shows affection to my devotees, will make friendship with you. With your mind devoted to my service, you will attain liberation, hard to obtain. ॥92॥
4.40.93: Sūta said: Meanwhile, those deer, having had the vision of Śaṅkara, all bowed and attained true liberation from the deer-birth. ॥93॥
4.40.94: Mounting an aerial chariot, they departed then with divine bodies; freed from the curse by the mere sight of Śiva, they went to heaven. ॥94॥
4.40.95: Śiva became Vyādheśvara on the mountain Arbudācala, who by being seen and worshipped immediately grants enjoyment and liberation. ॥95॥
4.40.96: And the hunter too, O best of brāhmaṇas, from that day on surely enjoyed pleasures, obtained Rāma's grace, and attained union with Śiva (śiva-sāyujya). ॥96॥
4.40.97: He attained union with Śiva by performing this vow unknowingly; how much more, then, do those endowed with devotion attain auspicious identity with him. ॥97॥
4.40.98: Having examined all the scriptures and the many forms of dharma, this Śivarātri vow has been declared the most excellent of all. ॥98॥
4.40.99: Various vows here, various holy places, wondrous gifts, and various sacrifices likewise, ॥99॥
4.40.100: various austerities and many recitations of mantras—these do not attain equality with this Śivarātri vow. ॥100॥
4.40.101: Therefore this most auspicious, divine Śivarātri vow, ever granting enjoyment and liberation, should be performed by those who desire their welfare. ॥101॥
4.40.102: All this has been narrated: the auspicious Śivarātri vow, renowned as the king of vows. What else do you wish to hear? ॥102॥
4.40.iti: Thus ends the fortieth adhyāya, named The description of the glory of the Śivarātri vow, in the Māhātmya of Vyādheśvara, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥40॥
4.41.1: The sages said: You have spoken of what is called liberation (mukti). What indeed happens in it here? And what kind of state would there be in it? Tell us this. ॥1॥
4.41.2: Sūta said: Liberation is declared to be of four kinds; listen, I shall tell you. It removes the afflictions of worldly existence and bestows supreme bliss. ॥2॥
4.41.3: They are Sārūpya and Sālokya, and likewise Sānnidhya, the next; and the fourth is Sāyujya — the one that would come about through this vow. ॥3॥
4.41.4: O best of sages, Śiva alone is said to be the giver of liberation. Brahmā and the others are not to be known as such; they are only givers of the three aims of life. ॥4॥
4.41.5: Brahmā and the others are lords of the three guṇas; Śiva is beyond the three guṇas. He is changeless, the supreme Brahman, the Fourth (turya), beyond Prakṛti. ॥5॥
4.41.6: He is of the form of knowledge, imperishable, the witness, reachable through knowledge, non-dual by himself. Here he is the giver of liberation as kaivalya, and indeed also the bestower of the three aims. ॥6॥
4.41.7: And the fifth, called Kaivalya, is in every way difficult for men to attain. I shall describe its characteristics; listen, O best of seers. ॥7॥
4.41.8: That from which everything arises, by which this world is sustained, into which it dissolves, and by which all this is pervaded — ॥8॥
4.41.9: that alone is declared to be the form of Śiva, O lords of sages. It is described in the Vedas as twofold: with parts (sakala) and without parts (niṣkala). ॥9॥
4.41.10: It was not known by Viṣṇu, nor likewise by Brahmā; it was not known by Kumāra and the others, nor indeed was it known by Nārada; ॥10॥
4.41.11: nor by Śuka the son of Vyāsa, nor by Vyāsa, nor by the lords of sages, nor by all the gods before them, nor by the Vedas and the śāstras. ॥11॥
4.41.12: It is Truth, Knowledge, and Infinite, designated as Being-Consciousness-Bliss. He is without qualities, without limiting adjuncts, imperishable, pure, and stainless. ॥12॥
4.41.13: He is not red, nor yellow, not white nor blue; not short nor long, not gross nor subtle. ॥13॥
4.41.14: That from which words turn back, together with the mind, without reaching it — that alone is declared the supreme, the Brahman itself, which is called Śiva. ॥14॥
4.41.15: Just as space is all-pervading, so too is this all-pervading: beyond Māyā, the supreme Self, beyond the pairs of opposites, free from envy. ॥15॥
4.41.16: Its attainment surely comes about here through the dawning of the knowledge of Śiva, or else, O twice-born, through worship of Śiva alone with the subtle understanding of the virtuous. ॥16॥
4.41.17: Knowledge is difficult in the world, while worship is considered easy. Therefore, O best ones, worship Śiva, even for the sake of liberation. ॥17॥
4.41.18: For Śiva, whose very self is knowledge, the supreme giver of liberation, is subject to worship. Through devotion alone many perfected ones have joyfully attained the supreme liberation. ॥18॥
4.41.19: Devotion to Śambhu is the mother of knowledge, ever bestowing liberation and enjoyment. It becomes easy to attain through his grace, and is marked by the sprouting of true love. ॥19॥
4.41.20: That devotion should be known as of various kinds, O twice-born: with qualities (saguṇa) and without qualities (nirguṇa); prescribed (vaidhī) and natural (svābhāvikī). Whichever is the better, that is regarded as the higher. ॥20॥
4.41.21: It is declared twofold by the division into steadfast (naiṣṭhikī) and non-steadfast (anaiṣṭhikī). The steadfast should be known as sixfold; the second is held to be of one kind. ॥21॥
4.41.22: The wise know it to be manifold through the division into enjoined and not enjoined; and because both of these are of many kinds, their full extent is not described here. ॥22॥
4.41.23: Both of these should be known as having nine limbs, by the divisions beginning with hearing (śravaṇa). They are very difficult without his grace, and easy through it. ॥23॥
4.41.24: Devotion and knowledge have been described by Śambhu as not different, O twice-born. Therefore no distinction should be made between them; for one who practises it there is always happiness. ॥24॥
4.41.25: O twice-born, true knowledge never arises for one opposed to devotion. For one who practises devotion to Śambhu, the dawning of knowledge comes swiftly. ॥25॥
4.41.26: Therefore, O lords of sages, devotion to Maheśa should be cultivated. Through it alone everything will be accomplished; there is no doubt. ॥26॥
4.41.27: Thus what you asked, that very thing I have told. Hearing it, one is freed from all sins; there is no doubt about this. ॥27॥
4.41.iti: Thus ends the forty-first adhyāya, named The exposition of liberation, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥41॥
4.42.1: The sages said: Who is Śiva, who is Hari, who is Rudra, and who is Vidhi (Brahmā)? Among these, who is the one without attributes? Cut away this doubt of ours. ॥1॥
4.42.2: Sūta said: That which arose in the very beginning from the attributeless Supreme Self — that alone, the knowers of the Veda and Vedānta know, bears the name Śiva. ॥2॥
4.42.3: From that arose Prakṛti, joined with Puruṣa. By those two austerity was performed there, in the primordial water, O wise one. ॥3॥
4.42.4: That place is Kāśī, renowned as Pañcakrośī, dearest above all; and that water, spreading in every direction, pervaded this whole universe. ॥4॥
4.42.5: Having come into being, Hari, united with Māyā, slept there; he is renowned as Nārāyaṇa, and Māyā is regarded as Nārāyaṇī. ॥5॥
4.42.6: He who was born in the lotus of his navel is the Grandfather (Brahmā). The one seen by him through that very austerity is called Viṣṇu. ॥6॥
4.42.7: O wise ones, the form shown by the attributeless Śiva to settle the dispute of those two is renowned as Mahādeva. ॥7॥
4.42.8: By him it was declared: I, Śambhu, shall come forth from the forehead of Brahmā. He is renowned by the name Rudra, the bestower of grace upon the worlds. ॥8॥
4.42.9: For the sake of meditation by all, the formless one became endowed with form; he is Śiva himself, who shows tender love to his devotees. ॥9॥
4.42.10: Between Śiva, who stands apart from the three guṇas, and Rudra, the abode of the guṇas, there is in reality no difference, just as between gold and an ornament made of it. ॥10॥
4.42.11: The two are alike in form and deeds, alike grant the goal to devotees, are alike worthy of service by all, and sport in many divine plays. ॥11॥
4.42.12: Rudra, of fierce valour, is in every way of the very form of Śiva; he arose for the sake of the devotees' tasks, giving help to Hari and Brahmā. ॥12॥
4.42.13: The others who have arisen go to dissolution in due order; Rudra does not do so — Rudra merges into Śiva. ॥13॥
4.42.14: These created beings, on uniting with Rudra, pass into him; but Rudra, on meeting them, does not pass into them — such is the teaching of the Śruti. ॥14॥
4.42.15: All indeed worship Rudra; Rudra worships no one. Yet out of love for his devotees he sometimes, of his own accord, does worship them. ॥15॥
4.42.16: Those who constantly worship another deity attain absorption into him; through that very deity they reach Rudra after a long time, O wise ones. ॥16॥
4.42.17: But whoever are devotees of Rudra attain Śiva-hood at that very moment; they have no dependence on anyone else — this is the eternal Śruti. ॥17॥
4.42.18: Ignorance is manifold; true knowledge is not manifold. I shall explain its nature; listen attentively, O twice-born ones. ॥18॥
4.42.19: Whatever is seen here, from Brahmā down to a blade of grass — all that is Śiva alone; the notion of multiplicity is false. ॥19॥
4.42.20: Before creation Śiva is declared to exist; in the midst of creation likewise Śiva; at the end of creation Śiva is declared; when all is void, there is Sadāśiva. ॥20॥
4.42.21: Therefore, O lords of sages, Śiva alone is called fourfold; he alone is to be known as possessing attributes; and because he possesses Śakti, he is also twofold. ॥21॥
4.42.22: It was he who gave to Viṣṇu all the eternal Vedas, the many letters and prosodic measures, the meditation on himself, and his worship. ॥22॥
4.42.23: He is the Lord of all branches of knowledge — this is the eternal Śruti. Therefore Śambhu is called the maker of the Veda and the lord of the Veda. ॥23॥
4.42.24: He himself is Śaṅkara, the bestower of grace on all; creator, sustainer and destroyer, the witness — he is indeed without attributes. ॥24॥
4.42.25: For others there is a measure of time, but for Time itself there is no reckoning. He himself is Mahākāla, in direct union with Mahākālī. ॥25॥
4.42.26: And thus the Brāhmaṇas speak of Rudra, and likewise of Kālī. From those two, then, everything has come forth through their will, in their true divine play. ॥26॥
4.42.27: There is none who brings him into being, nor any sustainer or destroyer of him. He himself is the cause of all; Acyuta and the others are effects. ॥27॥
4.42.28: He himself is the cause, and never an effect of himself. Though one, he has become many; and though many, he returns to oneness. ॥28॥
4.42.29: A single seed, having gone forth outwardly as a plant, again becomes seed; so too, in multiplicity, Maheśvara, having the form of Śiva, is himself everything. ॥29॥
4.42.30: This is the supreme knowledge of Śiva, declared as it truly is. Only one who possesses knowledge knows it, no one else, O lords of seers. ॥30॥
4.42.31: The sages said: Tell us that knowledge together with its characteristics, knowing which one attains Śiva-hood. How is Śiva all that, or how is everything Śiva alone? ॥31॥
4.42.32: Vyāsa said: Having heard these words, Sūta, the foremost of Purāṇa narrators, remembering the lotus feet of Śiva, spoke these words to those sages. ॥32॥
4.42.iti: Thus ends the forty-second adhyāya, named The description of the distinction between the saguṇa and the nirguṇa, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥42॥
4.43.1: Sūta said: Listen, all you sages: I shall relate the knowledge of Śiva just as I heard it, a great secret whose very nature is supreme liberation. ॥1॥
4.43.2: In the assembly of Brahmā (Ka), Nārada, the Kumāras, Vyāsa and Kapila, it was determined and declared by them. ॥2॥
4.43.3: This knowledge should always be understood: the entire world is made of Śiva. Śiva should be known as constituting everything by the wise one who knows all. ॥3॥
4.43.4: Whatever world is seen, from Brahmā down to a blade of grass, all that is Śiva alone; that god is called Śiva. ॥4॥
4.43.5: When the desire arises in him, then this world is made. He alone knows everything; no one knows him. ॥5॥
4.43.6: Having himself created it and entered it, he remains far off; he has not truly entered there, being untainted and of the nature of consciousness. ॥6॥
4.43.7: Just as a luminary is reflected in water and the like, yet in reality does not enter it, so too is Śiva himself. ॥7॥
4.43.8: In reality he himself is everything; the graded sequence merely appears fair. Difference of view is ignorance; there is nothing else, and again no duality. ॥8॥
4.43.9: In all the philosophical systems a difference of views is set forth; but the Vedāntins always proclaim non-duality. ॥9॥
4.43.10: The individual soul, a portion of his own portion, deluded by nescience and helpless, thinks, I am another; freed from that nescience, it becomes Śiva. ॥10॥
4.43.11: Pervading all, Śiva is directly the pervader in all creatures; Śaṅkara himself, lord of the sentient and insentient, is everywhere. ॥11॥
4.43.12: The discerning one who undertakes a means for seeing him, resorting to the path of Vedānta, obtains the fruit of that vision. ॥12॥
4.43.13: Just as fire is pervasive and abides in every piece of wood, he who churns that wood surely sees it without doubt. ॥13॥
4.43.14: The discerning one who here practises the means beginning with devotion surely sees that Śiva; there is no doubt of this. ॥14॥
4.43.15: Śiva, Śiva, and Śiva alone; there is nothing else whatsoever. Through delusion Śaṅkara always appears as having manifold forms. ॥15॥
4.43.16: Just as the ocean, clay, or again gold acquires multiplicity through limiting adjuncts, so does Śaṅkara. ॥16॥
4.43.17: The difference between effect and cause does not really exist; it is only through deluded understanding, and when that is absent, it perishes. ॥17॥
4.43.18: When a sprout from a seed displays multiplicity, in the end there is only the seed, and that sprout perishes. ॥18॥
4.43.19: The knower is the seed itself; the sprout is considered the modification. When that ceases, he is again the knower; there need be no deliberation about this. ॥19॥
4.43.20: All is Śiva, Śiva is all; there is no difference whatsoever. How then does one see variety, and how again unity? ॥20॥
4.43.21: Just as the single light called the sun is seen by people in manifold ways, especially in water and the like, so too is he. ॥21॥
4.43.22: Just as space, though pervading everywhere, is not bound by contact, so the all-pervading god is never bound anywhere. ॥22॥
4.43.23: The individual soul is thus with ego; freed from that, it is Śaṅkara himself. The soul is petty, an experiencer of karma; Śaṅkara is great and untainted. ॥23॥
4.43.24: Just as a single metal such as gold, mixed with silver and the like, becomes of little value, so too is the soul joined with ego. ॥24॥
4.43.25: Just as gold and the like, purified by alkali and such, becomes fine and regains its former value, so too the soul through purification. ॥25॥
4.43.26: First, having found a true guru, endowed with the sentiment of devotion, one fervently performs worship, remembrance and the like, regarding him as Śiva. ॥26॥
4.43.27: Through that understanding, the impurity consisting of all sins and the like departs from the body; then ignorance perishes, when one becomes possessed of knowledge. ॥27॥
4.43.28: Then the soul, freed from ego and of pure intellect, attains Śaṅkara-hood again by the grace of Śaṅkara. ॥28॥
4.43.29: Just as one's own form is seen in a mirror, so he sees Śambhu present everywhere; this is well ascertained. ॥29॥
4.43.30: He alone is liberated while living; when the body has decayed, he merges in Śiva. The body is under the sway of prārabdha karma; the knower is considered distinct from it. ॥30॥
4.43.31: Obtaining good, he should not rejoice; obtaining evil, he should not be angry. He who has equanimity amid the pairs of opposites is called a knower. ॥31॥
4.43.32: By yoga of the self or by discrimination of the principles (tattvas), one desiring liberation should act so that he departs from the body, never to return to a body. ॥32॥
4.43.33: The liberated one would dissolve into Sadāśiva and attain separation from the body. Spiritual inquiry is the root of knowledge, and of that the root is devotion to Śiva. ॥33॥
4.43.34: Of devotion, love is declared the root; of love, likewise, hearing the sacred lore; of hearing, the company of the good; and from the company of the good comes a wise guru. ॥34॥
4.43.35: And when knowledge is thus perfected, one certainly becomes liberated. If this is so, whoever is a knower should always worship Śambhu alone. ॥35॥
4.43.36: Endowed with undivided devotion, he should worship Śambhu again and again; at the end he attains liberation. There need be no deliberation about this. ॥36॥
4.43.37: Therefore, for attaining liberation there is no god greater than Śaṅkara, by taking refuge in whom one turns back from saṃsāra. ॥37॥
4.43.38: Thus, O brahmins, I have told you this manifold teaching, determined by the assembled sages; it should be held in mind with effort. ॥38॥
4.43.39: First it was given by Śambhu to Viṣṇu before the liṅga; by Viṣṇu it was given to Brahmā, and by Brahmā to Sanaka and the others. ॥39॥
4.43.40: Then that knowledge was told by Sanaka and the others to Nārada; it was told by Nārada to Vyāsa, and by him, the compassionate one, to me. ॥40॥
4.43.41: It was imparted by me to you, and by you, for the good of the world, it should be carefully established, for it brings the attainment of Śiva. ॥41॥
4.43.42: Thus I have explained to you what I was asked, O lords among sages. It should be carefully guarded. What else do you wish to hear? ॥42॥
4.43.43: Vyāsa said: Having heard this, the sages attained supreme bliss; bowing, they praised him again and again with voices choked with joy. ॥43॥
4.43.44: The sages said: O disciple of Vyāsa, salutation to you. You are blessed, O best of Śaivas. You have made us hear the supreme reality, the unsurpassed Śaiva knowledge. ॥44॥
4.43.45: By your grace the confusion of our minds is indeed gone. We are content, having received from you the true knowledge of Śiva that grants liberation. ॥45॥
4.43.46: Sūta said: It should not be told to an unbeliever, to one without faith, or to a deceitful person, nor to one not devoted to Maheśa, nor to one unwilling to listen, O brāhmaṇas. ॥46॥
4.43.47: Having repeatedly examined the Itihāsas and Purāṇas, the Vedas and the śāstras, and having extracted their essence, Vyāsa told it to me. ॥47॥
4.43.48: By hearing this even once, sin is reduced to ashes. The non-devotee gains devotion, and the devotee's devotion increases. ॥48॥
4.43.49: When heard again, true devotion arises; and by hearing it yet again, liberation would come. Therefore it should be heard again and again by those who seek the fruits of enjoyment and liberation. ॥49॥
4.43.50: Five recitations should be done with the supreme fruit in view; one obtains it, there is no doubt—this is the word of Vyāsa. ॥50॥
4.43.51: Nothing is hard to attain for one by whom this excellent knowledge has been heard; by hearing it five times, the vision of Śiva is obtained. ॥51॥
4.43.52: Ancient kings, brāhmaṇas and excellent vaiśyas, having heard this five times with attentive mind, attained the supreme accomplishment. ॥52॥
4.43.53: Even today, whatever man, intent on devotion, hears this knowledge called Śaiva will obtain both enjoyment and liberation. ॥53॥
4.43.54: Vyāsa said: Having heard these words of his, they attained supreme bliss and reverently worshipped Sūta with various offerings. ॥54॥
4.43.55: With salutations and hymns, preceded by the recitation of auspicious blessings, they honoured him with benedictions, content, their doubts dispelled. ॥55॥
4.43.56: Sūta and those wise sages, mutually content, regarding Śambhu as the supreme god, bowed to and worshipped him. ॥56॥
4.43.57: This excellent knowledge of Śiva is great and very dear to Śiva; it is divine, grants enjoyment and liberation, and increases devotion to Śiva. ॥57॥
4.43.58: This sacred and supreme saṃhitā named Koṭirudra, the fourth of the Śiva Purāṇa, bringing joy, has been narrated by me. ॥58॥
4.43.59: Whoever, with concentrated mind, hears this with devotion or causes it to be heard, having enjoyed all pleasures here, attains the supreme state in the end. ॥59॥
4.43.iti: Thus ends the forty-third adhyāya, named The exposition of knowledge, in the fourth saṃhitā, the Koṭirudra-saṃhitā, of the Śrī Śivamahāpurāṇa. ॥43॥
